sentences.zh: 李穀，字惟珍，潁州汝陰人。

translations.literal: Li Gu, style name Weizhen, was a man of Ruyin in Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gu, whose style name was Weizhen, came from Ruyin in Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 身長八尺，容貌魁偉。

translations.literal: His body was eight chi in height; his appearance was grand and imposing.
translations.idiomatic: He stood eight chi tall, with a grand and imposing bearing.

sentences.zh: 少勇力善射，以任俠為事，頗為鄉人所困，發憤從學，所覽如宿習。

translations.literal: In youth he was brave and strong and skilled at archery; he took chivalrous deeds as his occupation and was much troubled by fellow villagers; in anger he turned to study, and whatever he read was as if long practiced.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was strong and skilled at archery and lived by chivalrous deeds, which brought him much trouble from his neighbors. In anger he turned to study, and everything he read seemed already familiar to him.

sentences.zh: 年二十七，舉進士，連辟華、泰二州從事。

translations.literal: At age twenty-seven he passed the jinshi examination and was repeatedly summoned as adjutant in Hua and Tai prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-seven he passed the jinshi examination and was repeatedly invited to serve as adjutant in Hua and Tai prefectures.

sentences.zh: 開運二年秋，出為磁州刺史、北面水陸轉運使。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the second year of Kaiyun he went out as prefect of Ci Prefecture and commissioner for north-route water and land transport.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the second year of Kaiyun he was appointed prefect of Ci Prefecture and commissioner for north-route water and land transport.

sentences.zh: 契丹入汴，少帝蒙塵而北，舊臣無敢候謁者，穀獨拜迎於路，君臣相對泣下。

translations.literal: The Khitan entered Bian; the young emperor was borne away north in disgrace; none of the former ministers dared to wait upon him—Gu alone bowed to welcome him on the road, and ruler and minister wept facing each other.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan entered Bian, the young emperor was carried north in disgrace. None of the former ministers dared to attend him, but Gu alone bowed to welcome him on the road, and ruler and minister wept as they faced each other.

sentences.zh: 穀曰：“臣無狀，負陛下。

translations.literal: Gu said: "Your servant is unworthy and has failed Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Gu said, "Your servant is unworthy and has failed Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: ”因傾囊以獻。

translations.literal: Thereupon he emptied his purse and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: He then emptied his purse and offered it to him.

sentences.zh: 會契丹主發使至州，穀禽斬之，密送款於漢祖，潛遣河朔酋豪梁暉入據安陽，契丹主患之，即議北旋。

translations.literal: When the Khitan ruler sent envoys to the prefecture, Gu seized and executed them, secretly sent allegiance to the Han founder, and covertly dispatched the Hebei chieftain Liang Hui to seize Anyang; the Khitan ruler was troubled and at once deliberated turning north.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan ruler sent envoys to the prefecture, Gu seized and executed them, secretly pledged allegiance to the founder of Han, and covertly sent the Hebei chieftain Liang Hui to occupy Anyang. Troubled by this, the Khitan ruler at once considered withdrawing north.

sentences.zh: 會有告契丹以城中虛弱者，契丹還攻安陽，陷其城，穀自郡候契丹，遂見獲。

translations.literal: Someone reported to the Khitan that the city was weak; the Khitan returned to attack Anyang and took the city; Gu went from his prefecture to wait upon the Khitan and was then captured.
translations.idiomatic: Someone informed the Khitan that the city was weak. They returned to attack Anyang, took the city, and when Gu went from his prefecture to wait upon the Khitan, he was captured.

sentences.zh: 契丹主先設刑具，謂之曰：“爾何背我歸太原？

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler first set up instruments of torture and said to him: "Why did you betray me and return to Taiyuan?"
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler first set out instruments of torture and said to him, "Why did you betray me and go over to Taiyuan?"

sentences.zh: ”穀曰：“無之。

translations.literal: Gu said: "There was no such thing."
translations.idiomatic: Gu said, "There was no such thing."

sentences.zh: ”契丹主因引手車中，似取所獲文字，而穀知其詐，因請曰：“如實有此事，乞顯示之。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler then reached into the cart as if to take out captured documents, but Gu knew it was a trick and therefore requested: "If this truly happened, I beg you to display it."
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler reached into the cart as if to take out captured documents, but Gu knew it was a ruse and said, "If this truly happened, I beg you to show me."

sentences.zh: ”契丹國制，人未伏者不即置死。

translations.literal: By Khitan state law, one who had not submitted was not immediately put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Under Khitan law, a man who had not yet submitted was not immediately put to death.

sentences.zh: 自後凡詰穀者六次，穀詞不屈。

translations.literal: Afterward, whenever Gu was interrogated—six times in all—his words did not yield.
translations.idiomatic: After that he was interrogated six times in all, and each time Gu's answers did not waver.

sentences.zh: 契丹主病，且曰：“我南行時，人云爾謂我必不得北還，爾何術知之？

translations.literal: When the Khitan ruler fell ill, he said: "When I marched south, people said you declared I would certainly not return north. By what art did you know this?"
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan ruler fell ill, he said, "When I marched south, people said you declared I would never return north. What art told you that?"

sentences.zh: 今我疾甚，如能救我，則致爾富貴。

translations.literal: Now my illness is grave; if you can cure me, I will bring you wealth and honor.
translations.idiomatic: Now my illness is grave. If you can cure me, I will make you rich and honored.

sentences.zh: ”穀曰：“實無術，蓋為人所陷耳。

translations.literal: Gu said: "I truly have no art; I was surely framed by others."
translations.idiomatic: Gu said, "I truly have no art for that. I was simply framed by others."

sentences.zh: ”穀氣色不撓，卒寬之。

translations.literal: Gu's demeanor did not falter, and in the end he was leniently treated.
translations.idiomatic: Gu's bearing did not falter, and in the end he was spared.

sentences.zh: 俄而德光道殂，永康繼立，署穀給事中。

translations.literal: Before long Deguang died on the road; Yongkang succeeded to the throne and appointed Gu Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Deguang died on the road. Yongkang succeeded him and appointed Gu Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 時契丹將麻答守真定，而李崧、和凝與家屬皆在城中。

translations.literal: At that time the Khitan general Maduo held Zhending, and Li Song, He Ning, and their families were all in the city.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Khitan general Maduo held Zhending, and Li Song, He Ning, and their families were all inside the city.

sentences.zh: 會李筠、何福進率兵逐麻答，推護聖指揮使白再榮權知留後。

translations.literal: When Li Yun and He Fujin led troops to drive out Maduo, they installed Guardian of the Sacred Commander Bai Zairong as acting military governor.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Yun and He Fujin led troops to drive Maduo out, they installed Bai Zairong, Guardian of the Sacred Commander, as acting military governor.

sentences.zh: 再榮利崧等家財，令甲士圍其居以求賂，既得之，復欲殺崧等滅口。

translations.literal: Zairong coveted the families' wealth and ordered armed men to surround their residences demanding bribes; once he had obtained them, he wished again to kill Song and the others to silence them.
translations.idiomatic: Zairong coveted the wealth of Song and the others and sent armed men to surround their homes demanding bribes. Once he had the money, he wanted to kill Song and the others to silence them.

sentences.zh: 穀遽見再榮謂之曰：“今國亡主辱，公輩握勁兵，不能死節，雖逐一契丹將，城中戰死者數千人，非獨公之力也。

translations.literal: Gu hurried to see Zairong and said: "Now the state is perished and the lord humiliated; you men hold strong troops yet could not die for principle. Though you drove out one Khitan general, several thousand died fighting in the city—not by your strength alone."
translations.idiomatic: Gu hurried to see Zairong and said, "The state is destroyed and the sovereign humiliated, yet you hold strong troops and could not die for your principles. Though you drove out one Khitan general, several thousand men died fighting in the city—not by your strength alone."

sentences.zh: 一朝殺宰相，即日中原有主，責公以專殺，其將何辭以對？

translations.literal: If in a morning you kill a chief minister, that very day the Central Plains will have a lord who will charge you with unauthorized killing—what words will you have to answer?
translations.idiomatic: Kill a chief minister in the morning, and that very day the Central Plains will have a ruler who will charge you with murder on your own authority. What answer will you give then?

sentences.zh: ”再榮甚懼，崧等獲免。

translations.literal: Zairong was greatly afraid, and Song and the others were spared.
translations.idiomatic: Zairong was greatly frightened, and Song and the others were spared.

sentences.zh: 漢初，入拜左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Han he entered court and was appointed Left Regular Cavalryman Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Han dynasty he entered court and was appointed Left Regular Cavalryman Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 舊制，罷外郡歸本官，至是進秩，獎之也。

translations.literal: By the old regulation, when one left an outer prefecture one returned to one's original office; now he was promoted in rank, a reward.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old rule, leaving an outer prefecture meant returning to one's original office; now he was promoted in rank as a reward.

sentences.zh: 俄權判開封府。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed acting administrator of Kaifeng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made acting administrator of Kaifeng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時京畿多盜，中牟尤甚，穀誘邑人發其巢穴。

translations.literal: At the time there were many bandits in the capital region, Zhongmou especially; Gu induced local men to expose their dens.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits were numerous in the capital region, especially around Zhongmou. Gu induced local men to expose their hideouts.

sentences.zh: 有劉德輿者，梁時屢攝畿佐，居中牟，素有幹材，穀即署攝本邑主簿。

translations.literal: There was one Liu Deyu who during Liang had repeatedly served as capital-region deputy and resided in Zhongmou, possessed of ability; Gu immediately appointed him acting chief clerk of that county.
translations.idiomatic: There was a man named Liu Deyu who during the Liang had repeatedly served in the capital region and lived in Zhongmou, a man of proven ability. Gu immediately appointed him acting chief clerk of the county.

sentences.zh: 浹旬，穀請侍衛兵數千佐德輿，悉禽賊黨，其魁一即縣佐史，一御史臺吏。

translations.literal: Within ten days Gu requested several thousand palace guards to assist Deyu; they captured the whole bandit gang, whose leaders were one county assistant clerk and one censorate clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days Gu requested several thousand palace guards to assist Deyu. They captured the entire band, whose leaders were a county assistant clerk and a censorate clerk.

sentences.zh: 搜其家，得金玉財貨甚眾，自是行者無患。

translations.literal: Searching their homes they found much gold, jade, and property; from then on travelers were untroubled.
translations.idiomatic: Searching their homes turned up great quantities of gold, jade, and goods. From then on travelers went unharmed.

sentences.zh: 俄遷工部侍郎。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 周祖西征，為西南面行營水陸轉運使。

translations.literal: When the Zhou founder campaigned west, Gu served as commissioner for water and land transport of the southwest campaign army.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou founder campaigned west, Gu served as commissioner for water and land transport of the southwestern campaign army.

sentences.zh: 關右平，改陳州刺史。

translations.literal: When the area west of the passes was pacified, he was changed to prefect of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: When the region west of the passes was pacified, he was made prefect of Chen.

sentences.zh: 會有內難，急召赴闕。

translations.literal: When internal troubles arose, he was urgently summoned to court.
translations.idiomatic: When internal troubles broke out, he was urgently summoned to court.

sentences.zh: 周祖兵入汴，命權判三司。

translations.literal: When the Zhou founder's army entered Bian, he was ordered to act as administrator of the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou founder's army entered Bian, he was ordered to serve as acting administrator of the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 廣順初，加戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun he was added Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Guangshun he was made Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 未幾，拜中書侍郎、平章事，仍判三司。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat, Grand Councilor, and still administered the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor, while continuing to administer the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 初，漢乾祐中，周祖討河中，穀掌轉運，時周祖已有人望，屬漢政紊亂，潛貯異志，屢以諷穀，穀但對以人臣當盡節奉上而已。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the Qianyou era of Han when the Zhou founder attacked Hezhong, Gu managed transport; at that time the Zhou founder already enjoyed popular regard, and as Han government was chaotic he secretly harbored a different aim and often hinted at it to Gu, but Gu only replied that a minister should exhaust his loyalty in serving the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during the Qianyou era of Han, when the Zhou founder attacked Hezhong, Gu managed transport. The Zhou founder already enjoyed great popular regard, and with Han government in chaos he secretly harbored other ambitions and often hinted at them to Gu. Gu would only reply that a minister ought to exhaust his loyalty in serving the throne.

sentences.zh: 故開國之初，倚以為相。

translations.literal: Therefore at the founding of the state he was relied upon as chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason, at the founding of the dynasty he was relied upon as chief minister.

sentences.zh: 是歲，淮陽吏民數千詣闕請立生祠，許之，穀懇讓得止。

translations.literal: That year several thousand officials and people of Huaiyang came to court requesting a living shrine; permission was granted, but Gu earnestly declined and it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: That year several thousand officials and commoners from Huaiyang came to court asking that a living shrine be erected in his honor. Permission was granted, but Gu earnestly declined and the plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 先是，禁牛革法甚峻，犯者抵死。

translations.literal: Previously the law forbidding cattle hide was very severe; violators were punished by death.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the law against cattle hide had been very strict, and violators were punished with death.

sentences.zh: 穀乃校每歲用革之數，凡田十頃歲出一革，餘聽民私用。

translations.literal: Gu then calculated the annual use of hide: for every ten qing of fields one hide per year, the rest permitted for private use by the people.
translations.idiomatic: Gu then calculated the annual quota of hide: one hide per year for every ten qing of farmland, with the remainder left for private use by the people.

sentences.zh: 又奏罷屯田務，以民隸州縣課役，盡除宿弊。

translations.literal: He also memorialized to abolish the military colony offices, assigning the people to prefecture and county tax duties, fully removing long-standing abuses.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized to abolish the military colony offices and assign the people to prefectural and county tax duties, thereby removing long-standing abuses.

sentences.zh: 穀父祖本居河南洛陽，經巢之亂，園廬蕩盡，穀生於外。

translations.literal: Gu's father and grandfather had originally lived in Luoyang, Henan; through the Huang Chao turmoil their gardens and houses were utterly swept away, and Gu was born abroad.
translations.idiomatic: Gu's father and grandfather had originally lived in Luoyang in Henan. During the Huang Chao rebellion their gardens and houses were utterly destroyed, and Gu was born away from home.

sentences.zh: 既貴，訪得舊地，建蘭若，又立垣屋，凡族人之不可仕者分田居之。

translations.literal: Once he rose high he sought out the old site, built a Buddhist temple, and also erected walls and houses; all kinsmen unable to take office he allotted fields and dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: Once he had risen high in rank he found the old site, built a Buddhist temple, and erected walls and houses, allotting fields and dwellings to kinsmen who could not take office.

sentences.zh: 詔改清風鄉高陽里為賢相鄉勳德里。

translations.literal: An edict changed Qingfeng Township's Gaoyang Lane to Township of the Worthy Minister, Lane of Meritorious Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: An edict renamed Qingfeng Township's Gaoyang Lane to Worthy Minister Township, Lane of Meritorious Virtue.

sentences.zh: 二年，晨起仆階下，傷右臂，在告，旬中三上表辭相位，周祖不允，免朝參，視事本司，賜白藤肩輿，召至便殿勉諭。

translations.literal: In the second year, rising in the morning he fell on the steps and injured his right arm; on leave, within ten days he thrice submitted memorials declining the chief ministry; the Zhou founder did not consent, exempted him from court attendance, let him handle affairs in his own office, granted a white rattan sedan chair, and summoned him to the side hall to encourage him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he fell on the steps one morning and injured his right arm. While on leave he submitted three memorials within ten days asking to resign the chief ministry. The Zhou founder refused, exempted him from court attendance, let him conduct business in his own office, granted him a white rattan sedan chair, and summoned him to the side hall to encourage him.

sentences.zh: 穀不得已，起視事。

translations.literal: Gu had no choice but to rise and attend to business.
translations.idiomatic: Gu had no choice but to rise and resume his duties.

sentences.zh: 征兗州，為東京留守、判開封府事。

translations.literal: When Yanzhou was attacked, he became eastern capital regent and administrator of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: When the campaign against Yanzhou was launched, he was made regent of the eastern capital and administrator of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 顯德初，加右僕射、集賢殿大學士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiande he was made Right Vice Director and Grand Academician of the Hall for Assembling the Worthy.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xiande he was made Right Vice Director and Grand Academician of the Hall for Assembling the Worthy.

sentences.zh: 從世宗征太原，遇賊於高平，匿山谷中，信宿而出，追及乘輿，世宗慰撫之。

translations.literal: Accompanying Shizong on campaign against Taiyuan, they encountered the enemy at Gaoping; he hid in a mountain valley, emerged after two nights, caught up with the imperial carriage, and Shizong comforted him.
translations.idiomatic: Accompanying Shizong on the campaign against Taiyuan, he encountered the enemy at Gaoping, hid in a mountain valley, and emerged after two nights. He caught up with the imperial carriage, and Shizong comforted him.

sentences.zh: 世宗將趨太原，命穀先調兵食，又代符彥卿判太原行府事。

translations.literal: As Shizong was about to hurry to Taiyuan, he ordered Gu first to provision troops and also to replace Fu Yanqing as administrator of the Taiyuan campaign headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: As Shizong was about to press on to Taiyuan, he ordered Gu first to provision the troops and also to replace Fu Yanqing as administrator of the Taiyuan campaign headquarters.

sentences.zh: 師還，進位司空、門下侍郎，監修國史。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was advanced to Grand Marshal, Vice Director of the Chancellery, and supervised compilation of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, he was promoted to Grand Marshal and Vice Director of the Chancellery and was put in charge of compiling the national history.

sentences.zh: 穀以史氏所述本於起居注，喪亂以來遂廢其職，上言請令端明、樞密直學士編記言動，為內廷日曆，以付史官。

translations.literal: Gu observed that the historians' accounts derive from the diary of attendance and conduct, which since the chaos of collapse had been abandoned; he memorialized asking that Hanlin academicians compile records of words and deeds as an inner-court calendar to hand to the historians.
translations.idiomatic: Gu observed that historical writing depends on the diary of attendance and conduct, a duty abandoned since the chaos of war. He memorialized asking that Hanlin academicians compile a record of words and deeds as an inner-court calendar to be handed to the historians.

sentences.zh: 是歲，河大決齊、鄆，發十數州丁壯塞之，命穀領護，刻期就功。

translations.literal: That year the Yellow River burst its banks greatly in Qi and Yun; corvée was levied from more than ten prefectures to block it, and Gu was ordered to supervise, with a set date for completion.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Yellow River burst its banks in Qi and Yun. Corvée labor was levied from more than ten prefectures to block the breach, and Gu was ordered to supervise the work, with a fixed deadline for completion.

sentences.zh: 二年冬，議伐南唐，以穀為淮南道行營前軍都部署，兼知廬、壽等州行府事，忠武軍節度王彥副之，韓令坤以下十二將率從。

translations.literal: In the winter of the second year they deliberated attacking Southern Tang; Gu was made overall commander of the advance army of the Huainan circuit campaign headquarters, concurrently administering the campaign offices of Lu, Shou, and other prefectures; Wang Yan of Zhongwu military commission was his deputy, and twelve generals including Han Lingkun followed.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the second year they deliberated attacking Southern Tang. Gu was made overall commander of the advance army of the Huainan campaign headquarters and concurrently put in charge of the campaign offices of Lu, Shou, and other prefectures. Wang Yan, military commissioner of Zhongwu, served as his deputy, and twelve generals including Han Lingkun followed him.

sentences.zh: 穀領兵自正陽渡淮，先鋒都將白延遇敗吳軍數千於來遠，又破千餘人於山口鎮，進攻上窯，又敗千餘眾，獲其小校數十人，長圍壽春。

translations.literal: Gu led troops across the Huai from Zhengyang; advance commander Bai Yanyu defeated several thousand Wu troops at Laiyuan, broke over a thousand more at Shankou town, attacked Shangyao and again defeated over a thousand, capturing several dozen of their junior officers, and laid long siege to Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Gu led his troops across the Huai from Zhengyang. His advance commander Bai Yanyu defeated several thousand Wu troops at Laiyuan, broke another thousand at Shankou, attacked Shangyao and defeated over a thousand more, captured several dozen junior Wu officers, and laid a long siege to Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 南唐遣大將劉彥貞來援，穀召將佐謀曰：“今援軍已過來遠，距壽陽二百里，舟棹將及正陽。

translations.literal: Southern Tang sent the great general Liu Yanzhen to relieve; Gu summoned officers to counsel: "Now the relief army has passed Laiyuan, two hundred li from Shouyang; boats will soon reach Zhengyang."
translations.idiomatic: Southern Tang sent the great general Liu Yanzhen to relieve the siege. Gu summoned his officers and said, "The relief army has already passed Laiyuan and is two hundred li from Shouyang. Their boats will soon reach Zhengyang."

sentences.zh: 我師無水戰之備，萬一斷橋梁，隔絕王師，則腹背受敵矣。

translations.literal: Our army has no preparation for naval battle; if they should cut the bridges and separate the imperial army, we would be attacked front and rear.
translations.idiomatic: Our army is not prepared for naval combat. If they cut the bridges and cut off the imperial army, we will be attacked from front and rear.

sentences.zh: 不如退守浮梁，以待戎輅之至。

translations.literal: It would be better to withdraw and hold Fuliang, and await the arrival of the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: It would be better to withdraw and hold Fuliang until the imperial carriage arrives.

sentences.zh: ”初，世宗至圉鎮，已聞此謀，亟走內侍乘驛止之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Shizong reached Yuzhen he had already heard of this plan and urgently sent a palace attendant by post to stop it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Shizong reached Yuzhen, he had already heard of this plan and urgently sent a palace attendant by post relay to stop it.

sentences.zh: 穀已退保正陽，仍焚芻糧，回軍之際，遞相掠奪，淮北役夫數百悉陷於壽春。

translations.literal: Gu had already withdrawn to Zhengyang and still burned fodder and grain; on the retreat the troops plundered one another, and several hundred laborers north of the Huai were all lost in Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Gu had already withdrawn to Zhengyang and even burned fodder and grain. On the retreat the troops plundered one another, and several hundred laborers north of the Huai were all lost at Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 世宗聞之怒，亟命李重進率師伐之，以穀判壽州行府。

translations.literal: Shizong heard this with anger and urgently ordered Li Chongjin to lead troops to attack, appointing Gu administrator of the Shouzhou campaign office.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong was furious when he heard this and urgently ordered Li Chongjin to lead troops against the enemy, appointing Gu administrator of the Shouzhou campaign office.

sentences.zh: 是秋，詔歸闕，得風痹疾，告滿百日，累表請致仕，優詔不允。

translations.literal: That autumn an edict recalled him to court; he contracted wind paralysis, took leave for a full hundred days, repeatedly memorialized to retire, but gracious edicts refused.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn an edict recalled him to court. He contracted wind paralysis, took leave for a full hundred days, and repeatedly memorialized to retire, but gracious edicts refused his request.

sentences.zh: 每軍國大事，令中使就第問之。

translations.literal: For every great affair of state, palace envoys were sent to his residence to consult him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a major affair of state arose, palace envoys were sent to his residence to consult him.

sentences.zh: 四年春，吳人壁紫金山，築甬道以援壽春，不及者數里。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year the Wu men fortified Purple Gold Mountain and built a raised passage to relieve Shouchun, falling short by several li.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fourth year the Wu fortified Purple Gold Mountain and built a raised passage to relieve Shouchun, but it fell short by several li.

sentences.zh: 師老無功，時請罷兵為便，世宗令范質、王溥就穀謀之。

translations.literal: The army grew weary without success; at the time many urged withdrawing troops as expedient; Shizong sent Fan Zhi and Wang Pu to consult Gu.
translations.idiomatic: The army grew weary without success, and many at the time urged withdrawing the troops as the expedient course. Shizong sent Fan Zhi and Wang Pu to consult Gu.

sentences.zh: 穀手疏請親征，有必勝之利者三，世宗大悅，用其策。

translations.literal: Gu personally memorialized requesting the emperor campaign in person, citing three advantages of certain victory; Shizong was greatly pleased and adopted his plan.
translations.idiomatic: Gu personally memorialized asking the emperor to campaign in person, citing three advantages that guaranteed victory. Shizong was greatly pleased and adopted his plan.

sentences.zh: 及淮南平，賞賜甚厚。

translations.literal: When Huainan was pacified, rewards were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: When Huainan was pacified, his rewards were very generous.

sentences.zh: 出穀疏，令翰林學士承旨陶穀為讚以賜之。

translations.literal: Gu's memorial was published and Hanlin Academician Receiver Tao Gu was ordered to compose a eulogy to bestow on him.
translations.idiomatic: Gu's memorial was published, and Hanlin Academician Receiver Tao Gu was ordered to compose a eulogy to bestow on him.

sentences.zh: 是夏，世宗還，穀扶疾見便殿，詔令不拜，命坐御坐側。

translations.literal: That summer when Shizong returned, Gu, supporting his illness, was received in the side hall; an edict ordered him not to bow and commanded him seated beside the imperial seat.
translations.idiomatic: That summer, when Shizong returned, Gu was received in the side hall despite his illness. An edict ordered him not to bow and commanded him to sit beside the imperial seat.

sentences.zh: 以抱疾既久，請辭相位。

translations.literal: Because his illness had long endured, he requested to resign the chief ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Because his illness had long endured, he asked to resign the chief ministry.

sentences.zh: 世宗怡然勉之，謂曰：“譬如家有四子，一人有疾，棄而不養，非父之道也。

translations.literal: Shizong cheerfully encouraged him, saying: "It is like a household with four sons—if one is ill and cast aside without care, that is not a father's way."
translations.idiomatic: Shizong cheerfully encouraged him, saying, "It is like a household with four sons. If one falls ill and is cast aside without care, that is not how a father should act."

sentences.zh: 朕君臨萬方，卿處輔相之位，君臣之間，分義斯在，奈何以祿奉為言。

translations.literal: I rule the myriad realms; you occupy the post of chief minister—between ruler and minister this division of duty stands; how can you speak only of salary and rank?
translations.idiomatic: I rule the myriad realms, and you occupy the post of chief minister. The bond between ruler and minister lies in duty, not in salary and rank alone.

sentences.zh: ”穀愧謝而退。

translations.literal: Gu withdrew in shame and thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Gu withdrew in shame and gratitude.

sentences.zh: 俄以平壽州，敘功加爵邑。

translations.literal: Soon, for pacifying Shouzhou, his merit was reckoned and noble fief added.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, for pacifying Shouzhou, his merit was reckoned and his noble fief was increased.

sentences.zh: 是秋，穀抗表乞骸骨，罷相，守司空，加邑封，令每月肩輿一詣便殿，訪以政事。

translations.literal: That autumn Gu firmly memorialized begging his bones; he was dismissed from the chief ministry, retained as Grand Marshal, fief increased, and ordered monthly by sedan chair to come once to the side hall to be consulted on government.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Gu firmly memorialized asking to retire. He was dismissed from the chief ministry but retained as Grand Marshal with an increased fief, and was ordered once a month to come by sedan chair to the side hall to be consulted on government affairs.

sentences.zh: 五年夏，世宗平淮南回，賜穀錢百萬、米麥五百斛、芻粟薪炭等。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fifth year when Shizong returned from pacifying Huainan, he bestowed on Gu a million cash, five hundred hu of grain, fodder, fuel, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the fifth year, when Shizong returned from pacifying Huainan, he bestowed on Gu a million cash, five hundred hu of grain, and fodder, fuel, and other supplies.

sentences.zh: 恭帝即位，加開府儀同三司，進封趙國公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gong succeeded, he was made Provisionally Honored with the Three Dignities and advanced to Duke of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gong succeeded to the throne, Gu was made Provisionally Honored with the Three Dignities and advanced to Duke of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 求歸洛邑，賜錢三十萬，從其請。

translations.literal: He requested return to Luoyang; three hundred thousand cash was granted and his request allowed.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to return to Luoyang. Three hundred thousand cash was granted him, and his request was granted.

sentences.zh: 太祖即位，遣使就賜器幣。

translations.literal: When Taizu took the throne, envoys were sent to his residence to bestow vessels and silks.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu took the throne, envoys were sent to his home to bestow vessels and silks.

sentences.zh: 建隆元年，卒，年五十八。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianlong he died, aged fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianlong he died at the age of fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 太祖聞之震悼，贈侍中。

translations.literal: Taizu upon hearing was deeply shaken and grieved, posthumously appointing him Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu heard the news he was deeply shaken and grieved and posthumously appointed him Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 穀為人厚重剛毅，深沉有城府，雅善談論，議政事能近取譬，言多詣理，辭氣明暢，人主為之聳聽。

translations.literal: Gu as a man was weighty, firm, and resolute, deep and calculating, elegantly skilled in discourse; discussing government he could draw comparisons from nearby matters, his words mostly attaining reason, his tone clear and flowing, and rulers would listen upright.
translations.idiomatic: Gu was a man of weight, firmness, and resolution, deep and calculating. He was elegantly skilled in discourse; when discussing government he could draw apt comparisons from nearby matters, his words mostly reached the heart of the matter, and his tone was clear and flowing, so that rulers listened with rapt attention.

sentences.zh: 人有難必救，有恩必報。

translations.literal: If anyone faced hardship he surely rescued them; if anyone showed favor he surely repaid it.
translations.idiomatic: If anyone was in hardship he surely rescued them; if anyone showed him favor he surely repaid it.

sentences.zh: 好汲引寒士，多至顯位。

translations.literal: He loved to lift up poor scholars, many of whom reached prominent rank.
translations.idiomatic: He loved to lift up poor scholars, many of whom rose to prominent rank.

sentences.zh: 與韓熙載善，熙載將南渡，密告穀曰：“若江東相我，我當長驅以定中原。

translations.literal: He was on good terms with Han Xizai; when Xizai was about to cross south, he secretly told Gu: "If the lands east of the river make me chancellor, I shall drive far north to pacify the Central Plains."
translations.idiomatic: He was on good terms with Han Xizai. When Xizai was about to cross south, he secretly told Gu, "If the lands east of the river make me chancellor, I shall drive far north and pacify the Central Plains."

sentences.zh: ”穀笑曰：“若中原相我，下江南探囊中物耳。

translations.literal: Gu laughed and said: "If the Central Plains make me chancellor, taking Jiangnan will be like reaching into a bag for what's inside."
translations.idiomatic: Gu laughed and said, "If the Central Plains make me chancellor, taking Jiangnan will be like reaching into a bag for what is already inside."

sentences.zh: ”穀後果如其言。

translations.literal: Later Gu indeed spoke as foretold.
translations.idiomatic: Later events proved Gu's words true.

sentences.zh: 李昉嘗為穀記室，在淮上被病求先歸。

translations.literal: Li Fang had once been Gu's registry clerk; on the Huai he fell ill and begged to return first.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fang had once served as Gu's registry clerk. While on the Huai he fell ill and asked to return home first.

sentences.zh: 穀視之曰：“子他日官祿當如我。

translations.literal: Gu looked at him and said: "You one day will have office and emolument like mine."
translations.idiomatic: Gu looked at him and said, "One day your office and emolument will be like mine."

sentences.zh: ”昉後至宰相、司空。

translations.literal: Fang later reached chief minister and Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Fang later rose to chief minister and Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 周顯德中，扈載以文章馳名，樞密使王樸薦令知制誥。

translations.literal: In Zhou Xiande, Hu Zai was famed for literary talent; Military Affairs Commissioner Wang Pu recommended him for drafting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xiande era of Zhou, Hu Zai was famed for his literary talent, and Military Affairs Commissioner Wang Pu recommended him to draft edicts.

sentences.zh: 除書未下，樸詣中書言之。

translations.literal: Before the appointment edict issued, Pu went to the Secretariat to speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: Before the appointment edict was issued, Pu went to the Secretariat to speak of it.

sentences.zh: 穀曰：“斯人薄命，慮不克享耳。

translations.literal: Gu said: "This man's fate is thin; I fear he will not enjoy it to the end."
translations.idiomatic: Gu said, "This man's fate is thin. I fear he will not live to enjoy the appointment."

sentences.zh: ”樸曰：“公在衡石之地，當以材進人，何得言命而遺才。

translations.literal: Pu said: "Sir, you stand where the scale and stone weigh—you ought to advance people by talent; how can you speak of fate and abandon worth?"
translations.idiomatic: Pu said, "Sir, you stand where the scales weigh. You ought to advance people by talent. How can you speak of fate and abandon worth?"

sentences.zh: ”載遂知制誥，遷翰林學士，未幾卒。

translations.literal: Zai then became drafter of edicts, was transferred to Hanlin Academician, and before long died.
translations.idiomatic: Zai then became drafter of edicts, was transferred to Hanlin Academician, and before long died.

sentences.zh: 世謂樸能薦士，穀能知人。

translations.literal: The age said Pu could recommend scholars and Gu could know men.
translations.idiomatic: People said Wang Pu could recommend talent and Li Gu could discern character.

sentences.zh: 穀歸洛中，昭義李筠以穀周朝名相，遺錢五十萬，他物稱是，穀受之。

translations.literal: When Gu returned to Luoyang, Zhaoyi's Li Yun, regarding Gu as a famous chief minister of the Zhou court, sent five hundred thousand cash and other gifts in proportion; Gu accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: When Gu returned to Luoyang, Li Yun of Zhaoyi, taking him for a famous chief minister of the Zhou court, sent five hundred thousand cash and comparable gifts in kind, and Gu accepted them.

sentences.zh: 既而筠叛，穀憂恚而終。

translations.literal: Before long Yun rebelled, and Gu died of worry and indignation.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yun rebelled, and Gu died of grief and distress.

sentences.zh: 子吉至補闕，拱至太子中允。

translations.literal: His son Ji reached Remonstrating Censor; Gong reached Crown Prince Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ji rose to Remonstrating Censor, and Gong to Attendant in the Crown Prince's palace.

sentences.zh: 昝居潤

translations.literal: Zan Jurun
translations.idiomatic: Zan Jurun

sentences.zh: 昝居潤，博州高唐人。

translations.literal: Zan Jurun was a man of Gaotang in Bo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zan Jurun came from Gaotang in Bo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 善書計。

translations.literal: He was skilled in writing and reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled in writing and accounting.

sentences.zh: 後唐長興中，隸樞密院為小吏，以謹願稱。

translations.literal: In the Changxing era of Later Tang he served the Bureau of Military Affairs as a minor clerk and was known for diligence and sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: During the Changxing era of Later Tang he served the Bureau of Military Affairs as a junior clerk and was known for diligence and sincerity.

sentences.zh: 晉初，出掌滑州廩庾，遂補牙職。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jin he went out to manage the granaries of Hua Prefecture and was then appointed to a personal staff post.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jin he was sent to manage the granaries of Hua Prefecture and was then appointed to a staff post in the military headquarters.

sentences.zh: 會景延廣留守西洛，署為右職。

translations.literal: When Jing Yanguang held the western capital as regent, he appointed him to a senior staff post.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing Yanguang served as regent of the western capital, he appointed Zan to a senior staff post.

sentences.zh: 延廣卒，居潤往依陝帥白文珂，文珂致仕，乃表薦居潤於周祖。

translations.literal: When Yanguang died, Jurun went to rely on Shaanxi commander Bai Wenke; when Wenke retired, he submitted a memorial recommending Jurun to Zhou Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanguang died, Jurun went to serve under Bai Wenke, the military governor of Shaanxi; after Wenke retired, he memorialized the throne recommending Jurun to Zhou Taizu.

sentences.zh: 太祖立，加檢校太尉。

translations.literal: When Taizu took the throne, [Jurun] was promoted to Acting Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizu ascended the throne, Jurun was given the honorary title of Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 及征澤、潞，命赴澶州巡警。

translations.literal: When [the court] campaigned against Ze and Lu, he was ordered to go to Duan Prefecture to patrol and inspect.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign against Ze and Lu, he was ordered to Duan Prefecture to conduct patrol and inspection duties.

sentences.zh: 師還，權知鎮州，加左領軍衛上將軍。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was appointed acting governor of Zhen Prefecture and promoted to General-in-Chief of the Left Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: After the army returned, he served as acting prefect of Zhenzhou and was promoted to General-in-Chief of the Left Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: 建隆二年，又權知澶州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianlong, he was again appointed acting governor of Duan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Jianlong era, he again served as acting prefect of Duanzhou.

sentences.zh: 八月，拜義武軍節度，在鎮數年，得風痹，詔還京師。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he was appointed military commissioner of the Yiwu Army; after several years in the post he contracted wind paralysis, and an edict summoned him back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he was made military governor of the Yiwu Army. After several years in the province he developed paralysis from wind affliction, and an imperial edict recalled him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 乾德四年，卒，年五十九，贈太師。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Qiande he died, aged fifty-nine; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Qiande he died at the age of fifty-nine and was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 居潤性明敏，有節概，篤於行義。

translations.literal: Jurun was by nature acute and intelligent, possessed integrity and moral courage, and was devoted to righteous conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Jurun was quick-witted and perceptive, possessed firmness of character, and was deeply committed to doing what was right.

sentences.zh: 初，晉室將亡，景延廣委其族自洛赴難，至則為遼人所執。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Jin house was nearing collapse, Jing Yanguang sent his clan from Luoyang to join him in distress, but upon arrival they were seized by the Khitans.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, as the Jin dynasty was nearing its end, Jing Yanguang sent his kinsmen from Luoyang to join him in his emergency, but they were captured by the Khitans upon arrival.

sentences.zh: 遼人在洛者遽欲恣摽掠，延廣僚吏部曲悉遁，獨居潤力保護，其家以安。

translations.literal: The Khitans in Luoyang immediately sought to loot at will; Yanguang's staff officers and retainers all fled, but Jurun alone exerted himself to protect [the family], and their household was kept safe.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitans in Luoyang at once tried to plunder without restraint. Yanguang's staff and retainers all fled, but Jurun alone worked to protect the family, and they remained secure.

sentences.zh: 居潤與太祖同事世宗，情好款浹，嘗薦沈倫於太祖，以為純謹可用，後至宰相，世稱其知人。

translations.literal: Jurun and Taizu had served Shizong together; their friendship was warm and close. He once recommended Shen Lun to Taizu as pure, careful, and usable; Shen later reached Grand Chancellor, and the age praised Jurun for knowing men.
translations.idiomatic: Jurun had served Emperor Shizong alongside Taizu, and the two were on terms of warm friendship. He once recommended Shen Lun to Taizu as honest, careful, and fit for office; Shen later rose to grand chancellor, and people praised Jurun for discerning talent.

sentences.zh: 子惟質至內園使，弟居濟至水部員外郎。

translations.literal: His son Weizhi rose to Commissioner of the Inner Park; his younger brother Juji reached Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Waterworks.
translations.idiomatic: His son Weizhi rose to Commissioner of the Inner Park, and his younger brother Juji to Outer Gentleman in the Ministry of Waterworks.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符三年，錄其孫建中為三班借職。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dazhong Xiangfu, his grandson Jianzhong was enrolled as a borrowed officer of the Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Dazhong Xiangfu, his grandson Jianzhong was granted an honorary post as borrowed officer of the Third Rank.

sentences.zh: 竇貞固

translations.literal: Dou Zhengu
translations.idiomatic: Dou Zhengu

sentences.zh: 天福三年，詔百僚各上封事，貞固疏曰：“臣聞舉善為明，知人則哲。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianfu, an edict ordered all officials to submit sealed memorials; Zhengu memorialized, saying: "Your subject has heard that to promote the good is to be enlightened, and to know men is to be wise.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tianfu, the court ordered every official to submit a sealed memorial. Zhengu wrote: "I have heard that to elevate the worthy is enlightenment, and to know men is wisdom.

sentences.zh: 聖君在位，藪澤豈有隱淪；

translations.literal: When a sage ruler holds the throne, how could marshes and meadows hide the reclusive and obscure;
translations.idiomatic: When a sage ruler sits upon the throne, how could talent remain hidden in marsh and fen;

sentences.zh: 昭代用材，政理固無紊亂。

translations.literal: In a brilliant age that employs talent, governance and order surely suffer no disorder.
translations.idiomatic: In an enlightened age that puts talent to use, government and order will surely never fall into confusion.

sentences.zh: 求賢若渴，從諫如流，鄭所以譽子皮；

translations.literal: Thirsting for the worthy as for water, receiving remonstrance as a flowing stream—therefore Zheng criticized Zi Pi;
translations.idiomatic: Thirsting for the worthy as for water, heeding remonstrance as a flowing stream—therefore Zheng criticized Zi Pi;

sentences.zh: 囗囗囗囗，囗囗囗囗，魯所以譏文仲。

translations.literal: [text missing in source], [text missing in source], therefore Lu criticized Wen Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: [text missing in source], [text missing in source], therefore Lu criticized Wen Zhong.

sentences.zh: 為國之要，進賢是先。

translations.literal: The essential point in governing a state is to advance the worthy first.
translations.idiomatic: The first duty of governing a state is to advance the worthy.

sentences.zh: 陛下方樹丕基，宜求多士。

translations.literal: Your Majesty is just now establishing a great foundation; you should seek many officers of talent.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is now laying a lasting foundation; you should seek out men of talent in great number.

sentences.zh: 乞降詔百僚，令各司議定一人，有何能識，堪何職官，朝廷依奏用之。

translations.literal: I beg that you issue an edict to the hundred officials, ordering each department to deliberate and designate one man, stating what abilities he possesses and what office he is fit for, so that the court may appoint him according to the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that Your Majesty issue an edict to the hundred officials, directing each department to select one man after deliberation, stating what talents he possesses and what office he can fill, so that the court may appoint him as recommended.

sentences.zh: 若能符薦引，果謂當才，所奏之官，望加獎賞；

translations.literal: If the recommendation proves fitting and the man is truly regarded as the right talent, the recommending official should be rewarded;
translations.idiomatic: If the recommendation proves accurate and the man is truly the right talent, the official who submitted the memorial should be rewarded;

sentences.zh: 如乖其舉，或涉徇私，所奏之官，宜加黜罰。

translations.literal: If the recommendation misses the mark or involves favoritism, the recommending official should be demoted and punished.
translations.idiomatic: If the recommendation misses the mark or involves private favoritism, the official who submitted it should be demoted and punished.

sentences.zh: 自然官由德序，位以才升。

translations.literal: Then naturally offices will follow virtue in ranking, and positions will rise by merit of talent.
translations.idiomatic: Then offices will naturally be ordered by virtue, and rank will rise according to talent.

sentences.zh: 三人同行，尚聞擇善；

translations.literal: When three men walk together, one can still hear of choosing the good;
translations.idiomatic: When three men walk together, one can still learn to choose the good among them;

sentences.zh: 十目所視，必不濫知。

translations.literal: With ten eyes watching, knowledge will surely not be indiscriminately applied.
translations.idiomatic: With ten eyes upon a man, judgment will surely not be applied carelessly.

sentences.zh: 臣職在論思，敢陳狂狷。

translations.literal: Your subject's duty lies in deliberation and reflection; I dare submit this forthright, imprudent view.
translations.idiomatic: My duty is to deliberate and advise; I dare offer this blunt and presumptuous counsel.

sentences.zh: ”書奏，帝深嘉之，命所司著為令典。

translations.literal: " When the memorial was submitted, the emperor greatly praised it and ordered the relevant office to codify it as a standing regulation.
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial reached the throne, the emperor greatly praised it and ordered the responsible office to codify it as a standing regulation.

sentences.zh: 明年，改御史中丞，與太常卿崔棁、刑部侍郎呂琦、禮部侍郎張允同詳定正冬朝會禮節、樂章及二舞行列。

translations.literal: The following year he was transferred to Assistant Censor-in-Chief and, together with Grand Master of Ceremonies Cui Shuai, Vice Minister of Punishments Lu Qi, and Vice Minister of Rites Zhang Yun, worked out in detail the rites of the winter court assembly, the musical sections, and the formations of the two dances.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made Assistant Censor-in-Chief and, together with Grand Master of Ceremonies Cui Shuai, Vice Minister of Punishments Lu Qi, and Vice Minister of Rites Zhang Yun, worked out in detail the rites of the winter court assembly, the musical sections, and the formations of the two ritual dances.

sentences.zh: 歷刑部、門下二侍郎。

translations.literal: He served successively as Vice Minister of Punishments and Vice Minister of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as Vice Minister of Punishments and Vice Minister of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 少帝即位，拜工部尚書。

translations.literal: When the Young Emperor succeeded to the throne, he was appointed Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When the Young Emperor came to the throne, Zhengu was appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 遷禮部尚書，知貢舉。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Rites and put in charge of the civil service examinations.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Minister of Rites and placed in charge of the civil service examinations.

sentences.zh: 舊制，進士夜試，繼以三燭。

translations.literal: Under the old regulations, jinshi candidates were examined at night, continuing with three candles [of illumination].
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system, jinshi candidates were examined at night, with three candles allowed for the session.

sentences.zh: 長興二年改令晝試，貞固以晝晷短，難盡士材，奏復夜試。

translations.literal: In the second year of Changxing the regulation was changed to daytime examinations; Zhengu, considering the daylight hours too short to fully assess scholarly talent, memorialized to restore night examinations.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Changxing the rule was changed to daytime examinations. Zhengu argued that the daylight hours were too short to fully test scholarly talent and memorialized to restore night examinations.

sentences.zh: 擇士平允，時論稱之。

translations.literal: In selecting scholars he was fair and even-handed, and public opinion praised him.
translations.idiomatic: In selecting candidates he was fair and even-handed, and public opinion praised him.

sentences.zh: 改刑部尚書，出為潁州團練使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Punishments and sent out as military training commissioner of Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Minister of Punishments and sent out as military training commissioner of Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，復拜刑部尚書。

translations.literal: After more than a year, he was again appointed Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: After a little more than a year, he was again appointed Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 漢祖入汴，貞固與禮部尚書王松率百官見於滎陽西，漢祖駐駕，勞問久之。

translations.literal: When Han Taizu entered Bian, Zhengu and Minister of Rites Wang Song led the hundred officials to meet him west of Xingyang; Han Taizu halted his carriage and questioned and comforted them at length.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Taizu entered Bian, Zhengu and Minister of Rites Wang Song led the hundred officials to meet him west of Xingyang. Han Taizu halted his carriage and questioned and comforted them at length.

sentences.zh: 初營宗廟，帝以姓自漢出，遂襲國號，尊光武為始祖，並親廟為五。

translations.literal: When the ancestral temple was first established, the emperor, taking his surname as springing from Han, accordingly adopted that dynastic title, honored Emperor Guangwu as founding ancestor, and together made five temples including the ancestral line.
translations.idiomatic: When the ancestral temple was first established, the emperor, holding that his surname sprang from Han, accordingly adopted that dynastic name, honored Emperor Guangwu as founding ancestor, and together with the ancestral temples made five in all.

sentences.zh: 詔群臣議，貞固上言曰：“按《王制》：‘天子七廟，諸侯五，大夫三，士一。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the ministers to deliberate; Zhengu submitted saying: "According to the 'Royal Regulations': 'The Son of Heaven has seven temples; feudal lords have five; grand masters three; officers one.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the ministers to deliberate. Zhengu submitted a memorial saying: "According to the Royal Regulations: 'The Son of Heaven has seven temples; feudal lords have five; grand masters three; officers one.

sentences.zh: ’《正義》曰：‘周之制七廟者，太祖及文王、武王之祧與親廟四也。

translations.literal: ' The 'Correct Meaning' says: 'The Zhou system of seven temples comprises the founding ancestor and the distant temples of King Wen and King Wu, together with four ancestral temples.'
translations.idiomatic: ' The Correct Meaning says: 'The Zhou system of seven temples comprises the founding ancestor, the distant temples of King Wen and King Wu, and four ancestral temples.'

sentences.zh: ’又曰：‘七廟者，據周也。

translations.literal: ' It also says: 'Seven temples refers to the Zhou model.'
translations.idiomatic: ' It also says: 'Seven temples refers to the Zhou model.'

sentences.zh: 有其人則七，無其人則五。

translations.literal: 'When there are such men, there are seven; when there are not such men, there are five.'
translations.idiomatic: 'When there are such men, there are seven; when there are not such men, there are five.'

sentences.zh: ’至光武中興，及魏、晉、宋、齊、隋、唐，或立六廟，或立四廟，蓋建國之始，未盈其數也。

translations.literal: ' Down to Guangwu's restoration and through Wei, Jin, Song, Qi, Sui, and Tang, some established six temples, some four—because at the founding of a state the number had not yet been filled.
translations.idiomatic: ' From Guangwu's restoration down through Wei, Jin, Song, Qi, Sui, and Tang, some dynasties established six temples and some four, because at the founding of a state the full number had not yet been reached.

sentences.zh: 《禮》曰‘德厚者流光’，此天子可以祀六世之義也。

translations.literal: The 'Rites' says, 'Those of deep virtue shed light afar'—this is the principle by which the Son of Heaven may sacrifice to six generations.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites says, 'Those of deep virtue shed light afar'—this is the principle by which the Son of Heaven may sacrifice to six generations.

sentences.zh: 今陛下大定寰區，重興漢祚，旁求典禮，用正宗祧，伏請立高、曾、祖、禰四親廟。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty has greatly settled the realm, revived the Han destiny, and broadly sought ritual precedents to set the legitimate ancestral line; I respectfully request establishing four ancestral temples for great-grandfather, grandfather, father, and immediate forebear.
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty has greatly settled the realm, revived the Han destiny, and broadly sought ritual precedents to establish the legitimate ancestral line. I respectfully request establishing four ancestral temples for great-grandfather, grandfather, father, and immediate forebear.

sentences.zh: 及自古聖王祖有功、宗有德、更立始祖在四廟之外，不拘定數，所以或五廟或七廟。

translations.literal: And from antiquity sage emperors and ancestral kings who had merit to the clan or virtue to honor have additionally established a Founding Ancestor outside the four temples, not bound to a fixed number—hence sometimes five temples, sometimes seven.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, from antiquity sage emperors and ancestral kings who had merit to the clan or virtue to honor have additionally established a founding ancestor outside the four temples, not bound to a fixed number—hence sometimes five temples and sometimes seven.

sentences.zh: 今請尊高皇帝、光武皇帝為始祖，法文王、武王不遷之制，用歷代六廟之規，庶合典禮。

translations.literal: Now I request honoring Emperor Gao and Emperor Guangwu as founding ancestors, following the system of King Wen and King Wu who are not moved, and employing the six-temple precedent of successive dynasties, so that it may accord with ritual canon.
translations.idiomatic: Now I request honoring Emperor Gao and Emperor Guangwu as founding ancestors, following the system by which King Wen and King Wu are not moved, and employing the six-temple precedent of successive dynasties, so that the arrangement may accord with ritual canon.

sentences.zh: ”漢祖從之。

translations.literal: " Han Taizu agreed.
translations.idiomatic: " Han Taizu accepted the proposal.

sentences.zh: 論者以天子建國，各從其所起，堯自唐侯，禹生大夏是也。

translations.literal: Discussants held that when the Son of Heaven founds a state, each follows where he rose: Yao from Lord of Tang, Yu born in Great Xia—such were the cases.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators held that when the Son of Heaven founds a state, each follows the place from which he rose: Yao from Lord of Tang, Yu born in Great Xia—such were the cases.

sentences.zh: 立廟皆祖其有功，商之契，周之後稷，魏之武帝，晉之三廟是也。

translations.literal: In establishing temples all venerate those with merit to the clan: Qi of Shang, Hou Ji of Zhou, Emperor Wu of Wei, the three temples of Jin—such were the cases.
translations.idiomatic: In establishing temples, all venerate those who had merit to the clan: Qi of Shang, Hou Ji of Zhou, Emperor Wu of Wei, the three temples of Jin—such were the cases.

sentences.zh: 高祖起於晉陽，而追嗣兩漢，徒以同姓為遠祖，甚非其義；

translations.literal: The High Emperor rose at Jinyang, yet traced succession to the two Han dynasties, making distant ancestors merely by shared surname—this was greatly contrary to principle;
translations.idiomatic: The High Emperor rose at Jinyang, yet traced succession to the two Han dynasties, making distant forebears merely by shared surname—this was greatly contrary to principle;

sentences.zh: 貞固又以四親匹庶，上合高、光，失之彌遠矣。

translations.literal: Zhengu further paired the four ancestral temples with commoners yet equated them above with Gao and Guangwu—the error was all the greater;
translations.idiomatic: Zhengu further treated the four ancestral temples as equal to those of commoners while placing them above Gao and Guangwu—the error was all the greater;

sentences.zh: 但援立親廟可也，餘皆非禮。

translations.literal: Only supporting the establishment of the four ancestral temples was acceptable; the rest were all contrary to ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Only supporting the establishment of the four ancestral temples was acceptable; the rest were all contrary to ritual.

sentences.zh: 俄遷吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was transferred to Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 周祖兵起，貞固與蘇逢吉奉隱帝兵次於野，敗。

translations.literal: When Zhou Taizu raised his army, Zhengu and Su Fengji accompanied Emperor Yin with troops encamped in the field; they were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Taizu raised his army, Zhengu and Su Fengji accompanied Emperor Yin with troops encamped in the field and were defeated.

sentences.zh: 逢吉倉黃自殺，貞固遂詣周祖。

translations.literal: Fengji, in sudden panic, killed himself; Zhengu then went to Zhou Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji, in sudden panic, killed himself, and Zhengu then went to Zhou Taizu.

sentences.zh: 周祖稱太后制，委貞固與蘇禹珪、王峻同掌軍國政事。

translations.literal: Zhou Taizu issued an order in the Empress Dowager's name, entrusting Zhengu with Su Yugui and Wang Jun jointly to manage military and state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Taizu issued an order in the Empress Dowager's name, entrusting Zhengu with Su Yugui and Wang Jun jointly to manage military and state affairs.

sentences.zh: 周祖登位，加兼侍中。

translations.literal: When Zhou Taizu ascended the throne, [Zhengu] was additionally appointed Concurrent Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Taizu ascended the throne, Zhengu was additionally appointed Concurrent Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 會以馮道為首相，改監修國史。

translations.literal: When Feng Dao was appointed chief chancellor, [Zhengu] was changed to supervising compiler of dynastic history.
translations.idiomatic: When Feng Dao was appointed chief chancellor, Zhengu was reassigned as supervising compiler of dynastic history.

sentences.zh: 俄罷相，守司徒，封沂國公。

translations.literal: Soon removed from the chancellorship, he remained as Minister of Works and was enfeoffed as Duke of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon removed from the chancellorship, he retained the post of Minister of Works and was enfeoffed as Duke of Yi.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，以范質為司徒，貞固遂歸洛陽，輸課役，齒為編民。

translations.literal: When Shizong succeeded, Fan Zhi was made Minister of Works; Zhengu then returned to Luoyang, paid taxes and corvée labor, and was registered as an ordinary subject in the household rolls.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong succeeded to the throne, Fan Zhi was made Minister of Works. Zhengu then returned to Luoyang, paid taxes and corvée labor, and was registered on the rolls as an ordinary subject.

sentences.zh: 貞固不能堪，訴於留守向拱，拱不聽。

translations.literal: Zhengu could not bear it and appealed to regent Xiang Gong, who would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengu could not endure this and appealed to the regent Xiang Gong, but Gong would not listen.

sentences.zh: 宋初，以前三公赴闕陪位，詣范質，求任東宮三少，預朝請，質不為奏。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song, former Three Dukes went to court to attend investiture ceremonies; [Zhengu] called on Fan Zhi, requesting appointment as one of the Three Minor Tutors of the Eastern Palace with permission to attend court, but Zhi would not memorialize on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Song dynasty, former Three Dukes went to court to attend investiture ceremonies. Zhengu called on Fan Zhi and requested appointment as one of the Three Minor Tutors of the Eastern Palace with permission to attend court, but Zhi would not submit a memorial on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 乃還洛，放曠山水，與布衣輩攜妓載酒以自適。

translations.literal: He then returned to Luoyang, roamed mountains and rivers freely, and with men in plain clothes took courtesans and wine for his own pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: He then returned to Luoyang, roamed freely among mountains and rivers, and with commoners took courtesans and wine for his own pleasure.

sentences.zh: 開寶二年病困，自為墓誌，卒，年七十八。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaibao, gravely ill, he composed his own epitaph, died, aged seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaibao, gravely ill, he composed his own epitaph and died at the age of seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 李濤，字信臣，京兆萬年人。

translations.literal: Li Tao, styled Xinchen, was a man of Wannian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tao, styled Xinchen, came from Wannian in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 唐敬宗子郇王瑋十世孫。

translations.literal: Tenth-generation descendant of Prince Ye of Yun, son of Emperor Jingzong of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: He was a tenth-generation descendant of Prince Ye of Yun, son of Emperor Jingzong of Tang.

sentences.zh: 祖鎮，臨濮令。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhen was magistrate of Linpu.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhen served as magistrate of Linpu.

sentences.zh: 父元，將作監。

translations.literal: His father Yuan was Director of Palace Construction.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yuan served as Director of Palace Construction.

sentences.zh: 朱梁革命，元以宗室懼禍，挈濤避地湖南，依馬殷，署濤衡陽令。

translations.literal: When the Zhu Liang dynasty replaced Tang, Yuan, fearing calamity as a member of the imperial clan, took Tao and fled to Hunan, relying on Ma Yin; [Yin] appointed Tao magistrate of Hengyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhu Liang dynasty replaced Tang, Yuan, fearing calamity as a member of the imperial clan, took Tao and fled to Hunan, relying on Ma Yin, who appointed Tao magistrate of Hengyang.

sentences.zh: 濤從父兄郁仕梁為閣門使，上言濤父子旅湖湘，詔殷遣歸京師，補河陽令。

translations.literal: Tao's father's elder brother's son Yu served Liang as Gate Commander; he submitted a memorial that Tao and his father were sojourning in Hunan and Xiang; an edict ordered Yin to send them back to the capital, and [Tao] was appointed magistrate of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Tao's father's elder brother's son Yu served Liang as Gate Commander and submitted a memorial that Tao and his father were sojourning in Hunan and Xiang. An edict ordered Yin to send them back to the capital, and Tao was appointed magistrate of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 後唐天成初，舉進士甲科，自晉州從事拜監察御史，遷右補闕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiansheng in Later Tang, he passed the jinshi examination in the first class; from staff member in Jin Prefecture he was appointed Investigating Censor, then promoted to Right Remonstrating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tiansheng in Later Tang, he passed the jinshi examination in the first class. From staff member in Jin Prefecture he was appointed Investigating Censor, then promoted to Right Remonstrating Censor.

sentences.zh: 宋王從厚鎮鄴，以濤為魏博觀察判官。

translations.literal: When Prince of Song Wang Conghou governed Yecheng, he made Tao administrative adjutant for Weibo observation.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Song Wang Conghou governed Yecheng, he appointed Tao administrative adjutant for Weibo observation.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，入為起居舍人。

translations.literal: After more than a year, he entered [court] as Drafting Attendant of the Household.
translations.idiomatic: After a little more than a year, he entered court as Drafting Attendant of the Household.

sentences.zh: 晉天福初，改考功員外郎、史館修撰。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianfu in Jin, he was transferred to Secretary in the Ministry of Personnel, Outer Section, and historiographer in the History Institute.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Tianfu in Jin, he was transferred to Secretary in the Ministry of Personnel, Outer Section, and historiographer in the History Institute.

sentences.zh: 晉祖幸大梁，張從賞以盟津叛，陷洛陽，扼虎牢。

translations.literal: When Jin Taizu visited Daliang, Zhang Congshang rebelled at Mengjin, captured Luoyang, and seized Hulao Pass.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin Taizu visited Daliang, Zhang Congshang rebelled at Mengjin, captured Luoyang, and seized Hulao Pass.

sentences.zh: 故齊王全義子張繼祚者實黨之，晉祖將族其家。

translations.literal: The former Prince of Qi Zhang Quanyi's son Zhang Jizu was in fact his partisan; Jin Taizu was about to exterminate his entire family.
translations.idiomatic: The former Prince of Qi Zhang Quanyi's son Zhang Jizu was in fact his partisan, and Jin Taizu was about to exterminate his entire family.

sentences.zh: 濤上疏曰：“全義歷事累朝，頗著功效。

translations.literal: Tao submitted a memorial saying: "Quanyi served successive courts and achieved considerable merit.
translations.idiomatic: Tao submitted a memorial saying: "Quanyi served successive courts and achieved considerable merit.

sentences.zh: 當巢、蔡之亂，京師為墟，全義手披荊棘，再造都邑，垂五十年，洛民賴之。

translations.literal: During the disorders of Huang Chao and Cai, the capital became ruins; Quanyi personally cleared through thorns and brambles and rebuilt the capital, nearly fifty years—the people of Luoyang relied upon him.
translations.idiomatic: During the disorders of Huang Chao and Cai, the capital lay in ruins. Quanyi personally cleared through thorns and brambles and rebuilt the city. For nearly fifty years the people of Luoyang relied upon him.

sentences.zh: 乞以全義之故，止罪繼祚妻子。

translations.literal: I beg that for Quanyi's sake punishment be limited to Jizu's wife and children alone.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that for Quanyi's sake punishment be limited to Jizu's wife and children alone.

sentences.zh: ”從之。

translations.literal: " [The emperor] agreed.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 嘗奉詔為宋州括田使，前雄州刺史袁正辭齎束帛遺濤，以田園為託，濤表其事，晉祖嘉之。

translations.literal: He once received an edict to serve as land survey commissioner for Song Prefecture; the former prefect of Xiong Prefecture Yuan Zhengcí brought silks as a gift to Tao and entrusted his fields and gardens to him; Tao memorialized the matter, and Jin Taizu praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He once received an edict to serve as land survey commissioner for Song Prefecture. The former prefect of Xiong Prefecture, Yuan Zhengcí, brought silks as a gift to Tao and entrusted his fields and gardens to him. Tao memorialized the matter, and Jin Taizu praised him.

sentences.zh: 正辭坐降一階，濤遷浚儀令。

translations.literal: Zhengcí was demoted one rank for the offense; Tao was promoted to magistrate of Junyi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengcí was demoted one rank for the offense, and Tao was promoted to magistrate of Junyi.

sentences.zh: 改比部郎中、鹽判官，改刑部郎中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director in the Ministry of Revenue and salt commissioner, then to Director in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Director in the Ministry of Revenue and salt commissioner, then to Director in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 涇帥張彥澤殺記室張式，奪其妻，式家人詣闕上訴。

translations.literal: Jing military commissioner Zhang Yanze killed recorder Zhang Shi and seized his wife; Shi's family went to the palace gate to lodge a complaint.
translations.idiomatic: The military governor of Jing, Zhang Yanze, killed his recorder Zhang Shi and seized his wife. Shi's family went to the palace gate to lodge a complaint.

sentences.zh: 晉祖以彥澤有軍功，釋其罪。

translations.literal: Jin Taizu, because Yanze had military merit, released him from punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Taizu, because Yanze had military merit, released him from punishment.

sentences.zh: 濤伏閣抗疏，請置於法。

translations.literal: Tao submitted a memorial from within the gate in protest, requesting that [Yanze] be punished according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Tao submitted a memorial from within the gate in protest, requesting that Yanze be punished according to law.

sentences.zh: 晉祖召見諭之，濤植笏叩階，聲色俱厲，晉祖怒叱之，濤執笏如初。

translations.literal: Jin Taizu summoned him for an audience and tried to persuade him; Tao planted his tablet and knocked it on the steps—his voice and bearing both fierce; Jin Taizu angrily shouted at him, but Tao held his tablet as before.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Taizu summoned him for an audience and tried to persuade him. Tao planted his tablet and knocked it on the steps, his voice and bearing both fierce. Jin Taizu angrily shouted at him, but Tao held his tablet as before.

sentences.zh: 晉祖曰：“吾與彥澤有誓約，恕其死。

translations.literal: Jin Taizu said: "I have a sworn pact with Yanze and have promised to spare his life.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Taizu said, "I have a sworn pact with Yanze and have promised to spare his life.

sentences.zh: ”濤厲聲曰：“彥澤私誓，陛下不忍食其言；

translations.literal: " Tao said in a stern voice: "Yanze's oath was a private pledge—Your Majesty is unwilling to go back on your word;
translations.idiomatic: " Tao said sharply, "Yanze's oath was a private pledge. Your Majesty is unwilling to break your word;

sentences.zh: 范延光嘗賜鐵券，今復安在？

translations.literal: Fan Yanguang was once granted an iron certificate of immunity—where is it now?
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yanguang was once granted an iron certificate promising he would not be executed—where is it now?

sentences.zh: ”晉祖不能答，即拂衣起，濤隨之，諫不已。

translations.literal: " Jin Taizu could not answer; he at once brushed his robes and rose. Tao followed him, remonstrating without cease.
translations.idiomatic: " Jin Taizu had no reply. He brushed his robes and stood up at once. Tao followed him, remonstrating without letup.

sentences.zh: 晉祖不得已，召式父鐸、弟守貞、子希範等皆拜以官，罷彥澤節製。

translations.literal: Jin Taizu had no choice; he summoned Shi's father Duo, his younger brother Shouzhen, his son Xifan, and others, all appointing them to office, and removed Yanze's military commission.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Taizu had no choice. He summoned Shi's father Duo, his younger brother Shouzhen, his son Xifan, and the rest, appointing them all to office, and stripped Yanze of his military commission.

sentences.zh: 濤歸洛下，賦詩自悼，有“三諫不從歸去來”之句。

translations.literal: Tao returned to Luoyang, composed a poem to mourn himself, with the line "Three remonstrances rejected—I return whence I came."
translations.idiomatic: Tao returned to Luoyang and wrote a poem of self-lament containing the line, "Three remonstrances rejected—I return whence I came."

sentences.zh: 先是，范延光據鄴叛，晉祖賜鐵券許以不死，終亦不免，故濤引之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Fan Yanguang had seized Ye and rebelled; Jin Taizu granted him an iron certificate promising he would not be put to death, yet in the end he was not spared—therefore Tao cited this.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Fan Yanguang held Ye in rebellion, Jin Taizu had granted him an iron certificate promising he would not be executed, yet in the end he was not spared—therefore Tao invoked this precedent.

sentences.zh: 晉祖崩，濤坐不赴臨，停。

translations.literal: When Jin Taizu died, Tao was punished for not attending the mourning audience and was suspended from office.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin Taizu died, Tao was punished for failing to attend the mourning rites and was suspended from office.

sentences.zh: 未幾，起為洛陽令，遷屯田職方郎中、中書舍人。

translations.literal: Before long he was recalled as magistrate of Luoyang, then promoted to Gentleman of the Bureau of Tuntian and Fang and Deputy Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was recalled as magistrate of Luoyang, then promoted to Gentleman of the Bureau of Tuntian and Fang and Deputy Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 會契丹入汴，彥澤領突騎入京城，恣行殺害，人皆為濤危之。

translations.literal: When the Khitans entered Bian, Yanze led crack cavalry into the capital and killed at will; everyone feared for Tao's safety.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitans entered Bian, Yanze led crack cavalry into the capital and slaughtered without restraint. Everyone feared for Tao's life.

sentences.zh: 濤詣其帳，通刺謁見。

translations.literal: Tao went to his tent and sent in a visiting card to request an audience.
translations.idiomatic: Tao went to his tent and sent in a visiting card to request an audience.

sentences.zh: 彥澤曰：“舍人懼乎？

translations.literal: Yanze said: "Does the Deputy Director fear?
translations.idiomatic: Yanze said, "Are you afraid, Deputy Director?

sentences.zh: ”濤曰：“今日之懼，亦猶足下昔年之懼也。

translations.literal: " Tao said: "Today's fear is just like the fear you yourself knew in years past.
translations.idiomatic: " Tao said, "The fear I feel today is no different from the fear you once felt yourself.

sentences.zh: 向使先皇聽僕言，寧有今日之事。

translations.literal: Had the late emperor listened to my words, how could there be today's events?
translations.idiomatic: If the late emperor had listened to me, would any of this have happened?

sentences.zh: ”彥澤大笑，命酒對酌，濤神氣自若。

translations.literal: " Yanze laughed loudly, ordered wine, and they drank facing each other; Tao's spirit and bearing were as if nothing were amiss.
translations.idiomatic: " Yanze laughed loudly, ordered wine, and they drank together. Tao remained perfectly composed.

sentences.zh: 漢祖起義至洛，濤自汴奉百官表入對，漢祖問京師財賦，從契丹去後所存幾何，濤具對稱旨，漢祖嘉之。

translations.literal: When Han Taizu raised his revolt and reached Luoyang, Tao brought the memorial of all officials from Bian for an audience. Han Taizu asked about the capital's revenue and what remained after the Khitans withdrew; Tao answered in full to satisfaction, and Han Taizu praised him.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Taizu raised his revolt and reached Luoyang, Tao brought the memorial of all officials from Bian for an audience. Han Taizu asked how much revenue the capital still held after the Khitans withdrew. Tao answered in full to the emperor's satisfaction, and Han Taizu praised him.

sentences.zh: 至汴，以為翰林學士。

translations.literal: When they reached Bian, he was made a Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Bian, he was appointed Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 杜重威據鄴叛，高祖命高行周、慕容彥超討之，二帥不協。

translations.literal: Du Chongwei held Ye in rebellion; Gaozu ordered Gao Xingzhou and Murong Yanchao to suppress him, but the two commanders did not cooperate.
translations.idiomatic: Du Chongwei held Ye in rebellion. Gaozu ordered Gao Xingzhou and Murong Yanchao to suppress him, but the two commanders failed to cooperate.

sentences.zh: 濤密疏請親征。

translations.literal: Tao sent a secret memorial requesting that the emperor lead the campaign in person.
translations.idiomatic: Tao sent a secret memorial asking the emperor to lead the campaign in person.

sentences.zh: 高祖覽奏，以濤堪任宰輔，即拜中書侍郎兼戶部尚書、平章事。

translations.literal: Gaozu read the memorial and judged Tao fit for chief minister; he was at once appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat concurrently Minister of Revenue and Participant in Determining Affairs of State.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu read the memorial and judged Tao fit for chief minister. He was at once appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat, concurrently Minister of Revenue and Participant in Determining Affairs of State.

sentences.zh: 隱帝即位，楊邠、周祖共掌機密，史弘肇握兵柄，與武德使李鄴等中外爭權，互作威福。

translations.literal: When Yin Emperor ascended, Yang Bin and Zhou Taizu jointly handled confidential affairs; Shi Hongzhao held the military power; he and Military Virtue Commissioner Li Ye and others contested power inside and outside the court, each abusing authority for their own ends.
translations.idiomatic: When Yin Emperor ascended the throne, Yang Bin and Zhou Taizu jointly handled confidential affairs. Shi Hongzhao held military power, and he, Military Virtue Commissioner Li Ye, and others fought for authority inside and outside the court, each wielding power for personal gain.

sentences.zh: 濤疏請出邠等藩鎮，以清朝政。

translations.literal: Tao memorialized requesting that Bin and the others be sent out as military governors to purify court governance.
translations.idiomatic: Tao memorialized asking that Bin and the others be posted to military governorships so that court governance might be cleared up.

sentences.zh: 隱帝不能決，白於太后，太后召邠等諭之，反為所構，免相歸第。

translations.literal: Yin Emperor could not decide; he informed the empress dowager, who summoned Bin and the others to instruct them—but was in turn slandered by them; Tao was removed as chancellor and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Emperor could not decide and reported the matter to the empress dowager. She summoned Bin and the others to admonish them, but they slandered her in return. Tao was dismissed as chancellor and sent home.

sentences.zh: 時中書廚釜鳴者數四，濤晝寢閣中，夢嚴飾廳事，群吏趨走，云迎新宰相帶諸司使，既寤，心異之。

translations.literal: At the time the cauldrons in the Secretariat kitchen rang several times. Tao napped in his pavilion by day and dreamed of a grandly decorated hall, clerks hurrying about, saying they were receiving a new chancellor who would also hold the various commissioner posts. When he awoke, he felt it strange.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the cauldrons in the Secretariat kitchen rang several times. Tao napped in his pavilion by day and dreamed of a grandly decorated hall where clerks hurried about, saying a new chancellor was arriving who would also hold the various commissioner posts. When he awoke, he found it strange.

sentences.zh: 數日濤罷，以邠為相兼樞密使。

translations.literal: Several days later Tao was dismissed; Bin was made chancellor concurrently Commissioner of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Several days later Tao was dismissed, and Bin was made chancellor while also serving as Commissioner of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 及周祖舉兵，太后倉皇涕泣曰：“不用李濤之言，宜其亡也。

translations.literal: When Zhou Taizu raised his army, the empress dowager hurriedly wept and said: "Not heeding Li Tao's words—no wonder the dynasty is perishing.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Taizu raised his army, the empress dowager wept in alarm and said, "We did not heed Li Tao's advice. No wonder the dynasty is falling.

sentences.zh: 周初，起為太子賓客，歷刑部、戶部二尚書。
