translations.literal: At the start of Zhou, he was recalled as Guest of the Heir Apparent, then served successively as Minister of Justice and Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhou dynasty, he was recalled as Guest of the Heir Apparent and then served successively as Minister of Justice and Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 世宗宴駕，為山陵副使。

translations.literal: When Shizong died, he served as deputy commissioner for the imperial tomb.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong died, he served as deputy commissioner for the imperial tomb.

sentences.zh: 恭帝即位，封莒國公。

translations.literal: When Gongdi ascended, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Ju.
translations.idiomatic: When Gongdi ascended the throne, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Ju.

sentences.zh: 宋初，拜兵部尚書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song, he was appointed Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Song dynasty, he was appointed Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 建隆二年，濤被病。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianlong, Tao fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianlong, Tao fell ill.

sentences.zh: 有軍校尹勳董浚五丈河，陳留丁壯夜潰，勳擅斬隊長陳琲等十人，丁夫七十人皆杖一百，刵其左耳。

translations.literal: A camp officer, Yin Xun, was directing dredging of the Wuzhang River. The conscript laborers of Chenliu broke away by night. Xun on his own authority executed squad leader Chen Bei and nine others—ten men in all—and all seventy laborers were beaten one hundred strokes and had their left ears cut off.
translations.idiomatic: A camp officer named Yin Xun was supervising dredging of the Wuzhang River when the conscript laborers of Chenliu broke away one night. Xun on his own authority executed squad leader Chen Bei and nine others—ten men in all—and had all seventy laborers beaten one hundred strokes and their left ears cut off.

sentences.zh: 濤聞之，力疾草奏，請斬勳以謝百姓。

translations.literal: When Tao heard of this, though gravely ill he drafted a memorial asking that Xun be executed to appease the people.
translations.idiomatic: When Tao heard of this, though gravely ill he drafted a memorial asking that Xun be executed to appease the people.

sentences.zh: 家人謂濤曰：“公久病，宜自愛養，朝廷事且置之。

translations.literal: His family said to Tao: "You have been ill long; you should take care of yourself and set aside court affairs for now.
translations.idiomatic: His family said to Tao, "You have been ill for a long time. You should look after yourself and leave court affairs aside for now.

sentences.zh: ”濤憤言曰：“人孰無死，但我為兵部尚書，坐視軍校無辜殺人，烏得不奏？

translations.literal: " Tao said angrily: "Who does not die? But as Minister of War, if I sit by while a camp officer kills innocents, how could I not memorialize?
translations.idiomatic: " Tao said angrily, "Who does not die? But I am Minister of War. If I sit by while a camp officer kills innocent people, how can I fail to memorialize?

sentences.zh: ”太祖覽奏嘉之，詔削奪勳官爵，配隸許州。

translations.literal: " Taizu read the memorial and praised it; an edict stripped Xun of rank and fief and assigned him as convict labor in Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: " Taizu read the memorial and praised it. An edict stripped Xun of rank and title and assigned him as convict labor in Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 濤卒，年六十四，贈右僕射。

translations.literal: Tao died at sixty-four; posthumously awarded Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Tao died at sixty-four and was posthumously awarded Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 濤慷慨有大志，以經綸為己任。

translations.literal: Tao was bold and high-minded, taking statecraft as his personal charge.
translations.idiomatic: Tao was bold and ambitious, taking the governance of the realm as his personal duty.

sentences.zh: 工為詩，筆劄遒媚，性滑稽，善諧謔，亦未嘗忤物，居家以孝友聞。

translations.literal: He was skilled at poetry; his brushwork was forceful and elegant. By nature he was witty and good at humor, yet never gave offense; at home he was known for filial piety and brotherly affection.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at poetry and wrote with force and grace. By nature he was witty and fond of banter, yet never gave offense. At home he was known for filial piety and brotherly devotion.

sentences.zh: 景德三年，其孫惟勤詣闕自陳，詔授許州司士參軍。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jingde, his grandson Weiqin appeared at court to petition in person; an edict appointed him Assistant Magistrate of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jingde, his grandson Weiqin appeared at court to petition in person and was appointed Assistant Magistrate of Xuzhou by edict.

sentences.zh: 子承休至尚書水部郎中，承休子仲容。

translations.literal: His son Chenxiu reached Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Waterworks in the Secretariat; Chenxiu's son was Zhongrong.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chenxiu rose to Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Waterworks in the Secretariat. Chenxiu's son was Zhongrong.

sentences.zh: 弟 澣

translations.literal: Younger brother: Huan
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother: Huan

sentences.zh: 濤弟澣，字日新。

translations.literal: Tao's younger brother Huan, style name Rixin.
translations.idiomatic: Tao's younger brother Huan, style name Rixin.

sentences.zh: 幼聰敏，慕王、楊、盧、駱為文章。

translations.literal: From youth he was clever; he admired Wang, Yang, Lu, and Luo in their literary compositions.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was bright and quick, and he took Wang, Yang, Lu, and Luo as models in literary composition.

sentences.zh: 後唐長興初，吳越王錢騑卒，詔兵部侍郎楊凝式撰神道碑，令澣代草，凡萬餘言，文彩遒麗，時輩稱之。

translations.literal: At the start of Changxing in Later Tang, King Qian of Wuyue died. An edict ordered Vice Minister of War Yang Ningshi to compose the spirit-way stele; Huan was ordered to draft it in his place—more than ten thousand characters in all, the prose forceful and beautiful, and contemporaries praised it.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Changxing era in Later Tang, the King of Wuyue died. An edict ordered Vice Minister of War Yang Ningshi to compose the spirit-way stele, but Huan was told to draft it in his stead. The text ran to more than ten thousand characters, its prose forceful and beautiful, and contemporaries praised it.

sentences.zh: 秦王從榮召至幕中，從榮敗，勒歸田里。

translations.literal: Prince of Qin Congrong summoned him to his staff; when Congrong was defeated, he was compelled to return to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qin, Congrong, summoned him to his staff. When Congrong was defeated, Huan was forced to return to his home district.

sentences.zh: 久之，起為校書郎、集賢校理。

translations.literal: After some time he was recalled as Proofreader and Collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was recalled as Proofreader and Collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 晉天福中，拜右拾遺，俄召為翰林學士。

translations.literal: In the Tianfu era of Jin he was appointed Remonstrance Officer on the Right; soon after he was summoned as Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianfu era of Jin he was appointed Remonstrance Officer on the Right, and soon after was summoned as Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 會廢學士院，出為吏部員外郎，遷禮部郎中、知制誥。

translations.literal: When the Hanlin Academy was abolished, he went out as Outer Deputy Director of the Ministry of Personnel, then was promoted to Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites and Drafted Decrees.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hanlin Academy was abolished, he was sent out as Outer Deputy Director of the Ministry of Personnel, then promoted to Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites with responsibility for drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 復置翰林，遷中書舍人，再為學士。

translations.literal: When the Hanlin was reestablished, he was promoted to Deputy Director of the Secretariat and again became an academician.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hanlin Academy was restored, he was promoted to Deputy Director of the Secretariat and again became an academician.

sentences.zh: 時濤在西掖，縉紳榮之。

translations.literal: At the time Tao was in the Western Secretariat wing; officials honored them.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Tao served in the Western Secretariat wing, and court officials regarded the brothers with admiration.

sentences.zh: 契丹入汴，澣與同職徐台符俱陷塞北。

translations.literal: When the Khitans entered Bian, Huan and his colleague Xu Taifu both fell captive in the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitans entered Bian, Huan and his colleague Xu Taifu both fell captive north of the frontier.

sentences.zh: 永康王兀欲襲位，置澣宣政殿學士。

translations.literal: Prince Yongkang Wuyu seized the throne and appointed Huan Academician of the Xuanzheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yongkang Wuyu seized the throne and appointed Huan Academician of the Xuanzheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 兀欲死，述律立，以其妻族蕭海貞為幽州節度使。

translations.literal: When Wuyu died, Shulü was enthroned and appointed his wife's clan member Xiao Haizhen military governor of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuyu died, Shulü was enthroned and appointed Xiao Haizhen, a member of his wife's clan, military governor of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 海貞與澣相善，澣乘間諷海貞以南歸之計，海貞納之。

translations.literal: Haizhen was on friendly terms with Huan; Huan seized an opportunity to urge on Haizhen a plan to return south, and Haizhen accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Haizhen was on friendly terms with Huan. Huan seized an opportunity to suggest to Haizhen a plan to return south, and Haizhen accepted it.

sentences.zh: 周廣順二年，澣因定州孫方諫密表言契丹衰微之勢，周祖嘉焉，遣諜者田重霸齎詔慰撫，仍命澣通信。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangshun of Zhou, Huan sent a secret memorial through Sun Fangjian of Dingzhou on the Khitans' weakening trend. Zhou Taizu was pleased and dispatched the spy Tian Chongba bearing an edict of consolation, while also ordering Huan to maintain correspondence.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Guangshun under Zhou, Huan sent a secret memorial through Sun Fangjian of Dingzhou describing the Khitans' decline. Zhou Taizu was pleased and dispatched the agent Tian Chongba with an edict of consolation, while also ordering Huan to maintain correspondence.

sentences.zh: 澣復表述契丹主幼弱多寵，好擊鞠，大臣離貳，若出師討伐，因與通好，乃其時也，請速行之。

translations.literal: Huan again reported that the Khitan ruler was young and weak, surrounded by favorites, fond of cuju, and that great ministers were divided—if troops were sent on campaign and friendly ties established at the same time, this would be the moment; he asked that it be done swiftly.
translations.idiomatic: Huan again reported that the Khitan ruler was young and weak, surrounded by favorites, and fond of cuju, while his great ministers were divided. If an army were sent on campaign and friendly ties established at the same time, this would be the moment, he urged, and asked that it be done at once.

sentences.zh: 屬中原多事，不能用其言。

translations.literal: Just then the Central Plains had many troubles, and his advice could not be adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the Central Plains were beset by many troubles, and his advice could not be adopted.

sentences.zh: 澣在契丹嘗逃歸，為其所獲，防禦彌謹。

translations.literal: While in Khitan lands Huan once tried to escape and return south; he was captured by them and kept under stricter guard.
translations.idiomatic: While among the Khitans Huan once tried to escape and return south, but was captured and guarded more strictly thereafter.

sentences.zh: 契丹應曆十二年六月卒，時建隆三年也。

translations.literal: He died in the sixth month of the twelfth year of Yingli of the Khitans—corresponding to the third year of Jianlong.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the sixth month of the twelfth year of Yingli under the Khitans, which corresponded to the third year of Jianlong.

sentences.zh: 濤收澣文章編之為《丁年集》。

translations.literal: Tao collected Huan's writings and compiled them as the Dingnian Collection.
translations.idiomatic: Tao collected Huan's writings and compiled them into the Dingnian Collection.

sentences.zh: 澣二子，承確，主客郎中，承續，職方郎中。

translations.literal: Huan had two sons: Chenque, Gentleman of the Bureau of Hosts and Guests, and Chenxu, Gentleman of the Bureau of Fang.
translations.idiomatic: Huan had two sons: Chenque, Gentleman of the Bureau of Hosts and Guests, and Chenxu, Gentleman of the Bureau of Fang.

sentences.zh: 孫 仲容

translations.literal: Grandson: Zhongrong
translations.idiomatic: Grandson: Zhongrong

sentences.zh: 仲容，字儀父，舉進士甲科，除大理評事、知三原縣。

translations.literal: Zhongrong, style name Yifu, passed the jinshi in the top tier, was appointed Reviewing Official of the Grand Court of Justice and magistrate of Sanyuan County.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongrong, style name Yifu, passed the jinshi examination in the top tier and was appointed Reviewing Official of the Grand Court of Justice and magistrate of Sanyuan County.

sentences.zh: 累擢監察御史，為殿試進士考官。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Supervising Censor and served as examiner for the palace jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to Supervising Censor and served as examiner for the palace jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 真宗問題義，對稱旨，詔試中書，擢左司諫、直史館。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong questioned him on the meaning of the Classics; his answers pleased the emperor. An edict tested him at the Secretariat and promoted him to Left Remonstrance Officer and Compiler at the Historical Archives.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong questioned him on the meaning of the Classics, and his answers pleased the emperor. An edict tested him at the Secretariat and promoted him to Left Remonstrance Officer and Compiler at the Historical Archives.

sentences.zh: 天聖中，以起居郎為知制誥，累遷右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: In the Tiansheng era he served as Drafted Decrees while holding the post of Gentleman for Attending Affairs, and was repeatedly promoted to Right Remonstrance and Policy Adviser.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tiansheng era he served as drafter of edicts while holding the post of Gentleman for Attending Affairs, and was repeatedly promoted to Right Remonstrance and Policy Adviser.

sentences.zh: 在西掖八年，次當補學士，而不為宰相張士遜所喜，罷為給事中、集賢院學士、判史館、司農寺，復知制誥。

translations.literal: After eight years in the Western Secretariat wing, it was his turn to be appointed Hanlin Academician, but Grand Chancellor Zhang Shixun did not favor him; he was dismissed to serve as Attendant Imperial Counselor, Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, Commissioner for the Historical Archives and Director of the Directorate of Agriculture, while again holding Drafted Decrees.
translations.idiomatic: After eight years in the Western Secretariat wing, it was his turn to be appointed Hanlin Academician, but Grand Chancellor Zhang Shixun did not favor him. He was dismissed to serve as Attendant Imperial Counselor, Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, Commissioner for the Historical Archives and Director of the Directorate of Agriculture, while again holding responsibility for drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 及石中立、張觀補學士，始以為翰林侍讀學士。

translations.literal: When Shi Zhongli and Zhang Guan were appointed academicians, he was at last made Hanlin Attendant Reader Academician.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Zhongli and Zhang Guan were appointed academicians, he was at last made Hanlin Attendant Reader Academician.

sentences.zh: 久之，兼龍圖閣學士，至戶部侍郎卒。

translations.literal: After some time he concurrently served as Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and died as Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he concurrently served as Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and died while holding the post of Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 仲容性醇易，喜飲酒，不與物忤，與人言，未嘗及勢利。

translations.literal: Zhongrong's nature was mild and easy; he loved wine, gave no offense, and in conversation with others never touched on power or profit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongrong was mild and easygoing. He loved wine, gave no offense, and in conversation with others never spoke of power or profit.

sentences.zh: 三弟早卒，字其諸孤十餘人如己子，當世稱其長者。

translations.literal: Three younger brothers died early; he raised more than ten orphaned nephews as if they were his own sons, and his age called him a man of virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Three younger brothers died early. He educated more than ten orphaned nephews as if they were his own sons, and his age called him a man of virtue.

sentences.zh: 然於吏事非所長。

translations.literal: Yet he was not strong in administrative affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was not strong in administrative affairs.

sentences.zh: 自集制草為《冠鳳集》十二卷。

translations.literal: He himself compiled his draft edicts into the Guanfeng Collection in twelve juan.
translations.idiomatic: He himself compiled his draft edicts into the Guanfeng Collection in twelve juan.

sentences.zh: 王易簡

translations.literal: Wang Yijian
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yijian

sentences.zh: 王易簡，字國寶，京兆萬年人。

translations.literal: Wang Yijian, style name Guobao, was a man of Wannian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yijian, style name Guobao, was a native of Wannian in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 性介特寡合。

translations.literal: His character was upright and aloof; he did not easily agree with others.
translations.idiomatic: He was upright and aloof by nature and did not easily agree with others.

sentences.zh: 曾祖朏，唐劍州刺史。

translations.literal: Great-grandfather Fei was prefect of Jian Prefecture in Tang.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Fei served as prefect of Jian Prefecture under Tang.

sentences.zh: 祖遠，連州刺史。

translations.literal: Grandfather Yuan was prefect of Lian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yuan served as prefect of Lian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父貫，唐州刺史。

translations.literal: Father Guan was prefect of Tang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Guan served as prefect of Tang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 易簡少好學，工詩。

translations.literal: Yijian from youth loved learning and was skilled at poetry.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Yijian loved learning and was skilled at poetry.

sentences.zh: 會僖宗幸蜀，長安兵亂，避地山谷。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xizong went to Shu, troops rioted in Chang'an, and he fled to the mountain valleys.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xizong went to Shu, troops rioted in Chang'an, and Yijian fled to the mountain valleys.

sentences.zh: 梁乾化中，邵王友誨鎮陝，易簡舉進士，詣府拔解，友誨贈錢二十萬。

translations.literal: In the Ganhu era of Liang, Prince of Shao Youhui governed Shaan; Yijian entered the jinshi examination, went to the prefectural office for release from the local quota, and Youhui gave him two hundred thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: During the Ganhu era of Liang, Prince of Shao Youhui governed Shaan. Yijian entered the jinshi examination, went to the prefectural office for release from the local quota, and Youhui gave him two hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 明年遂擢第，復隱華山。

translations.literal: The next year he passed and again retired to Mount Hua.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he passed the examination and again retired to Mount Hua.

sentences.zh: 邠帥韓恭辟觀察支使。

translations.literal: The military governor of Bin, Han Gong, recruited him as Administrative Assistant of the Observation Commission.
translations.idiomatic: The military governor of Bin, Han Gong, recruited him as Administrative Assistant of the Observation Commission.

sentences.zh: 府罷，華帥李保衡復辟從事。

translations.literal: When that prefecture closed, the governor of Hua, Li Baoheng, again recruited him as staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: When that prefectural office closed, the governor of Hua, Li Baoheng, recruited him again as a staff officer.

sentences.zh: 逾年，尹皓代保衡，易簡仍在幕府。

translations.literal: More than a year later Yin Hao replaced Baoheng, and Yijian remained in the staff office.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later Yin Hao replaced Baoheng, and Yijian remained on the staff.

sentences.zh: 會朱友謙以河中叛歸莊宗，攻華州甚急，城中危懼，咸請築月城以自固。

translations.literal: When Zhu Youqian rebelled with Hezhong and submitted to Zhuangzong, attacking Hua Prefecture hotly, the city was in peril and fear; all urged building an outer semicircular wall for self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Youqian rebelled with Hezhong and submitted to Zhuangzong, pressing the attack on Hua Prefecture, the city was gripped by fear. Everyone urged building an outer semicircular wall for self-defense.

sentences.zh: 皓恃勇不聽，下令曰：“有敢復言者斬。

translations.literal: Hao relied on his courage and would not listen; he ordered: "Whoever dares speak of it again shall be executed.
translations.idiomatic: Hao relied on his courage and would not listen. He ordered, "Whoever dares speak of this again shall be executed.

sentences.zh: ”易簡固請，乃許。

translations.literal: " Yijian urgently petitioned again, and only then was it permitted.
translations.idiomatic: " Yijian urgently petitioned again, and only then was permission granted.

sentences.zh: 板築始畢，外城果壞，軍民賴之。

translations.literal: As soon as the plank-wall construction was finished, the outer wall indeed collapsed; soldiers and civilians relied on it.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as the plank-wall construction was finished, the outer wall indeed collapsed, and soldiers and civilians owed their safety to it.

sentences.zh: 會夜不能攻，友謙遂遁去。

translations.literal: When night fell they could not continue the assault, and Youqian fled away.
translations.idiomatic: When night fell the attackers could not press the assault, and Youqian withdrew.

sentences.zh: 皓卒，易簡歸田里。

translations.literal: When Hao died, Yijian returned to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: When Hao died, Yijian returned to his home district.

sentences.zh: 久之，召為著作郎，數月棄去。

translations.literal: After some time he was summoned as Archivist but within months resigned.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was summoned as Archivist, but within months he resigned.

sentences.zh: 復召為右拾遺，上書忤旨，出為鄧州節度推官。

translations.literal: He was again summoned as Remonstrance Officer on the Right; a memorial displeased the throne and he was sent out as judicial investigator under the military governor of Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was again summoned as Remonstrance Officer on the Right, but a memorial displeased the throne and he was sent out as judicial investigator under the military governor of Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 晉初，賜金紫，判弘文館、史館事。

translations.literal: At the start of Jin he was granted gold and purple rank insignia and served as commissioner for the Hall of Spread Culture and Historical Archives.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jin he was granted gold and purple rank insignia and served as commissioner for the Hall of Spread Culture and the Historical Archives.

sentences.zh: 晉祖為治務求速效，易簡上《漸治論》以諫之，詔書褒答，以論付史館。

translations.literal: Jin Taizu in governing sought quick results; Yijian submitted the "Gradual Governance Discourse" to remonstrate; an edict praised and answered him, and the essay was deposited in the Historical Archives.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Taizu in governing sought quick results. Yijian submitted the "Gradual Governance Discourse" to remonstrate with him. An edict praised and answered him, and the essay was deposited in the Historical Archives.

sentences.zh: 及廢翰林學士，易簡兼知內制，又拜御史中丞，歷右丞、吏部侍郎、左丞、判吏部銓。

translations.literal: When the Hanlin Academicians were abolished, Yijian concurrently handled inner court drafting; he was also appointed Censor-in-Chief, then served successively as Right Vice Censor, Vice Minister of Personnel, Left Vice Censor, and Commissioner for Personnel Selection in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hanlin Academicians were abolished, Yijian concurrently handled inner court drafting. He was also appointed Censor-in-Chief and then served successively as Right Vice Censor, Vice Minister of Personnel, Left Vice Censor, and Commissioner for Personnel Selection in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 嘗上言：“選門格敕條件具存，藩府官僚習熟者少，凡給文解，未曉規程，以致選人詣都，親求解樣，往來跋涉，重可傷閔，傳寫少差，旋復驗放。

translations.literal: He once submitted: "The regulations and edict provisions for the selection gate are all on record, yet few officials in the military prefectures are familiar with them. Whenever credentials are issued, they fail to understand the rules, so that candidates come to the capital to request specimen forms in person—traveling back and forth, a heavy burden and deeply pitiable—and slight errors in transcription lead at once to rejection and release.
translations.idiomatic: He once submitted: "The regulations and edict provisions governing the selection gate are all on record, yet few officials in the military prefectures are familiar with them. Whenever credentials are issued, they fail to understand the rules, so candidates must come to the capital in person to request specimen forms—traveling back and forth at great hardship, a matter deeply pitiable—and slight errors in transcription lead at once to rejection and release.

sentences.zh: 乞自今委南曹詳定解樣，兼錄長定格取解條，下諸州，板置州院門，每取解時，準條式遵行。

translations.literal: I request that from now on the Southern Office be charged with carefully determining the specimen credential form, and also record the provisions for obtaining credentials from the Changding regulations, distribute them to all prefectures, post them on boards at prefecture gate offices, and whenever credentials are submitted for the examination, follow the rules and formats accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: He requested that from now on the Southern Office be charged with carefully determining the specimen credential form, that the provisions for obtaining credentials from the Changding regulations also be recorded and distributed to all prefectures, posted on boards at prefecture gate offices, and that whenever credentials were submitted for the examination, the rules and formats be followed accordingly.

sentences.zh: ”從之。

translations.literal: It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 晉祖在大梁，臺省湫隘，易簡奏舉故事，一歲得元省錢二百萬，繕治省署及造器物，號為舉職。

translations.literal: When Jin Taizu was at Daliang, the central offices were cramped. Yijian memorialized proposing ancient precedents and in one year obtained two million strings of cash from the original provincial budget, repaired the provincial offices and manufactured utensils—a performance termed "fulfilling one's duties."
translations.idiomatic: When Jin Taizu was at Daliang, the central offices were cramped. Yijian memorialized proposing ancient precedents and in one year obtained two million strings of cash from the original provincial budget, repaired the provincial offices, and manufactured utensils—a performance termed "fulfilling one's duties."

sentences.zh: 周朝諱“簡”，易止名易。

translations.literal: The Zhou court tabooed the character "Jian," so Yi changed his name and was known simply as Yi.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou court tabooed the character "Jian," so Yi dropped the character from his name and was known simply as Yi.

sentences.zh: 廣順初，遷禮部尚書。

translations.literal: At the start of Guangshun he was transferred to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Guangshun he was transferred to Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 是冬，合三銓為一，令易簡權判，俄改刑部尚書。

translations.literal: That winter the three selection bureaus were combined into one; Yi was ordered to serve as acting commissioner; soon afterward he was changed to Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the three selection bureaus were combined into one, and Yi was ordered to serve as acting commissioner. Soon afterward he was transferred to Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 周祖將親郊，命判兵部，會冊四廟，命為副使。

translations.literal: When Zhou Taizu was about to perform the suburban sacrifice in person, he was ordered to serve as commissioner of the Ministry of War; when the four temples were enfeoffed, he was appointed deputy envoy.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Taizu was about to perform the suburban sacrifice in person, Yi was ordered to serve as commissioner of the Ministry of War. When the four ancestral temples were enfeoffed, he was appointed deputy envoy.

sentences.zh: 周祖晏駕，為山陵副使。

translations.literal: When Zhou Taizu died, he served as deputy envoy for the imperial tomb.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Taizu died, Yi served as deputy envoy for the imperial tomb.

sentences.zh: 顯德四年，告老，以太子少保致仕，歸鄉里。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xiande he requested retirement on grounds of age and retired as Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, returning to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Xiande he requested retirement on grounds of age, retired as Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and returned to his home district.

sentences.zh: 宋初，召加少傅。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he was summoned and promoted to Junior Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Song he was summoned and promoted to Junior Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 所居華陰，構一鳴堂、二品樓，優遊自適。

translations.literal: At his residence in Huayin he built the Hall of One Cry and the Second-Rank Tower, living at ease in comfort.
translations.idiomatic: At his residence in Huayin he built the Hall of One Cry and the Second-Rank Tower, living at ease in comfort.

sentences.zh: 建隆四年四月，無疾卒，年七十九。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fourth year of Jianlong he died without illness at age seventy-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the fourth year of Jianlong he died without illness at age seventy-nine.

sentences.zh: 子景讓，進士及第，至尚書郎。

translations.literal: His son Jingrang passed the jinshi examination and rose to Secretary in the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingrang passed the jinshi examination and rose to Secretary in the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 趙上交

translations.literal: Zhao Shangjiao
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Shangjiao

sentences.zh: 趙上交，涿州范陽人。

translations.literal: Zhao Shangjiao was a man of Fanyang in Zhuo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Shangjiao came from Fanyang in Zhuo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 本名遠，字上交，避漢祖諱，遂以字稱。

translations.literal: His original name was Yuan; his style name was Shangjiao. To avoid the taboo of Han Taizu, he was thereafter known by his style name.
translations.idiomatic: His original name was Yuan and his style name was Shangjiao. To avoid the taboo of Han Taizu, he was thereafter known by his style name.

sentences.zh: 祖光鄴，鄂州錄事參軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Guangye was administrative aide of E Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Guangye served as administrative aide of E Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父簡章，涿州司馬。

translations.literal: His father Jianzhang was vice prefect of Zhuo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jianzhang served as vice prefect of Zhuo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 上交身長七尺，黑色，美風儀，善談論，負才任氣，為鄉里所推。

translations.literal: Shangjiao stood seven chi tall, with dark complexion, handsome bearing, skilled in discourse, proud of his talent and self-assured—esteemed by his community.
translations.idiomatic: Shangjiao stood seven chi tall, with a dark complexion, handsome bearing, and skill in discourse. Proud of his talent and self-assured, he was esteemed by his community.

sentences.zh: 後唐同光中，嘗詣中山干王都。

translations.literal: During the Tongguang era of Later Tang he once went to Zhongshan to seek audience with Wang Du.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tongguang era of Later Tang he once went to Zhongshan to seek audience with Wang Du.

sentences.zh: 有和少微者亦在都門下，忌之，頗毀訾上交，都遂不為禮。

translations.literal: One He Shaowei was also in Du's retainer circle; jealous of Shangjiao, he slandered him at length, and Du then showed him no courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: One He Shaowei was also in Du's retainer circle. Jealous of Shangjiao, he slandered him at length, and Du then showed him no courtesy.

sentences.zh: 上交不得志，因南遊洛陽，與中官驃騎大將軍馬紹宏善。

translations.literal: Failing to achieve his aims, Shangjiao traveled south to Luoyang and became friendly with the eunuch Commander-in-Chief of the Right Ma Shaohong.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to achieve his aims, Shangjiao traveled south to Luoyang and became friendly with the eunuch Commander-in-Chief of the Right, Ma Shaohong.

sentences.zh: 紹宏領北面轉運制置大使，表為判官，遷殿中丞。

translations.literal: Shaohong held the post of commissioner for north-route transport and supply; he recommended Shangjiao as adjutant, who was promoted to Palace Aide.
translations.idiomatic: Shaohong held the post of commissioner for north-route transport and supply. He recommended Shangjiao as adjutant, and Shangjiao was promoted to Palace Aide.

sentences.zh: 秦王從榮開府兼判軍衛，以上交為虞部員外郎，充六軍諸衛推官。

translations.literal: When Prince of Qin Congrong opened a princely establishment and concurrently served as commissioner of the military guard, Shangjiao was appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of Works and served as judicial reviewer for the Six Armies and various guard units.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Qin, Congrong, opened a princely establishment and concurrently served as commissioner of the military guard, Shangjiao was appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of Works and served as judicial reviewer for the Six Armies and various guard units.

sentences.zh: 李澣、張沆、魚崇遠皆白衣在秦府，悉與上交友善。

translations.literal: Li Huan, Zhang Hang, and Yu Chongyuan were all commoners in the Qin princely establishment; Shangjiao befriended them all.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huan, Zhang Hang, and Yu Chongyuan were all commoners in the Qin princely establishment, and Shangjiao befriended them all.

sentences.zh: 累遷司封郎中，充判官。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Director in the Ministry of Rites and served as adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to Director in the Ministry of Rites and served as adjutant.

sentences.zh: 從榮素豪邁，不遵禮法，好昵群小。

translations.literal: Congrong was naturally bold and unrestrained, failing to observe rites and law, and fond of associating with petty men.
translations.idiomatic: Congrong was naturally bold and unrestrained, failed to observe rites and law, and was fond of associating with petty men.

sentences.zh: 上交從容言曰：“王位尊崇，當修令德以慰民望，王忍為此，獨不見恭世子、戾太子之事乎？

translations.literal: Shangjiao spoke calmly and said: "The princely position is exalted; you ought to cultivate virtue to satisfy the people's hopes. How can you bear to do this? Have you not seen what befell Crown Prince Shen and Crown Prince Li?"
translations.idiomatic: Shangjiao spoke calmly and said, "The princely position is exalted. You ought to cultivate virtue to satisfy the people's hopes. How can you bear to do this? Have you not seen what befell Crown Prince Shen and Crown Prince Li?"

sentences.zh: ”從榮怒出之，歷涇、秦二鎮州節度判官。

translations.literal: Congrong was angered and dismissed him; he then served successively as adjutant to the military governors of Jing and Qin prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Congrong was angered and dismissed him. Shangjiao then served successively as adjutant to the military governors of Jing and Qin prefectures.

sentences.zh: 從榮及禍，僚屬皆坐斥，上交由是知名。

translations.literal: When Congrong met disaster, all his staff were dismissed and punished; Shangjiao thereby became well known.
translations.idiomatic: When Congrong met disaster, all his staff were dismissed and punished. Shangjiao thereby became well known.

sentences.zh: 晉初，召為左司郎中、度支判官，歷右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jin he was summoned as Director in the Left Secretariat and fiscal adjutant, then served as Right Remonstrating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jin he was summoned as Director in the Left Secretariat and fiscal adjutant, then served as Right Remonstrating Censor.

sentences.zh: 會廢翰林學士，以上交為中書舍人、知內外制，遷刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: When the Hanlin Academicians were abolished, Shangjiao was appointed Drafting Secretary in the Secretariat and charged with inner and outer court drafting, then promoted to Vice Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hanlin Academicians were abolished, Shangjiao was appointed Drafting Secretary in the Secretariat and charged with inner and outer court drafting, then promoted to Vice Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 嘗上言：“伏睹長興中詔書：‘州縣官在任詳讞刑獄、昭雪人命者，不限歲月赴選，許令超資注官，仍賜章服。

translations.literal: He once submitted: "I respectfully observe the edict of the Changxing era: 'For prefectural and county officials who during their tenure carefully review criminal cases and exonerate wrongfully convicted lives, regardless of how many months before selection they may come, they are permitted to be registered for office above their normal grade and are granted ceremonial robes.'"
translations.idiomatic: He once submitted, "I respectfully observe the edict of the Changxing era: 'For prefectural and county officials who during their tenure carefully review criminal cases and exonerate the wrongly condemned, regardless of how many months before selection they may come, they are permitted to be registered for office above their normal grade and are granted ceremonial robes.'"

sentences.zh: 諸道州府給付公驗，躬赴行部投狀，隨給優牒，庶絕欺罔，以存激勸。

translations.literal: Each circuit and prefecture shall issue official travel documents; [the official] shall personally go to the circuit headquarters to submit a petition, and a certificate of merit shall be issued promptly, so that deceit may be eliminated and incentive preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Each circuit and prefecture shall issue official travel documents; the official shall personally go to the circuit headquarters to submit a petition, and a certificate of merit shall be issued promptly, so that deceit may be eliminated and incentive preserved.

sentences.zh: ’載詳元詔，止言州縣，未該內外職司。

translations.literal: Upon examining the original edict, it speaks only of prefectural and county officials and does not cover inner and outer court offices.
translations.idiomatic: Upon examining the original edict, it speaks only of prefectural and county officials and does not cover inner and outer court offices.

sentences.zh: 乞自今但能雪活冤獄，不限中外官，並加旌賞。

translations.literal: I request that from now on whoever can exonerate the wrongly condemned and save lives, regardless of whether they are inner or outer court officials, shall all receive commendation and reward.
translations.idiomatic: He requested that from now on whoever could exonerate the wrongly condemned and save lives, regardless of whether they were inner or outer court officials, should all receive commendation and reward.

sentences.zh: 諸道州縣委長吏抄案以聞。

translations.literal: Each circuit and prefecture shall entrust the chief official to copy the case record and report it.
translations.idiomatic: Each circuit and prefecture should entrust the chief official to copy the case record and report it.

sentences.zh: 俟本人考滿，即詣刑部投狀，毋得隔越年歲，庶使內外同律。

translations.literal: When the official himself completes his term of evaluation, he shall go to the Ministry of Punishments to submit his petition; he must not skip years in between, so that inner and outer offices may be judged by the same rule.
translations.idiomatic: When the official himself completed his term of evaluation, he should go to the Ministry of Punishments to submit his petition and must not skip years in between, so that inner and outer offices might be judged by the same rule.

sentences.zh: ”詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved the request.

sentences.zh: 俄遷戶部侍郎，拜御史中丞，彈舉無所阿避。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue, appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief, and in impeachments showed favor to none.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue and appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief. In impeachments he showed favor to none.

sentences.zh: 契丹入汴，立明宗幼子許王從益為帝，以禮部尚書王崧為左丞相，上交為右丞相。

translations.literal: When the Khitan entered Bian, they installed Mingzong's young son Prince Xu Congyi as emperor, appointing Minister of Rites Wang Song as Left Chancellor and Shangjiao as Right Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan entered Bian, they installed Mingzong's young son, Prince Xu Congyi, as emperor, appointing Minister of Rites Wang Song as Left Chancellor and Shangjiao as Right Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 契丹去，上交請去偽號，稱梁王。

translations.literal: After the Khitan departed, Shangjiao requested removal of the false title and that he be called Prince of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: After the Khitan departed, Shangjiao requested removal of the false imperial title and that Congyi be called Prince of Liang.

sentences.zh: 漢祖將至，從益遣上交馳表獻款，授檢校禮部尚書、太僕卿，遷秘書監。

translations.literal: When Han Taizu was about to arrive, Congyi sent Shangjiao with a fast dispatch to submit allegiance; he was appointed Honorary Minister of Rites and Grand Master of the Stable, then transferred to Director of the Imperial Library.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Taizu was about to arrive, Congyi sent Shangjiao with a fast dispatch to submit allegiance. Shangjiao was appointed Honorary Minister of Rites and Grand Master of the Stable, then transferred to Director of the Imperial Library.

sentences.zh: 周祖監國，命太師馮道迎湘陰公於徐州，以上交副之。

translations.literal: When Zhou Taizu served as regent, he ordered Grand Preceptor Feng Dao to welcome the Duke of Xiangyin from Xuzhou, with Shangjiao as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Taizu served as regent, he ordered Grand Preceptor Feng Dao to welcome the Duke of Xiangyin from Xuzhou, with Shangjiao as deputy.

sentences.zh: 廣順初，拜禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: At the start of Guangshun he was appointed Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Guangshun he was appointed Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 會將試貢士，上交申明條制，頗為精密，始復糊名考校。

translations.literal: When the examination of tribute scholars was about to be held, Shangjiao clarified the regulations with considerable precision, restoring for the first time sealed-name examination.
translations.idiomatic: When the examination of tribute scholars was about to be held, Shangjiao clarified the regulations with considerable precision and for the first time restored sealed-name examination.

sentences.zh: 擢扈載甲科，及取梁周翰、董淳之流，時稱得士。

translations.literal: He selected Hu Zai for first rank, and also admitted Liang Zhouhan, Dong Chun, and others—at the time called having obtained worthy men.
translations.idiomatic: He selected Hu Zai for first rank and also admitted Liang Zhouhan, Dong Chun, and others. At the time this was called having obtained worthy men.

sentences.zh: 轉戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 明年再知舉，謗議紛然。

translations.literal: The following year he again served as chief examiner; criticism arose on all sides.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he again served as chief examiner, and criticism arose on all sides.

sentences.zh: 時樞密使王峻用事，常薦童子，上交拒之。

translations.literal: At the time Director of Military Affairs Wang Jun wielded power and often recommended youths; Shangjiao refused them.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Director of Military Affairs Wang Jun wielded power and often recommended youths, but Shangjiao refused them.

sentences.zh: 峻怒，奏上交選士失實，貶商州司馬，朝議以為太重，會峻貶乃止，但坐所取士李觀、侯璨賦落韻，改太子詹事。

translations.literal: Jun was angered and memorialized that Shangjiao's selection of scholars was false; he was demoted to Vice Prefect of Shang Prefecture. Court opinion held this excessive; when Jun himself was demoted the sentence was halted, but because the scholars he had selected, Li Guan and Hou Can, had failed rhyme in their fu compositions, he was punished and made Crown Prince's Household Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was angered and memorialized that Shangjiao's selection of scholars was false. Shangjiao was demoted to Vice Prefect of Shang Prefecture, but court opinion held this excessive, and when Jun himself was demoted the sentence was halted. Because the scholars he had selected, Li Guan and Hou Can, had failed rhyme in their fu compositions, however, he was punished and made Crown Prince's Household Administrator.

sentences.zh: 顯德初，遷賓客。

translations.literal: At the start of Xiande he was transferred to Guest of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Xiande he was transferred to Guest of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 二年，拜吏部侍郎，多請告不朝，時出遊別墅。

translations.literal: In the second year he was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel; he frequently requested leave and did not attend court, often going out to his country villa.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel. He frequently requested leave and did not attend court, often going out to his country villa.

sentences.zh: 世宗因問陶穀曰：“上交豈衰老乎？

translations.literal: Shizong therefore asked Tao Gu: "Has Shangjiao perhaps grown old?"
translations.idiomatic: Shizong therefore asked Tao Gu, "Has Shangjiao perhaps grown old?"

sentences.zh: ”穀對曰：“上交昔掌貢舉，放鬻市家子李觀及第，受所獻名園，多植花卉，優遊自適。

translations.literal: Tao Gu answered: "When Shangjiao formerly managed the tribute examination, he let a market merchant's son, Li Guan, pass, and accepted from him a famed garden as a gift; he planted many flowers and lived at ease in comfort."
translations.idiomatic: Tao Gu answered, "When Shangjiao formerly managed the tribute examination, he let a market merchant's son, Li Guan, pass and accepted from him a famed garden as a gift. He planted many flowers and lived at ease in comfort."

sentences.zh: ”世宗怒，免其官。

translations.literal: Shizong was angered and removed him from office.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong was angered and removed him from office.

sentences.zh: 宋初，起為尚書右丞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he was recalled as Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Song he was recalled as Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 建隆二年正月，卒，年六十七。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Jianlong he died at age sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year of Jianlong he died at age sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 上交所蒞官以幹聞，當時稱有公輔器。

translations.literal: Shangjiao was known for competence when he took office; at the time he was said to possess the makings of a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Shangjiao was known for competence when he took office, and at the time he was said to possess the makings of a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 尤好吟詠，有集二十卷，張昭為序。

translations.literal: He was especially fond of composing poetry; he had a collection in twenty scrolls, for which Zhang Zhao wrote the preface.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially fond of composing poetry. He had a collection in twenty scrolls, for which Zhang Zhao wrote the preface.

sentences.zh: 子曮，字可畏。

translations.literal: His son Yan, style name Kewei.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yan, whose style name was Kewei.

sentences.zh: 七歲喪母過哀。

translations.literal: At seven he mourned his mother with excessive grief.
translations.idiomatic: At seven he mourned his mother with excessive grief.

sentences.zh: 十二能屬文，與兄晙同舉進士，未成名而兄夭，遂以蔭補千牛備身，歷秘書郎、殿中丞、著作郎。

translations.literal: At twelve he could compose prose; he and his elder brother Jun both entered for the jinshi examination together. Before he had achieved fame his brother died young; he then entered office by inherited privilege as Personal Guard of the Thousand Oxen, and served successively as Secretary, Palace Aide, and Archivist.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he could compose prose. He and his elder brother Jun both entered for the jinshi examination together, but before he had achieved fame his brother died young. He then entered office by inherited privilege as Personal Guard of the Thousand Oxen and served successively as Secretary, Palace Aide, and Archivist.

sentences.zh: 卒，年二十六。

translations.literal: He died at age twenty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died at age twenty-six.

sentences.zh: 有集十卷，太宗嘗取以入內。

translations.literal: He had a collection in ten scrolls; Taizong once took it into the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: He had a collection in ten scrolls, and Taizong once took it into the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 張錫，福州閩縣人。

translations.literal: Zhang Xi was a man of Min County in Fu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xi came from Min County in Fu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 梁末，劉君鐸任棣州刺史，辟為軍事判官。

translations.literal: At the end of Liang, Liu Junduo served as prefect of Di Prefecture and summoned him as military adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Liang, Liu Junduo served as prefect of Di Prefecture and summoned him as military adjutant.

sentences.zh: 棣為鄆之屬郡，郡有麴務，鄆以牙將主之，頗橫恣，民有犯麴三斤，牙將欲置於死，君鐸力不能救。

translations.literal: Di was a subordinate commandery of Yan; the commandery had a brewing monopoly, and Yan sent a military officer to oversee it who was quite overbearing. When a commoner violated the brewing law with three jin of mash, the military officer sought to put him to death; Junduo lacked the power to save him.
translations.idiomatic: Di was a subordinate commandery of Yan. The commandery had a brewing monopoly, and Yan sent a military officer to oversee it who was quite overbearing. When a commoner violated the brewing law with three jin of mash, the military officer sought to put him to death, and Junduo lacked the power to save him.

sentences.zh: 既而牙將盜麥百斛私造麴，事覺，錫判曰：“麴犯三斤，求生不克，麥盜百斛，免死誠難。

translations.literal: Later the military officer stole a hundred hu of wheat to brew mash privately; when the affair was discovered, Xi rendered judgment: "For a brewing offense of three jin, [the man] could not obtain life; for stealing a hundred hu of wheat, exemption from death is truly difficult."
translations.idiomatic: Later the military officer stole a hundred hu of wheat to brew mash privately. When the affair was discovered, Xi rendered judgment: "For a brewing offense of three jin, the man could not obtain life; for stealing a hundred hu of wheat, exemption from death is truly difficult."

sentences.zh: ”時郡吏以使府牙將乞免，錫不允，固置於法。

translations.literal: At the time commandery clerks, on behalf of the military governor's military officer, begged exemption; Xi did not consent and firmly applied the law.
translations.idiomatic: At the time commandery clerks, on behalf of the military governor's military officer, begged exemption, but Xi did not consent and firmly applied the law.

sentences.zh: 同光末，趙在禮舉兵於鄴，瀕河諸州多構亂，錫權知州事，即出省錢賞軍，皆大悅，一郡獨全，棣人賴之。

translations.literal: At the end of Tongguang, Zhao Zaili raised troops at Ye; prefectures along the Yellow River largely fell into turmoil. Xi temporarily managed prefectural affairs and immediately disbursed provincial funds to reward the troops; all were greatly pleased, and the commandery alone remained intact—the people of Di relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Tongguang, Zhao Zaili raised troops at Ye, and prefectures along the Yellow River largely fell into turmoil. Xi temporarily managed prefectural affairs and immediately disbursed provincial funds to reward the troops. All were greatly pleased, and the commandery alone remained intact—the people of Di relied on him.

sentences.zh: 後為淄川令，不畏強禦，專務愛民，刺史有所徵，不答，由是銜之。

translations.literal: Later he served as magistrate of Zichuan; he feared no powerful oppressors and devoted himself to loving the people. When the prefect sought levies he did not respond, and for this the prefect bore a grudge.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as magistrate of Zichuan. He feared no powerful oppressors and devoted himself to loving the people. When the prefect sought levies he did not respond, and for this the prefect bore a grudge.

sentences.zh: 及代，白其事於宰相馮道。

translations.literal: When his term ended, he reported the matter to Chancellor Feng Dao.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended, he reported the matter to Chancellor Feng Dao.

sentences.zh: 道知錫介直，即奏召為監察御史，出為陝、虢觀察判官。

translations.literal: Dao knew Xi's firm integrity and at once memorialized to summon him as Supervising Censor; he went out as adjutant to the military governor of Shan and Guo circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Dao knew Xi's firm integrity and at once memorialized to summon him as Supervising Censor. Xi then went out as adjutant to the military governor of Shan and Guo circuits.

sentences.zh: 晉開運二年，拜右補闕，歷起居郎、刑部員外郎、開封府判官、浚儀令、司門駕部二郎中，並以清節聞。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaiyun of Jin he was appointed Right Supplementation Censor and served successively as Diarist, Vice Director in the Ministry of Punishments, adjutant of the Kaifeng prefectural government, magistrate of Junyi, and Director in the Ministry of Revenue and Ministry of War—all renowned for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaiyun of Jin he was appointed Right Supplementation Censor and served successively as Diarist, Vice Director in the Ministry of Punishments, adjutant of the Kaifeng prefectural government, magistrate of Junyi, and Director in the Ministry of Revenue and Ministry of War—all renowned for integrity.

sentences.zh: 周顯德中，以老疾求解官，授右諫議大夫致政。

translations.literal: During Xiande of Zhou, on grounds of old age and illness he requested resignation and was granted retirement as Right Remonstrating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: During Xiande of Zhou, on grounds of old age and illness he requested resignation and was granted retirement as Right Remonstrating Censor.

sentences.zh: 宋初，改給事中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he was reappointed Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Song he was reappointed Supervising Secretary.

sentences.zh: 錫無子，宰相范質嘗兄事之，館於別墅。

translations.literal: Xi had no son; Chancellor Fan Zhi once treated him as an elder brother and lodged him at his country villa.
translations.idiomatic: Xi had no son. Chancellor Fan Zhi once treated him as an elder brother and lodged him at his country villa.

sentences.zh: 錫以執政之門，不欲久處，往依鄉人鄧州觀察判官黃保緒。

translations.literal: Xi, being at the house of the chief minister, did not wish to stay long and went to lodge with his fellow townsman Huang Baoxu, adjutant to the military governor of Deng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Being at the house of the chief minister, Xi did not wish to stay long and went to lodge with his fellow townsman Huang Baoxu, adjutant to the military governor of Deng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 建隆二年六月，卒於穰下。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the second year of Jianlong he died at Rangxia.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the second year of Jianlong he died at Rangxia.

sentences.zh: 張鑄，字司化，河南洛陽人。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhu, style name Sihua, was a man of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhu, whose style name was Sihua, came from Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 性清介，不事生產。

translations.literal: By nature upright and scrupulous, he did not engage in productive enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: By nature upright and scrupulous, he did not engage in productive enterprise.

sentences.zh: 曾祖居卿，祖裼，父文蔚，在唐俱舉進士。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Jujing, grandfather Ti, and father Wenwei—all passed the jinshi examination under Tang.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Jujing, grandfather Ti, and father Wenwei all passed the jinshi examination under Tang.

sentences.zh: 裼至翰林學士承旨、天平軍節度、檢校吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Ti rose to Hanlin Academician-in-Attendance, military governor of Tianping, and Honorary Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Ti rose to Hanlin Academician-in-Attendance, military governor of Tianping, and Honorary Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 文蔚，中書侍郎、平章事，《五代史》有傳。

translations.literal: Wenwei served as Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Counselor; he has a biography in the History of the Five Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Wenwei served as Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Counselor and has a biography in the History of the Five Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 鑄，梁貞明三年舉進士，補福昌衛、集賢校理，拜監察御史，遷殿侍御史。

translations.literal: Zhu passed the jinshi examination in the third year of Zhenming of Liang, was appointed to Fu Chang Guard and collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, was made Supervising Censor, and was promoted to Palace Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu passed the jinshi examination in the third year of Zhenming of Liang, was appointed to Fu Chang Guard and collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, was made Supervising Censor, and was promoted to Palace Censor.

sentences.zh: 仕後唐，歷起居郎、金部員外郎，賜緋，改右司員外郎。

translations.literal: Serving Later Tang, he served successively as Diarist and Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue, was granted purple rank insignia, and was changed to Vice Director in the Right Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Serving Later Tang, he served successively as Diarist and Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue, was granted purple rank insignia, and was transferred to Vice Director in the Right Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 明宗初，轉金部郎中，賜金紫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Mingzong he was transferred to Director in the Ministry of Revenue and granted gold and purple rank insignia.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Mingzong he was transferred to Director in the Ministry of Revenue and granted gold and purple rank insignia.

sentences.zh: 嘗上言曰：“國家以務農為本，守令以勸課為先，廣辟田疇，用實倉廩。

translations.literal: He once submitted: "The state takes devoted attention to agriculture as its foundation; local officials take exhortation of cultivation as their priority, broadly opening fields to fill the granaries.
translations.idiomatic: He once submitted, "The state takes devoted attention to agriculture as its foundation; local officials take exhortation of cultivation as their priority, broadly opening fields to fill the granaries.

sentences.zh: 竊見所在鄉村浮戶，方事墾辟，甫成生計，種田未至二頃，植木未及十年，縣司以定色役，民畏責斂，捨之而去，殊乖撫恤之方，徒設招攜之令。

translations.literal: I have observed that in the villages, floating households who are in the midst of opening wasteland and have just established livelihoods—having cultivated less than two qing of fields and planted trees for less than ten years—when the county office fixes their tax and corvée assignments, the people fear levies and abandon the land and leave. This greatly contradicts the method of nurturing and soothing and empties the orders to attract and gather settlers."
translations.idiomatic: I have observed that in the villages, floating households who are in the midst of opening wasteland and have just established livelihoods—having cultivated less than two qing of fields and planted trees for less than ten years—when the county office fixes their tax and corvée assignments, the people fear levies and abandon the land and leave. This greatly contradicts the method of nurturing and soothing and empties the orders to attract and gather settlers."

sentences.zh: 望令諸州應有荒田縱民墾蒔，俟及五頃已上，三年外始聽差科。

translations.literal: I hope an order will be issued that in all prefectures wasteland shall be left to the people to reclaim and sow; only after it reaches five qing or more may corvée and tax be imposed after three years.
translations.idiomatic: He hoped an order would be issued that in all prefectures wasteland should be left to the people to reclaim and sow, and that only after it reached five qing or more might corvée and tax be imposed after three years.

sentences.zh: ”從之。

translations.literal: It was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 使兩浙還，遷考功郎中。

translations.literal: After returning from a mission to the Two Zhes, he was promoted to Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: After returning from a mission to the Two Zhes, he was promoted to Director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 鑄美姿儀，善筆劄，老能燈下細書如蠅頭。

translations.literal: Zhu had handsome appearance, was skilled at calligraphy, and in old age could write fine characters by lamplight like fly heads.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu had a handsome appearance and was skilled at calligraphy. In old age he could write fine characters by lamplight like fly heads.

sentences.zh: 由晉以來，天地、宗廟及上徽號、封拜王公冊文，皆詔鑄書之。

translations.literal: From the Jin period onward, edicts for Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temples, and imperial honorific titles, as well as investiture documents enfeoffing princes and dukes, were all ordered written by Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: From the Jin period onward, edicts for Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temples, and imperial honorific titles, as well as investiture documents enfeoffing princes and dukes, were all ordered written by Zhu.

sentences.zh: 及卒，身無兼衣，家人鬻其服馬、園圃，得錢十萬以葬。

translations.literal: When he died he had no spare garment; his family sold his riding robes and garden to obtain a hundred thousand cash for burial.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he had no spare garment. His family sold his riding robes and garden to obtain a hundred thousand cash for burial.

sentences.zh: 邊歸讜

translations.literal: Bian Guidang
translations.idiomatic: Bian Guidang

sentences.zh: 邊歸讜，字安正，幽州薊人，父退思，檀州刺史。

translations.literal: Bian Guidang, style name Anzheng, was a man of Ji in You Prefecture; his father Tuisi was prefect of Tan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Guidang, whose style name was Anzheng, came from Ji in You Prefecture. His father Tuisi was prefect of Tan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 歸讜弱冠以儒學名。

translations.literal: Guidang at young adulthood was famed for classical learning.
translations.idiomatic: Guidang was famed for classical learning from young adulthood.

sentences.zh: 後唐末，客遊幷、邠。

translations.literal: At the end of Later Tang he traveled as a guest to Bing and Bin.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Later Tang he traveled as a guest to Bing and Bin.

sentences.zh: 晉祖鎮太原，召置門下，表為河東節度推官、試秘書省校書郎，改太原府推官、試大理評事。

translations.literal: The Jin founder garrisoned Taiyuan, summoned and placed him in his personal staff, memorialized to appoint him investigating officer of the Hedong military commission and acting proofreader of the Secretariat, then changed to investigating officer of the Taiyuan prefecture and acting judicial reviewer of the Grand Court.
translations.idiomatic: When the founding emperor of Later Jin was stationed at Taiyuan, he summoned Guidang into his personal staff and memorialized for his appointment as investigating officer on the Hedong military commission and acting proofreader in the Secretariat. He was later reassigned as investigating officer of Taiyuan prefecture and acting judicial reviewer in the Grand Court.

sentences.zh: 天福初，拜監察御史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianfu, appointed Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tianfu era, he was appointed Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 歷殿中侍御史、禮部員外郎，充戶部判官。

translations.literal: Served successively as Palace Attending Censor and Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites, and served as chief clerk of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as Palace Attending Censor and Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites, and also held the post of chief clerk in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 遷水部郎中，賜金紫，拜比部郎中、知制誥。

translations.literal: Promoted to Director of the Water Bureau, granted gold and purple, appointed Director of the Tribute Bureau and drafter of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Director of the Water Bureau, granted gold and purple insignia, and appointed Director of the Tribute Bureau with responsibility for drafting imperial edicts.

sentences.zh: 歷右諫議大夫、給事中。

translations.literal: Served successively as Right Remonstrator and Chief of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as Right Remonstrator and Chief of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 嘗上言：“使臣經過州縣，券料外妄自徵需，以豐傔從，多索人驢，用遞行李。

translations.literal: Once he submitted a memorial saying: "When envoys pass through prefectures and counties, beyond their warrants and rations they recklessly levy demands to enrich their attendants, requisition many people's donkeys, and use them to relay baggage."
translations.idiomatic: He once submitted a memorial saying, "When envoys pass through prefectures and counties, they go beyond their authorized warrants and rations and levy demands at will to enlarge their retinues. They requisition people's donkeys in large numbers and use them to relay their baggage."

sentences.zh: 挾命為勢，淩下作威，供億稍遲，即加鞭箠，吏民受辱，寧免怨嗟。

translations.literal: They wield imperial orders as power, bully subordinates and lord it over them, and if provisions are slightly delayed they at once add whipping and beating. Officials and commoners suffer insult—how could resentment and lament be avoided?
translations.idiomatic: They wield imperial orders as a source of power, bully their subordinates, and throw their weight around. If provisions are even slightly delayed, they immediately resort to whipping and beating. Officials and commoners suffer humiliation, and resentment is inevitable.

sentences.zh: 欲望察訪得情，嚴示懲戒。

translations.literal: I hope that investigation will ascertain the facts and strict punishment be displayed as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the court investigate these matters thoroughly and impose strict punishment as a warning.

sentences.zh: ”從之。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 俄遷右散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Soon promoted to Right Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was promoted to Right Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 漢初，歷禮部、刑部二侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Later Han, served successively as Vice Minister of Rites and Vice Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Later Han, he served successively as Vice Minister of Rites and Vice Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 時史弘肇怙權專殺，閭里告訐成風。

translations.literal: At the time Shi Hongzhao relied on power and killed at will, and denunciation in neighborhoods became the fashion.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Shi Hongzhao wielded power and executed people at will, and mutual denunciation in neighborhoods had become widespread.

sentences.zh: 歸讜言曰：“邇來有匿名書及言風聞事，構害善良，有傷風化，遂使貪吏得以報復私怨，讒夫得以肆其虛誕。

translations.literal: Guidang said: "Recently there have been anonymous letters and reports based on hearsay, framing and harming the good, injuring public morals, so that greedy officials can settle private grudges and slanderers can give free rein to their fabrications."
translations.idiomatic: Guidang said, "Recently anonymous letters and accusations based on hearsay have been used to frame and harm good people, damaging public morals. This allows corrupt officials to settle private scores and gives slanderers free rein to spread falsehoods.

sentences.zh: 請明行條制，禁遏誣罔。

translations.literal: I request that regulations be clearly enforced to forbid and restrain false accusation.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that clear regulations be enforced to forbid and suppress false accusations.

sentences.zh: 凡顯有披論，具陳姓名。

translations.literal: Whenever there is an open accusation, the accuser's name should be fully stated.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever an accusation is made openly, the accuser's name should be fully disclosed.

sentences.zh: 其匿名書及風聞事者並望止絕。

translations.literal: Anonymous letters and hearsay cases are both hoped to be entirely stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Anonymous letters and cases based on hearsay should both be abolished entirely.

sentences.zh: ”論者韙之。

translations.literal: Commentators approved it.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators praised the proposal.

sentences.zh: 周廣順初，遷兵部、戶部二侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun under Later Zhou, promoted to Vice Minister of War and Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Guangshun era under Later Zhou, he was promoted to Vice Minister of War and Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 世宗聞其亮直，擢為尚書右丞、樞密直學士，以備顧問。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong heard of his candor and integrity and promoted him to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Academician Directly Attached to the Bureau of Military Affairs, to serve for consultation.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong, having heard of his candor and integrity, promoted him to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Academician Directly Attached to the Bureau of Military Affairs, so that he might be available for consultation.

sentences.zh: 就轉左丞，世宗以累朝以來憲綱不振，命為御史中丞。

translations.literal: He was immediately transferred to Left Vice Director; Shizong, because over successive reigns the censorial discipline had not been enforced, appointed him Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was immediately transferred to Left Vice Director. Because censorial discipline had languished through successive reigns, Shizong appointed him Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 歸讜雖號廉直，而性剛介，言多忤物。

translations.literal: Although Guidang was known as incorrupt and upright, by nature he was stern and uncompromising, and his words often offended people.
translations.idiomatic: Although Guidang was known for integrity and uprightness, he was by nature stern and uncompromising, and his words often gave offense.

sentences.zh: 顯德三年冬，大宴廣德殿，歸讜酒酣，揚袂言曰：“至於一杯而已。

translations.literal: In the winter of the third year of Xiande, at a great banquet in the Hall of Broad Virtue, Guidang, deep in wine, waved his sleeve and said: "It comes to no more than one cup."
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the third year of Xiande, during a grand banquet in the Hall of Broad Virtue, Guidang, already well into his cups, waved his sleeve and cried out, "It all comes down to a single cup!"

sentences.zh: ”世宗命黃門扶出之。

translations.literal: Shizong ordered the palace eunuchs to support him out.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong ordered the palace eunuchs to escort him out.

sentences.zh: 歸讜回顧曰：“陛下何不決殺趙守微。

translations.literal: Guidang looked back and said: "Your Majesty, why not simply execute Zhao Shouwei?"
translations.idiomatic: Guidang looked back and said, "Your Majesty, why not simply have Zhao Shouwei beaten to death?"

sentences.zh: ”守微者，本村民，因獻策擢拾遺，有妻復娶，又言涉指斥，坐決杖配流，故歸讜語及之。

translations.literal: Shouwei had originally been a village commoner; because he submitted a policy proposal he was promoted to Reminder. He took a second wife though he already had one, and his words were also said to involve denunciation of the ruler. He was sentenced to beating with the execution stick and exile—hence Guidang mentioned him.
translations.idiomatic: Shouwei had originally been a village commoner. Because he submitted a policy proposal, he was promoted to Reminder. Though he already had a wife, he took another, and his words were also said to involve denunciation of the ruler. He was sentenced to beating with the execution stick and exile, which is why Guidang mentioned him.

sentences.zh: 翌日，伏閣請罪，詔釋之，仍於閣門復飲數爵，以愧其心。

translations.literal: The next day he prostrated himself at the palace gate to beg forgiveness; an edict pardoned him, and he was again given several cups to drink at the Gate of the Secretariat, to shame his heart.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he prostrated himself at the palace gate to beg forgiveness. An edict pardoned him, and at the Gate of the Secretariat he was given several more cups of wine, intended to make him feel ashamed.

sentences.zh: 五年秋，歸讜與百官班廣德殿門外，忽厲聲聞於帝，詔奪一季奉。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fifth year, Guidang stood in ranks with the hundred officials outside the gate of the Hall of Broad Virtue; suddenly a sharp voice reached the emperor, and an edict stripped him of one season's salary.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the fifth year, as Guidang stood in ranks with the other officials outside the gate of the Hall of Broad Virtue, a sharp voice suddenly reached the emperor. An edict stripped him of one season's salary.

sentences.zh: 宋初，遷刑部尚書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song, promoted to Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Song dynasty, he was promoted to Minister of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 建隆三年，告老，拜戶部尚書致仕。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianlong, he reported old age and was appointed Minister of Revenue with retirement.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jianlong, he requested retirement on grounds of age and was appointed Minister of Revenue with permission to retire.

sentences.zh: 乾德二年，卒，年五十七。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qiande he died, age fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Qiande at the age of fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 子定，雍熙二年進士及第。

translations.literal: His son Ding passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Yongxi.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ding passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Yongxi.

sentences.zh: 劉溫叟

translations.literal: Liu Wensou
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wensou

sentences.zh: 劉溫叟，字永齡，河南洛陽人。

translations.literal: Liu Wensou, style name Yongling, was a man of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wensou, whose style name was Yongling, came from Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 性重厚方正，動遵禮法。

translations.literal: By nature he was grave, solid, and upright, and in action he always observed ritual and law.
translations.idiomatic: He was grave, solid, and upright by nature, and in all his conduct he observed ritual and law.

sentences.zh: 唐武德功臣政會之後。

translations.literal: A descendant of Zhenghui, a meritorious minister of the Wude era of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: He was a descendant of Zhenghui, a meritorious minister of the Wude era under Tang.

sentences.zh: 叔祖崇望，相昭宗。

translations.literal: His granduncle Chongwang served as chancellor under Emperor Zhaozong.
translations.idiomatic: His granduncle Chongwang had served as chancellor under Emperor Zhaozong.

sentences.zh: 父岳，後唐太常卿。

translations.literal: His father Yue was Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices under Later Tang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yue was Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices under Later Tang.

sentences.zh: 溫叟七歲能屬文，善楷隸。

translations.literal: Wensou at age seven could compose prose and was skilled in regular and clerical script.
translations.idiomatic: Wensou could compose prose at the age of seven and was skilled in regular and clerical script.

sentences.zh: 岳時退居洛中，語家人曰：“吾兒風骨秀異，所未知者壽耳。

translations.literal: Yue at the time had retired to live in Luoyang and told his family: "My son's bearing is outstanding and unusual; what is not yet known is only his lifespan."
translations.idiomatic: Yue was then living in retirement in Luoyang and told his family, "My son's bearing is outstanding and unusual. The only thing we cannot yet know is how long he will live."

sentences.zh: 今世難未息，得與老夫皆為溫、洛之叟足矣。

translations.literal: The troubles of the age have not yet ceased; it would be enough if he and I could both become old men of Wen and Luo.
translations.idiomatic: The troubles of the age have not yet ceased. It would be enough if he and I could both grow old together as elders of Wen and Luo.

sentences.zh: ”故名之溫叟。

translations.literal: Therefore he was named Wensou.
translations.idiomatic: That is why he was given the name Wensou, "Warm Elder."

sentences.zh: 以蔭補國子四門助教，河南府文學。

translations.literal: By yin privilege he was appointed Assistant Instructor of the Four Gates at the Directorate of Education and Literary Officer of Henan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: By yin privilege he was appointed Assistant Instructor of the Four Gates at the Directorate of Education and Literary Officer of Henan prefecture.

sentences.zh: 清泰中，為左拾遺、內供奉。

translations.literal: During Qingtai, he served as Left Reminder and Inner Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qingtai era, he served as Left Reminder and Inner Attendant.

sentences.zh: 以母老乞歸就養，改監察御史，分司。

translations.literal: Because his mother was old he requested to return home to support her, and was changed to Supervising Censor with a detached post.
translations.idiomatic: Because his mother was elderly, he asked to return home to care for her and was reassigned as Supervising Censor with a detached post.

sentences.zh: 時臺署廢弛，溫叟作新之。

translations.literal: At the time the censorate offices had fallen into neglect; Wensou restored them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the censorate offices had fallen into neglect, and Wensou restored them.

sentences.zh: 未幾，召為右補闕。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned as Right Supplementation Officer.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was summoned to serve as Right Supplementation Officer.

sentences.zh: 契丹入汴，溫叟懼，隨契丹北遷，與承旨張允共上表求解職。

translations.literal: When the Khitan entered Bian, Wensou was afraid and followed the Khitan north in relocation; together with Academician Recipient Zhang Yun he jointly submitted a memorial requesting release from office.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan entered Bian, Wensou, in fear, followed them north in relocation. Together with Academician Recipient Zhang Yun, he submitted a memorial requesting release from office.

sentences.zh: 契丹主怒，欲出允等為縣令。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler was angry and wished to send out Yun and the others as county magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler was enraged and wished to demote Yun and the others to county magistrates.

sentences.zh: 趙延壽曰：“若學士才不稱職求解者，守本官可也，不可加貶出。

translations.literal: Zhao Yanshou said: "If academicians whose talent does not fit their duties request release, they may keep their original rank; they should not be further demoted and sent out."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yanshou said, "If academicians whose talents do not suit their posts request release, they may retain their original rank. They should not be further demoted and sent out."

sentences.zh: ”遂得罷職出院。

translations.literal: They were thus able to be dismissed from office and leave the academy.
translations.idiomatic: They were thus dismissed from office and allowed to leave the academy.

sentences.zh: 漢祖南下，溫叟自洛從至鄭州，稱疾不行。

translations.literal: When the Han founder marched south, Wensou followed from Luoyang as far as Zhengzhou, then pleaded illness and did not go on.
translations.idiomatic: When the founder of Later Han marched south, Wensou followed from Luoyang as far as Zhengzhou, then pleaded illness and went no farther.

sentences.zh: 及入汴，溫叟久之方至，授駕部郎中。

translations.literal: When he entered Bian, Wensou arrived only after a long delay and was appointed Director of the Chariot Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When the court entered Bian, Wensou arrived only after a long delay and was appointed Director of the Chariot Bureau.

sentences.zh: 周初，拜左諫議大夫，逾年，改中書舍人，加史館修撰，判館事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhou, appointed Left Remonstrator; after a year, changed to Drafting Secretary, with added duty as Compiler in the Historiography Institute, and put in charge of institute affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Later Zhou, he was appointed Left Remonstrator. After a year he was reassigned as Drafting Secretary, with the added title of Compiler in the Historiography Institute and responsibility for its affairs.

sentences.zh: 顯德初，遷禮部侍郎、知貢舉，得進士十六人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiande, promoted to Vice Minister of Rites and put in charge of the examinations, obtaining sixteen jinshi graduates.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Xiande era, he was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites and put in charge of the examinations, selecting sixteen jinshi graduates.

sentences.zh: 有譖於帝者，帝怒，黜十二人，左遷太子詹事。
