translations.literal: Someone slandered him to the emperor; the emperor was angry, dismissed twelve of the graduates, and demoted Wensou to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Someone slandered him to the emperor. The emperor was enraged, dismissed twelve of the graduates, and demoted Wensou to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 溫叟實無私，後數年，其被黜者相繼登第。

translations.literal: Wensou in fact had no partiality; several years later those who had been dismissed passed the examinations in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Wensou had in fact shown no favoritism. Several years later, those who had been dismissed passed the examinations one after another.

sentences.zh: 溫叟與張昭同修漢隱帝及周祖實錄，恭帝即位，遷工部侍郎兼判國子祭酒事。

translations.literal: Wensou together with Zhang Zhao compiled the Veritable Records of Emperor Yindi of Han and the Zhou founder; when Emperor Gongdi ascended, he was promoted to Vice Minister of Works with concurrent charge of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Wensou and Zhang Zhao jointly compiled the Veritable Records of Emperor Yindi of Han and the Zhou founder. When Emperor Gongdi ascended the throne, Wensou was promoted to Vice Minister of Works with concurrent charge of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 宋初，改刑部。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song, changed to the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Song dynasty, he was transferred to the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 建隆九年，拜御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Jianlong, appointed Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Jianlong, he was appointed Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 丁內艱，退居西洛，旋復本官。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his mother, retired to western Luoyang, and soon resumed his original post.
translations.idiomatic: Upon entering mourning for his mother, he retired to western Luoyang, but soon resumed his original post.

sentences.zh: 三年，兼判吏部銓。

translations.literal: In the third year, concurrently put in charge of the Ministry of Personnel's selection board.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, he was given concurrent charge of the Ministry of Personnel's selection board.

sentences.zh: 因上言曰：“伏見兩京百司，漸乏舊人，多隳故事。

translations.literal: Thereupon he submitted a memorial saying: "I observe that in the hundred offices of the two capitals, veteran personnel are gradually lacking and many established practices are being abandoned."
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial saying, "I observe that in the offices of the two capitals, veteran personnel are gradually disappearing and many established practices are being abandoned."

sentences.zh: 雖檢閱具存於往冊，而舉行須在於攸司。

translations.literal: Although review materials fully exist in former registers, carrying them out depends on the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: Although the regulations still exist in the old registers, putting them into practice depends on the offices responsible for them.

sentences.zh: 蓋因年限得官，歸司者例與減選；

translations.literal: This is because those who obtain office by seniority, when returning to their bureaus, are by precedent given reduced selection priority;
translations.idiomatic: This is because officials who obtain posts through seniority, when they return to their bureaus, are by precedent given reduced selection priority;

sentences.zh: 冬集赴調，授任者尋又出京。

translations.literal: those who assemble in winter for reassignment, once appointed, soon leave the capital again.
translations.idiomatic: those who assemble in the winter for reassignment, once appointed, soon leave the capital again;

sentences.zh: 兼有裁滿初官，不還舊局，但稱前資，用圖免役。

translations.literal: There are also those who have barely completed their first term, do not return to their former bureau, but merely cite their previous rank to seek exemption from service duties.
translations.idiomatic: there are also those who have barely completed their first term, do not return to their former bureau, but merely cite their previous rank in order to avoid service duties;

sentences.zh: 又有嘗因停任，切欲歸司，而元敕不該，無由復職。

translations.literal: There are also those who once had their appointments suspended and earnestly wish to return to their bureaus, but the original edict does not cover their case and they have no means to resume office.
translations.idiomatic: and there are still others who, having once had their appointments suspended, earnestly wish to return to their bureaus, but because the original edict does not cover their case, they have no way to resume office.

sentences.zh: 遂使在司者失於教習，歷事者難於追還。

translations.literal: Thus those remaining in the bureaus lack instruction and practice, and those with experience are hard to bring back.
translations.idiomatic: The result is that those who remain in the bureaus lack instruction and practice, while experienced officials are hard to bring back.

sentences.zh: 伏望自今諸司職掌，除官勒留及歸司者，如理減外欠三選以下，仍須在司執行公事，及三十月即許赴集；

translations.literal: I hope that from now on, for the duties of the various bureaus, except for officials forcibly retained and those returning to their bureaus: if beyond the proper reduction they owe fewer than three selection cycles, they should still perform official business in the bureau, and after thirty months be permitted to assemble for reassignment;
translations.idiomatic: I ask that from now on, for the duties of the various bureaus, except for officials forcibly retained and those returning to their bureaus: if beyond the proper reduction they owe fewer than three selection cycles, they should still perform official business in the bureau, and after thirty months be permitted to assemble for reassignment;

sentences.zh: 如理選外欠三選以上，及在官不成資考者，即準元敕處分。

translations.literal: if beyond the proper selection they owe three or more cycles, and those in office who fail to complete their qualification review, they should be handled according to the original edict.
translations.idiomatic: if beyond the proper selection they owe three or more cycles, and those in office who fail to complete their qualification review, they should be handled according to the original edict;

sentences.zh: 若在任停官及在司停職者，經恩後於刑部出給雪牒，卻勒歸司，如無闕員，即令守闕，餘依敕格處分。

translations.literal: if suspended from office while in post or suspended from duty while in the bureau, after an amnesty the Ministry of Punishments should issue a certificate of rehabilitation, then compel return to the bureau; if there is no vacancy, let them hold a waiting post—otherwise handle according to edicts and regulations.
translations.idiomatic: if suspended from office while in post or suspended from duty while in the bureau, after an amnesty the Ministry of Punishments should issue a certificate of rehabilitation and compel their return to the bureau; if there is no vacancy, let them hold a waiting post. All other cases should be handled according to edicts and regulations.

sentences.zh: 一日晚歸由闕前，太祖方與中黃門數人偶登明德門西闕，前騶者潛知之，以白溫叟。

translations.literal: One day, returning late and passing before the gate-tower, Taizu happened with several inner palace eunuchs to ascend the western tower of the Gate of Bright Virtue. The outriders secretly learned of it and informed Wensou.
translations.idiomatic: One day, as Wensou was returning late and passing before the gate-tower, Taizu happened to be ascending the western tower of the Gate of Bright Virtue with several inner palace eunuchs. The outriders secretly learned of this and informed Wensou.

sentences.zh: 溫叟令傳呼如常過闕。

translations.literal: Wensou ordered the heralds to announce his passage as usual when crossing before the tower.
translations.idiomatic: Wensou ordered the heralds to announce his passage as usual when crossing before the tower.

sentences.zh: 翌日請對，具言：“人主非時登樓，則近制咸望恩宥，輦下諸軍亦希賞給。

translations.literal: The next day he requested an audience and fully stated: "When the ruler ascends the tower at an unscheduled time, those nearby all hope for grace and pardon, and the armies below the capital also expect rewards."
translations.idiomatic: The next day he requested an audience and explained in full, "When the ruler ascends a tower at an unscheduled time, those nearby all hope for grace and pardon, and the armies below the capital also expect rewards."

sentences.zh: 臣所以嗬導而過者，欲示眾以陛下非時不登樓也。

translations.literal: The reason I had the heralds cry out and passed through as usual was to show the multitude that Your Majesty does not ascend the tower at unscheduled times.
translations.idiomatic: The reason I had the heralds cry out and passed through as usual was to show everyone that Your Majesty does not ascend the tower at unscheduled times.

sentences.zh: ”太祖善之。

translations.literal: Taizu approved of it.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu approved of this.

sentences.zh: 憲府舊例，月賞公用茶，中丞受錢一萬，公用不足則以贓罰物充。

translations.literal: An old custom of the censorate was monthly provision of public-use tea; the Censor-in-Chief received ten thousand cash, and if public funds were insufficient, confiscated goods from corruption cases were used to make up the difference.
translations.idiomatic: An old custom of the censorate provided monthly public-use tea. The Censor-in-Chief received ten thousand cash, and if public funds were insufficient, confiscated goods from corruption cases were used to make up the difference.

sentences.zh: 溫叟惡其名不取。

translations.literal: Wensou disliked the name of it and did not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Wensou disliked the taint associated with this practice and refused to accept the money.

sentences.zh: 任臺丞十二年，屢求代。

translations.literal: He served as censorate chief for twelve years and repeatedly requested a successor.
translations.idiomatic: He served as head of the censorate for twelve years and repeatedly requested a successor.

sentences.zh: 太祖難其人，不允。

translations.literal: Taizu found no suitable person and did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu could find no suitable replacement and did not grant the request.

sentences.zh: 開寶四年被疾，太祖知其貧，就賜器幣，數月卒，年六十三。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaibao he fell ill; Taizu knew he was poor and sent gifts of vessels and silks to his home. Several months later he died, age sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Kaibao he fell ill. Taizu, knowing he was poor, sent gifts of vessels and silks to his home. Several months later he died at the age of sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 溫叟事繼母以孝聞，雖盛暑非冠帶不敢見。

translations.literal: Wensou was famed for filial service to his stepmother; even in the height of summer he would not see her unless fully capped and girded.
translations.idiomatic: Wensou was renowned for filial devotion to his stepmother. Even in the height of summer he would not visit her unless fully capped and girded.

sentences.zh: 五代以來，言執禮者惟溫叟焉。

translations.literal: From the Five Dynasties onward, when one spoke of observing ritual, it was only Wensou.
translations.idiomatic: From the Five Dynasties onward, when people spoke of strict observance of ritual, they meant Wensou.

sentences.zh: 立朝有德望，精賞鑒，門生中尤器楊徽之、趙鄰幾，後皆為名士。

translations.literal: In court he had moral stature and refined judgment; among his students he especially valued Yang Huizhi and Zhao Linji, who later both became noted men.
translations.idiomatic: In court he enjoyed moral stature and refined judgment. Among his students he especially valued Yang Huizhi and Zhao Linji, who later both became celebrated figures.

sentences.zh: 范杲幼時，嘗以文贄溫叟，大加稱獎，以女妻之。

translations.literal: When Fan Gao was young, he once presented a literary work to Wensou, who greatly praised it and gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Gao was young, he once presented a literary work to Wensou, who praised it highly and gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 太宗在晉邸，聞其清介，遣吏遺錢五百千，溫叟受之，貯廳西舍中，令府吏封署而去。

translations.literal: When Taizong was at the Prince of Jin's residence, hearing of his integrity he sent an official to present five hundred thousand cash. Wensou accepted it, stored it in the western wing of the hall, had the prefectural clerk seal it, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong was at the Prince of Jin's residence, having heard of Wensou's integrity, he sent an official to present five hundred thousand cash. Wensou accepted the gift, stored it in the western wing of the hall, had the prefectural clerk seal it, and left.

sentences.zh: 明年重午，又送角黍、執扇，所遣吏即送錢者，視西舍封識宛然，還以白太宗。

translations.literal: The next year at the Double Fifth festival he again sent rice dumplings and a hand fan; the official sent was the same one who had brought the money. Seeing the seal on the western wing intact, he returned and reported to Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: The next year at the Double Fifth festival he again sent rice dumplings and a hand fan. The official sent was the same one who had brought the money. Seeing that the seal on the western wing remained intact, he returned and reported this to Taizong.

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：“我錢尚不用，況他人乎？

translations.literal: Taizong said: "Even my money he will not use—how much less anyone else's?"
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said, "Even my money he will not use—how much less anyone else's?"

sentences.zh: 昔日納之，是不欲拒我也；

translations.literal: In accepting it then, he did not wish to reject me;
translations.idiomatic: In accepting it then, he did not wish to reject me;

sentences.zh: 今周歲不啟封，其苦節愈見。

translations.literal: now a full year without breaking the seal—his austere integrity is all the more evident.
translations.idiomatic: now a full year has passed without the seal being broken. His austere integrity is all the more evident.

sentences.zh: ”命吏輦歸邸。

translations.literal: He ordered the official to have it carried back to the residence.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the official to have the money carried back to the residence.

sentences.zh: 是秋，太宗侍宴後苑，因論當世名節士，具道溫叟前事，太祖再三賞歎。

translations.literal: That autumn, Taizong attended a banquet in the rear garden and, discussing men of renown and integrity in the age, fully related Wensou's earlier conduct; Taizu repeatedly praised and sighed over it.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, while attending a banquet in the rear garden, Taizong spoke of men of renown and integrity in the age and fully related Wensou's earlier conduct. Taizu repeatedly praised and sighed over it.

sentences.zh: 雍熙初，子炤罷徐州觀察推官待選，以貧詣登聞求注官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongxi, his son Zhao, having left the post of investigating officer under the Xuzhou observation commission and awaiting selection, because of poverty went to the Petition Office to request an appointment.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yongxi era, his son Zhao, having left the post of investigating officer under the Xuzhou observation commission and awaiting selection, went to the Petition Office to request an appointment because of poverty.

sentences.zh: 及引對，太宗問誰氏子，炤以溫叟對。

translations.literal: When he was brought for audience, Taizong asked whose son he was; Zhao answered that he was Wensou's son.
translations.idiomatic: When he was brought for audience, Taizong asked whose son he was. Zhao replied that he was Wensou's son.

sentences.zh: 太宗愀然，召宰相語其事，且言當今大臣罕有其比。

translations.literal: Taizong looked grave, summoned the chancellor to tell him the matter, and said that among the great ministers of the day few could compare with him.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong's expression turned grave. He summoned the chancellor to tell him the story and said that among the great ministers of the day, few could compare with Wensou.

sentences.zh: 因問：“炤當得何官？

translations.literal: He then asked: "What office should Zhao receive?"
translations.idiomatic: He then asked, "What office should Zhao receive?"

sentences.zh: ”宰相言：“免選以為厚恩。

translations.literal: The chancellor said: "Exemption from the selection process would be generous favor."
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor said, "Exemption from the selection process would be generous favor."

sentences.zh: ”帝曰：“其父有清操，錄其子登朝，庶足示勸。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "His father had pure integrity; recording the son for court service would sufficiently serve as encouragement."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "His father maintained pure integrity. Enrolling the son for court service would sufficiently serve as encouragement."

sentences.zh: ”擢炤太子右讚善大夫，歷判三司理欠、憑由司，江南轉運司，入朝為司封郎中。

translations.literal: Zhao was promoted to Right Tutor of the Heir Apparent, served successively as chief judge of the Three Departments' Arrears and Credential Office, the Jiangnan transport commission, and upon entering court became Director of the Office of Enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao was promoted to Right Tutor of the Heir Apparent. He served successively as chief judge of the Three Departments' Arrears and Credential Office and on the Jiangnan transport commission, and upon entering court became Director of the Office of Enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 炳、燁並進士及第。

translations.literal: Bing and Ye both passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Bing and Ye both passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 子 燁

translations.literal: Son: Ye
translations.idiomatic: Son: Ye

sentences.zh: 燁，字耀卿，進士及第。

translations.literal: Ye, style name Yaoqing, passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Ye, whose style name was Yaoqing, passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 積官秘書省著作郎。

translations.literal: Through successive appointments he reached Drafting Officer in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive appointments to Drafting Officer in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 知龍門縣，群盜殺人，燁捕得之，將械送府，恐道亡去，皆斬之。

translations.literal: As magistrate of Longmen County, when bandits committed murder, Ye captured them; intending to send them to the prefecture in shackles, he feared they might escape on the road, and so executed them all.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as magistrate of Longmen County, Ye captured a band of murderers. He intended to send them to the prefectural seat in shackles, but fearing they might escape along the way, he had them all executed.

sentences.zh: 眾服其果。

translations.literal: The people admired his decisiveness.
translations.idiomatic: The people admired his decisiveness.

sentences.zh: 通判益州，召還，時王曙治蜀，或言其政苛暴。

translations.literal: As vice prefect of Yizhou, he was recalled to court. At the time Wang Shu was governing Shu, and some said his administration was harsh and severe.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as vice prefect of Yizhou, he was recalled to court. Wang Shu was then governing Shu, and some said his administration was harsh and severe.

sentences.zh: 真宗問：“曙治狀與淩策孰愈？

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong asked: "Whose record of governance is better, Shu's or Ling Ce's?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhenzong asked, "Whose record of governance is better—Wang Shu's or Ling Ce's?"

sentences.zh: ”燁曰：“策在蜀，歲豐事簡，故得以寬假民。

translations.literal: Ye said: "When Ce was in Shu, harvests were abundant and affairs were simple, so he was able to show leniency toward the people."
translations.idiomatic: Ye said, "When Ling Ce was in Shu, harvests were abundant and affairs were straightforward, so he could afford to be lenient toward the people."

sentences.zh: 比歲小歉，盜賊竊發，非誅殺不能禁。

translations.literal: In recent years there have been slight crop failures; thieves and bandits have secretly risen, and without executions they cannot be checked.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years there have been minor crop failures, and banditry has begun to stir. Without executions it cannot be suppressed.

sentences.zh: 然曙所行，亦未嘗出陛下法外。

translations.literal: Yet what Shu has done has never gone beyond Your Majesty's laws.
translations.idiomatic: Yet what Wang Shu has done has never exceeded the bounds of Your Majesty's laws.

sentences.zh: ”帝善之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved of this.

sentences.zh: 天禧元年，始置監官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianxi, supervisory censorial posts were first established.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianxi, supervisory censorial posts were established for the first time.

sentences.zh: 帝謂宰相曰：“諫官御史，當識朝廷大體。

translations.literal: The emperor said to the chancellor: "Remonstrating officials and investigating censors ought to understand the great principles of the court."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told the chancellor, "Remonstrating officials and investigating censors ought to understand the court's larger principles."

sentences.zh: ”於是以燁為右正言。

translations.literal: Thereupon Ye was appointed Right Rectifier.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Ye was appointed Right Rectifier.

sentences.zh: 會歲薦饑，河決滑州，大興力役，饑殍相望。

translations.literal: It happened that there was famine year after year; the Yellow River broke its banks at Huazhou; corvée labor was launched on a massive scale; and starved corpses lined the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Famine struck year after year. The Yellow River broke its banks at Huazhou, massive corvée projects were launched, and starved corpses lined the roads.

sentences.zh: 燁請策免宰相，以應天變。

translations.literal: Ye requested that the chancellor be removed by imperial edict in response to heaven's warning.
translations.idiomatic: Ye requested that the chancellor be removed by imperial edict in response to this omen from heaven.

sentences.zh: 都城東南有泉出，民爭傳可以已疾，詔即其地建祥源觀。

translations.literal: A spring appeared southeast of the capital; the people widely claimed it could cure illness; an edict ordered building the Xiangyuan Temple on that site.
translations.idiomatic: A spring appeared southeast of the capital, and people spread the rumor that its water could cure illness. An edict ordered the construction of the Xiangyuan Temple on that spot.

sentences.zh: 燁言其詭妄不經，且亢旱，不可興土木以營不急；

translations.literal: Ye said it was deceitful and absurd, and moreover in severe drought one must not undertake construction for unurgent purposes;
translations.idiomatic: Ye argued that this was deceitful nonsense, and that amid severe drought one ought not undertake construction for nonessential purposes;

sentences.zh: 又請罷提點刑獄，禁民棄父母事佛老者。

translations.literal: he also requested abolishing judicial intendants and forbidding the people to abandon their parents to follow Buddhism or Daoism.
translations.idiomatic: He also called for abolishing judicial intendants and forbidding people to abandon their parents in order to follow Buddhism or Daoism.

sentences.zh: 皆不報。

translations.literal: None received reply.
translations.idiomatic: None of these memorials received a response.

sentences.zh: 表請補外，帝以燁屢言事，乃以判三司戶部勾院，出安撫京西。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial requesting an outside appointment; because Ye repeatedly submitted memorials, the emperor gave him chief auditor of the Three Departments Revenue Office and sent him out as Pacification Commissioner of Jingxi.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial requesting a provincial appointment. Because Ye had repeatedly remonstrated, the emperor made him chief auditor of the Three Departments Revenue Office and sent him out as Pacification Commissioner of Jingxi.

sentences.zh: 還，直集賢院，同修起居注，遷右司諫。

translations.literal: Upon return he served duty at the Hall of Assembled Worthies, jointly compiled the Veritable Records, and was promoted to censor of the Right Remonstrance Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Upon his return he served at the Hall of Assembled Worthies, jointly compiled the Veritable Records, and was promoted to censor in the Right Remonstrance Bureau.

sentences.zh: 以尚書工部員外郎兼侍御史知雜事，權判吏部流內銓。

translations.literal: As Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Works in the Secretariat with additional appointment as Attendant Censor in charge of miscellaneous affairs, he acted as chief of the Ministry of Personnel's inward selection.
translations.idiomatic: Serving as Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Works in the Secretariat while also acting as Attendant Censor in charge of miscellaneous affairs, he held acting responsibility for the Ministry of Personnel's inward selection.

sentences.zh: 請京朝官遭父母憂，官司毋得奏留，故事當起復者如舊。

translations.literal: He requested that when capital officials suffered parental bereavement, the offices must not memorialize to retain them; established precedent allowing leave-from-mourning appointments would remain as before.
translations.idiomatic: He requested that when capital officials suffered parental bereavement, no office might memorialize to retain them, while established precedent allowing leave-from-mourning appointments would remain unchanged.

sentences.zh: 因詔益、梓、利、夔路長吏，仍舊奏裁，餘乞免持服者論其罪。

translations.literal: Accordingly an edict ordered that prefectural administrators of the Yi, Zi, Li, and Kui circuits might still submit memorials for imperial decision, while others who requested exemption from mourning dress would be prosecuted.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly an edict ruled that the chief administrators of the Yi, Zi, Li, and Kui circuits might still submit such cases for imperial decision, while all others who sought exemption from mourning dress would be prosecuted.

sentences.zh: 改三司戶部副使，擢龍圖閣待制，提舉諸司庫務，權發遣開封府事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to deputy commissioner of the Three Departments Revenue Office, promoted to associate drafting officer of the Dragon Diagram Hall, put in charge of the various warehouse offices, and given acting authority over Kaifeng prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to deputy commissioner of the Three Departments Revenue Office, promoted to associate drafting officer of the Dragon Diagram Hall, placed in charge of the various warehouse offices, and given acting authority over Kaifeng prefectural affairs.

sentences.zh: 累遷刑部郎中、龍圖閣直學士、知河南府，徙河中府，卒。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he reached Court Gentleman of the Ministry of Punishments, Direct Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall, and prefect of Henan; he was moved to prefect of Hezhong and died.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive promotions to Court Gentleman of the Ministry of Punishments and Direct Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall, served as prefect of Henan, was transferred to Hezhong, and died there.

sentences.zh: 初，王曙坐寇準貶官，在朝無敢往見者。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Wang Shu was demoted on account of Kou Zhun, no one at court dared go to see him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Wang Shu was demoted on account of Kou Zhun, no one at court dared visit him.

sentences.zh: 燁歎曰：“友朋之義，獨不行於今歟？

translations.literal: Ye sighed and said: "Is the bond of friendship alone no longer practiced today?"
translations.idiomatic: Ye sighed and said, "Has the bond of friendship alone ceased to be practiced in our age?"

sentences.zh: ”往餞之，經宿而還。

translations.literal: He went to send him off and returned after staying overnight.
translations.idiomatic: He went to send Wang Shu off and did not return until the following day.

sentences.zh: 嘗善河中處士李瀆，瀆死，為陳其高行，詔以著作郎贈之。

translations.literal: He had once been close to the recluse Li Du of Hezhong; when Du died, Ye set forth his lofty conduct, and an edict conferred on him posthumously the title of Drafting Officer.
translations.idiomatic: He had once been close to the recluse Li Du of Hezhong. When Du died, Ye set forth his lofty character, and an edict posthumously conferred on him the title of Drafting Officer.

sentences.zh: 唐末五代亂，衣冠舊族多離去鄉里，或爵命中絕而世系無所考。

translations.literal: In the disorder of the late Tang and Five Dynasties, many old families of the gentry departed their home districts; some had lines of enfeoffment and office cut off, and their genealogies could no longer be traced.
translations.idiomatic: In the chaos of the late Tang and Five Dynasties, many old gentry families left their home districts. Some had their lines of rank and office cut off, leaving their genealogies impossible to trace.

sentences.zh: 惟劉氏自十二代祖北齊中書侍郎環俊以下，仕者相繼，而世牒具存焉。

translations.literal: Only the Liu clan, from the twelfth-generation ancestor Huanjun, Vice Director of the Secretariat under Northern Qi, downward, had officials succeeding one another, with the genealogical records fully preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Liu clan, from their twelfth-generation ancestor Huanjun, Vice Director of the Secretariat under Northern Qi, onward, had officials succeeding one another across the generations, with their genealogical records fully preserved.

sentences.zh: 子几。

translations.literal: His son Ji.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ji.

sentences.zh: 孫 几

translations.literal: Grandson: Ji
translations.idiomatic: Grandson: Ji

sentences.zh: 几，字伯壽，以燁任為將作監主簿。

translations.literal: Ji, style name Boshou, entered office by Ye's appointment as Master Recorder of the Directorate of Imperial Works.
translations.idiomatic: Ji, whose style name was Boshou, entered office through Ye's yin privilege as Master Recorder of the Directorate of Imperial Works.

sentences.zh: 生而豪俊，長折節讀書，第進士。

translations.literal: By nature bold and spirited, in adulthood he restrained himself to study books and passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Bold and spirited by nature, he later restrained himself and devoted himself to study, then passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 從范仲淹辟，通判邠州。

translations.literal: Recruited by Fan Zhongyan, he served as vice prefect of Bin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Recruited by Fan Zhongyan, he served as vice prefect of Bin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 邠地鹵，民病遠汲，几浚渠引水注城中。

translations.literal: Bin territory was saline; the people suffered from having to draw water from afar; Ji dredged a canal to bring water into the city.
translations.idiomatic: Bin was a saline region, and the people suffered from having to draw water from far away. Ji dredged a canal to bring water into the city.

sentences.zh: 役興，客曰：“自郭汾陽城此州，苟外水可釃，何待今日？

translations.literal: When the project began, a visitor said: "Since Guo Ziyi fortified this prefecture, if outside water could be used, why wait until today?
translations.idiomatic: When the project began, a visitor said, "Since Guo Ziyi fortified this prefecture, if water from outside could have been used, why wait until today?

sentences.zh: 無為虛費勞人也！

translations.literal: Do not waste labor in vain!"
translations.idiomatic: Do not waste labor in vain!"

sentences.zh: ”几不答。

translations.literal: Ji did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Ji did not reply.

sentences.zh: 未幾，水果至，鑿五池於通逵，民大便利。

translations.literal: Before long water did arrive; he excavated five ponds along the main thoroughfare, greatly benefiting the people.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the water did arrive. He excavated five ponds along the main thoroughfare, greatly benefiting the people.

sentences.zh: 孫沔薦其才堪將帥，換如京使、知寧州。

translations.literal: Sun Mian recommended his talent as suited for generalship; he was transferred to Envoy of the Capital and made prefect of Ning Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Mian recommended him as talented enough for command. He was transferred to Envoy of the Capital and appointed prefect of Ning Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 俗喜巫，軍校仗妖法結其徒，亂有日。

translations.literal: The local custom favored spirit-mediums; military officers relied on occult arts to gather followers, and disorder was imminent.
translations.idiomatic: The local people favored spirit-mediums. Military officers used occult arts to gather followers, and rebellion was imminent.

sentences.zh: 几使他兵伏壘門以伺，夜半盡禽之。

translations.literal: Ji sent other troops to lie in wait at the camp gate; at midnight they captured them all.
translations.idiomatic: Ji sent other troops to lie in wait at the camp gate and at midnight captured them all.

sentences.zh: 加本路兵馬鈐轄、知邠州。

translations.literal: He was additionally made Military Intendant of the circuit and prefect of Bin.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally appointed Military Intendant of the circuit and prefect of Bin.

sentences.zh: 儂智高犯嶺南，几上書願自效，以為廣東、西捉殺。

translations.literal: When Nong Zhigao invaded Lingnan, Ji submitted a memorial offering himself for service and was made Pursuit-and-Suppression Commissioner of Guangdong and Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: When Nong Zhigao invaded Lingnan, Ji submitted a memorial offering to serve and was made Pursuit-and-Suppression Commissioner of Guangdong and Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 道聞蔣偕、張忠戰沒，疾馳至長沙，見狄青曰：“賊若退守巢穴，瘴毒方興，當班師以俟再舉。

translations.literal: On the road he heard that Jiang Xie and Zhang Zhong had fallen in battle; he galloped to Changsha and said to Di Qing: "If the rebels withdraw to their lair, miasma and pestilence will soon arise; the army should withdraw and wait for another campaign.
translations.idiomatic: On the road he learned that Jiang Xie and Zhang Zhong had fallen in battle. He galloped to Changsha and told Di Qing, "If the rebels withdraw to their lair, miasma and pestilence will soon arise. The army should withdraw and wait for another campaign.

sentences.zh: 若恃勝求戰，此成擒耳。

translations.literal: If they rely on victory and seek battle, they can be taken alive."
translations.idiomatic: If they grow overconfident and seek battle, they can be taken alive."

sentences.zh: ”賊果悉眾來，大戰於歸仁鋪。

translations.literal: The rebels indeed came with their entire force, and a great battle was fought at Guiren Station.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels indeed came with their entire force, and a great battle was fought at Guiren Station.

sentences.zh: 前鋒孫節死，几以右軍搏鬥，自辰至巳，勝負未決。

translations.literal: The vanguard commander Sun Jie was killed; Ji fought with the right wing from the chen hour to the si hour, with victory undecided.
translations.idiomatic: The vanguard commander Sun Jie was killed. Ji fought with the right wing from mid-morning until late morning, and the outcome remained in doubt.

sentences.zh: 几言於青，出勁騎五千，張左右翼搗其中堅，賊駭潰。

translations.literal: Ji said to Qing: deploy five thousand elite cavalry, spread left and right wings, and strike their center; the rebels, terrified, broke and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Ji told Di Qing to deploy five thousand elite cavalry, spread left and right wings, and strike the enemy center. The rebels, terrified, broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 進皇城使、知涇州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Commissioner of the Imperial City and made prefect of Jing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Commissioner of the Imperial City and appointed prefect of Jing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 陛見，辭以母老，丐復文階歸養。

translations.literal: At audience he declined on grounds of his aged mother and begged to return to civil rank to care for her.
translations.idiomatic: At audience he declined the appointment on grounds of his aged mother and begged to return to civil rank so he could care for her.

sentences.zh: 仁宗諭之曰：“涇，內地也，將母莫便焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong instructed him: "Jing is interior territory; nowhere is it more convenient to bring one's mother."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong told him, "Jing is interior territory. Nowhere could be more convenient for bringing your mother."

sentences.zh: ”命特賜冠帔。

translations.literal: He ordered special gifts of cap and sash.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered special gifts of cap and sash for Ji's mother.

sentences.zh: 領循州刺史，遷西上閣門使，再歸郎中班。

translations.literal: He was made prefect of Xunzhou concurrently, promoted to Western Upper Gate Commissioner, and returned again to the Secretariat Gentleman roster.
translations.idiomatic: He concurrently served as prefect of Xunzhou, was promoted to Western Upper Gate Commissioner, and returned again to the Secretariat Gentleman roster.

sentences.zh: 曾公亮薦之，復以嘉州團練使為太原、涇原路總管。

translations.literal: Zeng Gongliang recommended him; he was again made Regimental Commissioner of Jia Prefecture and overall commander of the Taiyuan and Jingyuan circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Gongliang recommended him, and he was again made Regimental Commissioner of Jia Prefecture and overall commander of the Taiyuan and Jingyuan circuits.

sentences.zh: 夏人寇周家堡，轉運使陳述古攝渭帥，几移文索援兵，不聽，率諸將偕請，又不聽，乃趣以手書。

translations.literal: When the Tangut raided Zhoujiabao, Transport Commissioner Chen Shugu acted as interim commander of Wei; Ji sent an official communication requesting reinforcements but was refused; leading the generals together he again requested, again without success; then he pressed the matter with a handwritten letter.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tangut raided Zhoujiabao, Transport Commissioner Chen Shugu was acting as interim commander of Wei. Ji sent an official communication requesting reinforcements but was refused. He then led the generals in a joint request, again without success, and finally pressed the matter in a handwritten letter.

sentences.zh: 述古怒，移几為鳳翔，且劾生事。

translations.literal: Shugu was angry, transferred Ji to Fengxiang, and also impeached him for stirring up trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shugu was furious. He transferred Ji to Fengxiang and also impeached him for stirring up trouble.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以總管非轉運使所得徙置，遣御史出按，述古黜，几亦改鄜州。

translations.literal: The court held that the overall commander was not someone a transport commissioner could transfer; it dispatched an investigating censor, demoted Shugu, and Ji was also transferred to Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The court ruled that an overall commander was not someone a transport commissioner could transfer at will. It dispatched an investigating censor, demoted Chen Shugu, and transferred Ji to Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 召判三班院。

translations.literal: He was recalled to serve as chief judge of the Three Ranks Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as chief judge of the Three Ranks Office.

sentences.zh: 邊吏告夏人趨大順，英宗問几。

translations.literal: Border officials reported the Tangut advancing on Dashun; Emperor Yingzong asked Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Border officials reported that the Tangut were advancing on Dashun. Emperor Yingzong asked Ji about it.

sentences.zh: 几曰：“大順天險，非夏人可得近，正恐與趙明為仇爾。

translations.literal: Ji said: "Dashun is a natural stronghold; the Tangut cannot approach it. I fear only that they mean to make an enemy of Zhao Ming."
translations.idiomatic: Ji said, "Dashun is a natural stronghold that the Tangut cannot approach. I fear only that they mean to make an enemy of Zhao Ming."

sentences.zh: ”帝曰：“明之子奔馬入城，幾為所掩，卿料敵一何神也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Ming's son fled on horseback into the city and was nearly ambushed. How divinely you read the enemy!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Zhao Ming's son fled on horseback into the city and was nearly ambushed. How uncannily you read the enemy!"

sentences.zh: ”以為秦鳳總管。

translations.literal: He was made overall commander of Qin and Feng.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed overall commander of Qin and Feng.

sentences.zh: 神宗即位，轉四方館使、知保州，治狀為河北第一。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shenzong took the throne, Ji was transferred to Commissioner of the Four Directions Hall and made prefect of Bao Prefecture; his record of governance ranked first in Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shenzong took the throne, Ji was transferred to Commissioner of the Four Directions Hall and appointed prefect of Bao Prefecture. His record of governance ranked first in Hebei.

sentences.zh: 逾六年，即請老，還為秘書監致仕。

translations.literal: After more than six years he immediately requested retirement and returned as Retired Supervisor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After more than six years he immediately requested retirement and was granted the post of Retired Supervisor of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 元豐三年，祀明堂，大臣言几知音，詔詣太常定雅樂。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanfeng, when sacrificing at the Bright Hall, ministers said Ji understood music; an edict ordered him to the Court of Ceremonial to fix the court ritual music.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yuanfeng, during the Bright Hall sacrifice, ministers said Ji understood music, and an edict ordered him to the Court of Ceremonial to fix the court ritual music.

sentences.zh: 几曰：“古樂備四清聲，沿五季亂離廢，請增之。

translations.literal: Ji said: "Ancient music included all four clear tones; through the disorder of the Five Dynasties they were abandoned; I request restoring them."
translations.idiomatic: Ji said, "Ancient music included all four clear tones, but they were abandoned in the chaos of the Five Dynasties. I request restoring them."

sentences.zh: ”樂成，予一子官。

translations.literal: When the music was completed, one son was granted an office.
translations.idiomatic: When the music was completed, one of his sons was granted an official appointment.

sentences.zh: 几得謝二十年，放曠嵩、少間，遇唐末異人靖長宮者得養生訣，故益老不衰。

translations.literal: Ji received dismissal for twenty years, lived freely between Mount Song and Mount Shao, met the Tang-dynasty recluse Jing Changgong and obtained the secret of nourishing life, and so grew ever older without decline.
translations.idiomatic: Ji enjoyed retirement for twenty years, living freely between Mount Song and Mount Shao. He met the Tang-dynasty recluse Jing Changgong and learned the secret of nourishing life, and so grew ever older without decline.

sentences.zh: 間與人語邊事，謂張耒曰：“比見詔書禁邊吏夜飲。

translations.literal: Occasionally when speaking with others about border affairs he said to Zhang Lei: "Recently I saw an edict forbidding border officials to drink at night.
translations.idiomatic: From time to time, when discussing border affairs, he told Zhang Lei, "Recently I saw an edict forbidding border officials from drinking at night.

sentences.zh: 此曹一旦有急，將使輸其肝腦，此平日禁其為樂，為今役者不亦難乎？

translations.literal: When these men face sudden crisis, they will be asked to give their very lives; yet in peacetime they are forbidden their pleasure—in such circumstances who will submit to today's orders?"
translations.idiomatic: When these men face sudden crisis, they will be asked to give their very lives. Yet in peacetime they are forbidden their pleasures. Under such circumstances, who will readily submit to today's orders?"

sentences.zh: 夫椎牛釃酒，豐犒而休養之，非欲以醉飽為德，所以增士氣也。

translations.literal: Slaughtering cattle and libating wine, rewarding them generously and letting them rest—this is not meant to bestow the virtue of drunkenness and fullness; it is meant to raise morale.
translations.idiomatic: Slaughtering cattle and libating wine, rewarding them generously and letting them rest—this is not meant to bestow the virtue of drunkenness and fullness. It is meant to raise morale.

sentences.zh: ”耒敬識其語。

translations.literal: Lei respectfully noted his words.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lei respectfully noted his words.

sentences.zh: 再加通議大夫，卒，年八十一。

translations.literal: He was further promoted to Grand Master of Conferring Counsel and died, age eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He was further promoted to Grand Master of Conferring Counsel and died at the age of eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 几篤於風義，推父遺恩官從兄，已得任子，必先兄弟子之孤者。

translations.literal: Ji was devoted to righteousness among friends; extending his father's legacy of privilege appointments to a paternal cousin, when he already had a yin appointment for his son, he always gave precedence to orphaned sons of his brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Ji was deeply devoted to the duties of friendship and honor. When extending his father's legacy of privilege appointments to a paternal cousin, he already had a yin appointment for his own son but always gave precedence to orphaned sons of his brothers.

sentences.zh: 其議樂律最善，以為：“律主於人聲，不以尺度求合。

translations.literal: His discussions of musical pitch were the finest; he held: "Pitch pipes depend on human voice; one must not seek accord through measure and scale alone."
translations.idiomatic: He was at his best when discussing musical pitch. He held that pitch pipes depend on the human voice and must not be forced into accord by measure and scale alone.

sentences.zh: 古今異時，聲亦隨變，猶以古冠服加於今人，安得而稱。

translations.literal: Times ancient and modern differ; sounds also change with them. It is like putting ancient caps and robes on people of today—how could they fit?
translations.idiomatic: Ancient times and the present differ, and sounds change with them. It is like putting ancient caps and robes on people today—how could they fit properly?

sentences.zh: 儒者泥古，致詳於形名度數間，而不知清濁輕重之用，故求於器雖合，而考於聲則不諧。

translations.literal: Confucian scholars cling to antiquity, pursuing minute detail in nomenclature and measurement while ignorant of the use of clear and murky, light and heavy tones; thus though instruments may accord, when tested by sound they are not harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: Confucian scholars cling to antiquity, wrangling over nomenclature and measurement while ignoring the use of clear and murky, light and heavy tones. Thus though instruments may appear to accord, when tested by sound they prove disharmonious.

sentences.zh: ”嘗遊佛寺，聞鍾聲，曰：“聲澌而悲，主者且不利。

translations.literal: Once while visiting a Buddhist temple he heard a bell and said: "The sound is breaking and mournful; the abbot will soon suffer misfortune."
translations.idiomatic: Once while visiting a Buddhist temple he heard a bell and said, "The sound is breaking and mournful. The abbot will soon suffer misfortune."

sentences.zh: ”是夕，主僧死。

translations.literal: That evening the chief monk died.
translations.idiomatic: That evening the chief monk died.

sentences.zh: 在保州，聞角聲，曰：“宮微而商離，至秋，守臣憂之。

translations.literal: While at Bao Prefecture he heard the sound of horns and said: "The gong tone is faint and the shang tone is detached; by autumn the defending official will have cause for worry."
translations.idiomatic: While at Bao Prefecture he heard horn signals and said, "The gong tone is faint and the shang tone is detached. By autumn the defending official will have cause for worry."

sentences.zh: ”及期，几遇疾。

translations.literal: When the season came, Ji fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: When autumn came, Ji fell ill.

sentences.zh: 然所學頗雜鄭、衛云。

translations.literal: Yet what he studied was quite mixed with Zheng and Wei music.
translations.idiomatic: Yet what he studied was somewhat mixed with the licentious music of Zheng and Wei.

sentences.zh: 劉濤，字德潤，徐州彭城人，後唐天成中，舉進士，釋褐為鳳翔掌書記，拜右拾遺，賜緋。

translations.literal: Liu Tao, style name Derun, was a man of Pengcheng in Xu Prefecture. In the middle of Tian Cheng under Later Tang he passed the jinshi examination, took his first office as Recorder of Fengxiang, was appointed Right Remonstrating Censor, and was granted crimson robes.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tao, whose style name was Derun, came from Pengcheng in Xu Prefecture. During the Tian Cheng era under Later Tang he passed the jinshi examination, took his first post as Recorder of Fengxiang, was appointed Right Remonstrating Censor, and was granted crimson robes.

sentences.zh: 時太常丞史在德上章，詞理鄙俗，仍犯廟諱。

translations.literal: At the time Grand Master of Ceremonial Shi Zaide submitted a memorial whose language was vulgar in reasoning and also violated taboo names of the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Grand Master of Ceremonial Shi Zaide submitted a memorial whose language was coarse and who also violated the ancestral temple's taboo names.

sentences.zh: 濤上言請正其罪，雖不允，時論是之。

translations.literal: Tao submitted a memorial requesting that his offense be punished; though it was not granted, contemporary opinion approved him.
translations.idiomatic: Tao submitted a memorial requesting that his offense be punished. Though the request was denied, contemporary opinion approved of Tao.

sentences.zh: 出為山南東道節度判官，召為左補闕，遷起居舍人。

translations.literal: He went out as military adjutant of the Shannan East Circuit, was recalled as Left Supplementing Censor, and was promoted to Diarist.
translations.idiomatic: He served as military adjutant of the Shannan East Circuit, was recalled as Left Supplementing Censor, and was promoted to Diarist.

sentences.zh: 晉天福初，改司勳員外郎、史館修撰，遷工部郎中，賜金紫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tian Fu under Jin he was changed to Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Merits and Compiler of the History Institute, promoted to Court Gentleman of the Ministry of Works, and granted gold and purple.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tian Fu era under Jin he was transferred to Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Merits and Compiler of the History Institute, promoted to Court Gentleman of the Ministry of Works, and granted gold and purple robes.

sentences.zh: 歷度支、職方二郎中，掌左藏庫。

translations.literal: He served successively as Court Gentleman of the ministries of Revenue and of Military Appointments and managed the Left Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as Court Gentleman of the ministries of Revenue and of Military Appointments, and managed the Left Treasury.

sentences.zh: 時少帝奢侈，常以銀易金，廣其器皿。

translations.literal: At the time the Young Emperor was extravagant; he often exchanged silver for gold to enlarge his vessels.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Young Emperor was extravagant and often exchanged silver for gold to enlarge his vessels.

sentences.zh: 李崧判三司，令上庫金之數。

translations.literal: Li Song as chief of the Three Departments ordered the count of gold in the upper treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Li Song, as chief of the Three Departments, ordered an accounting of the gold in the upper treasury.

sentences.zh: 及崧以元簿較之，少數千鎰。

translations.literal: When Song compared it with the original ledger, it was short by several thousand yi.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Song compared it with the original ledger, the count was short by several thousand yi.

sentences.zh: 崧責曰：“帑庫通式，一日不受虛數，毫厘則有重典。

translations.literal: Song rebuked him: "The standard practice of the treasury does not for one day accept false counts; the slightest discrepancy brings severe punishment."
translations.idiomatic: Li Song rebuked him, saying, "Treasury regulations do not tolerate false counts for even a single day. The slightest discrepancy brings severe punishment."

sentences.zh: ”濤曰：“帑司常有報不盡數，以備宣索。

translations.literal: Tao said: "Treasury officials often report incomplete counts to prepare for imperial requisitions."
translations.idiomatic: Tao said, "Treasury officials often report incomplete counts to prepare for imperial requisitions."

sentences.zh: ”崧令有司劾濤，濤事迫，以情告樞密使桑維翰，乃止罰一月奉。

translations.literal: Song ordered the responsible office to impeach Tao; Tao's situation was desperate, and he confided the facts to Military Affairs Commissioner Sang Weihan; the punishment was limited to one month's salary.
translations.idiomatic: Li Song ordered the responsible office to impeach Tao. With the case pressing, Tao confided the facts to Military Affairs Commissioner Sang Weihan, and the punishment was limited to one month's salary.

sentences.zh: 漢初，宰相蘇禹珪薦為中書舍人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Han, Chancellor Su Yudui recommended him as Drafting Secretary of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Han dynasty, Chancellor Su Yudui recommended him for the post of Drafting Secretary of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 周廣順中，坐令子監察御史頊代草誥命，左遷少府少監，分司西京；

translations.literal: In the Guangshun era of Zhou, for the offense of having his son, Supervising Censor Xu, draft edicts on his behalf, he was demoted to Vice Director of the Palace Workshops and assigned to a subsidiary post at the Western Capital;
translations.idiomatic: During the Guangshun era of Zhou, Tao was demoted to Vice Director of the Palace Workshops and assigned to a subsidiary post at the Western Capital for having his son, Supervising Censor Xu, draft edicts on his behalf;

sentences.zh: 頊亦貶復州司戶。

translations.literal: Xu was also demoted to Registrar of Fu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xu was also demoted to Registrar of Fu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 顯德初，就改太常少卿，俄拜右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiande he was transferred to Vice Minister of Ceremonies, and soon after was appointed Right Remonstrance Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Xiande era he was transferred to Vice Minister of Ceremonies, and soon after was appointed Right Remonstrance Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 四年，再知貢舉。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he again supervised the civil service examinations.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he again supervised the civil service examinations.

sentences.zh: 樞密使王樸嘗薦童子劉譜於濤，濤不納，樸銜之。

translations.literal: Military Affairs Commissioner Wang Pu once recommended the young candidate Liu Pu to Tao; Tao did not accept him, and Pu harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Military Affairs Commissioner Wang Pu once recommended the young candidate Liu Pu to Tao, but Tao did not accept him. Pu took offense.

sentences.zh: 時世宗南征在迎鑾，濤引新及第人赴行在。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Shizong was on his southern campaign at Yingluan; Tao led the newly passed candidates to the imperial camp.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Emperor Shizong was on his southern campaign at Yingluan, Tao led the newly passed candidates to the imperial camp.

sentences.zh: 樸時留守上都，飛章言濤取士不精。

translations.literal: Pu was then left to guard the capital and sent an urgent memorial saying Tao's selection of scholars was not rigorous.
translations.idiomatic: Pu, who was then left to guard the capital, sent an urgent memorial accusing Tao of selecting scholars without sufficient rigor.

sentences.zh: 世宗命翰林學士李昉覆試，出者七人。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong ordered Hanlin Academician Li Fang to conduct a re-examination; seven were eliminated.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong ordered Hanlin Academician Li Fang to conduct a re-examination, and seven candidates failed.

sentences.zh: 濤坐責授太子右讚善大夫。

translations.literal: Tao was punished and appointed Right Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Tao was punished and appointed Right Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 恭帝即位，遷右詹事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gongdi ascended the throne, Tao was transferred to Right Household Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gongdi ascended the throne, Tao was transferred to Right Household Mentor.

sentences.zh: 濤性剛毅不撓，素與宰相范質不協，常鬱鬱不得志，遂退居洛陽之清化里，杜門以書史自娛。

translations.literal: Tao's nature was firm and unyielding; he had long been at odds with Chancellor Fan Zhi, was often depressed and unfulfilled, and so retired to Qinghua Lane in Luoyang, closing his doors and amusing himself with books and history.
translations.idiomatic: Tao was firm and unyielding by nature. He had long been at odds with Chancellor Fan Zhi and often felt depressed and thwarted, so he retired to Qinghua Lane in Luoyang, shut his doors, and amused himself with books and history.

sentences.zh: 太祖素知濤履行，開寶二年召赴闕，以老病求退，授秘書監致仕。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizu had long known Tao's conduct; in the second year of Kaibao he was summoned to court, pleaded retirement on grounds of age and illness, and was granted Director of the Secretariat with retirement honors.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu had long known Tao's character. In the second year of Kaibao he was summoned to court, pleaded retirement on grounds of age and illness, and was granted the post of Director of the Secretariat with retirement honors.

sentences.zh: 年七十二卒。

translations.literal: He died at age seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 清泰初，中書舍人盧導受詔主文，將鎖宿，濤力薦薛居正，以為文章器業必至臺輔，導取之，後果為相。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai, Drafting Secretary Lu Dao received an edict to preside over the examinations; as he was about to be sequestered, Tao strongly recommended Xue Juzheng, saying his literary talent and capacity would surely reach the highest offices; Dao selected him, and he later indeed became chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Qingtai era, Drafting Secretary Lu Dao received an edict to preside over the examinations. As he was about to be sequestered, Tao strongly recommended Xue Juzheng, saying his literary talent and capacity would surely carry him to the highest offices. Dao selected him, and Xue later did indeed become chancellor.

sentences.zh: 世稱其知人。

translations.literal: The age praised his discernment of men.
translations.idiomatic: His contemporaries praised his discernment in judging men.

sentences.zh: 頊子晟，晟子訥、譚，並進士及第。

translations.literal: Xu's son Sheng, and Sheng's sons Ne and Tan, all passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Xu's son Sheng, and Sheng's sons Ne and Tan, all passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 晟至屯田員外郎，訥為殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: Sheng reached Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Agriculture; Ne served as Palace Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng rose to Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Agriculture, and Ne served as Palace Censor.

sentences.zh: 邊光範

translations.literal: Bian Guangfan
translations.idiomatic: Bian Guangfan

sentences.zh: 邊光範，字子儀，幷州陽曲人。

translations.literal: Bian Guangfan, style name Ziyi, was a man of Yangqu in Bing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Bian Guangfan, whose style name was Ziyi, came from Yangqu in Bing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 性謙退和雅，有吏材。

translations.literal: His nature was modest, retiring, and refined; he had administrative talent.
translations.idiomatic: He was modest, retiring, and refined by nature, and possessed administrative talent.

sentences.zh: 父仁嗣，忠武軍節度副使。

translations.literal: His father Rensi was military vice commissioner of the Zhongwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: His father Rensi served as military vice commissioner of the Zhongwu Army.

sentences.zh: 光範，後唐天成二年，起家榆次令，召為殿中丞，賜緋。

translations.literal: Guangfan, in the second year of Tiancheng under Later Tang, began his career as magistrate of Yuci, was summoned as Palace Aide, and was granted crimson robes.
translations.idiomatic: Guangfan began his career in the second year of Tiancheng under Later Tang as magistrate of Yuci. He was then summoned as Palace Aide and granted crimson robes.

sentences.zh: 長興四年，改太常丞。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Changxing he was transferred to Aide of the Ministry of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Changxing he was transferred to Aide of the Ministry of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 丁內艱。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He entered mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 晉天福初，服闋，授檢校戶部員外郎、北京留守判官兼侍御史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tian Fu under Jin, when mourning ended, he was appointed Supernumerary Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Revenue, adjutant to the military governor of the Northern Capital, and concurrently Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tian Fu era under Jin, when his mourning ended, he was appointed Supernumerary Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Revenue, adjutant to the military governor of the Northern Capital, and concurrently Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 二年，拜太府少卿。

translations.literal: In the second year he was appointed Vice Minister of the Palace Storehouses.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was appointed Vice Minister of the Palace Storehouses.

sentences.zh: 上書曰：“臣聞唐太宗有言：‘朕居深宮之中，視聽不能及遠，所委者惟都督、刺史。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial saying: "Your subject has heard that Emperor Taizong of Tang said: 'I dwell deep within the palace; my sight and hearing cannot reach far, and those I entrust are only the regional commanders and prefectural governors.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial saying, "Your subject has heard that Emperor Taizong of Tang said, 'I dwell deep within the palace. My sight and hearing cannot reach far, and those I entrust are only the regional commanders and prefectural governors.

sentences.zh: ’則知此官實係治亂，必須得人。

translations.literal: 'Thus one knows that these offices truly bear on order and disorder, and the right men must be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: 'From this one knows that these offices truly bear on order and disorder, and the right men must be found.

sentences.zh: 今則刺史或因緣世祿，或貢奉家財，或微立軍功，或但循官序。

translations.literal: Now prefectural governors may obtain office through hereditary privilege, or by presenting family wealth as tribute, or by slight military merit, or merely by following the official sequence.
translations.idiomatic: Today prefectural governors may obtain office through hereditary privilege, by presenting family wealth as tribute, through slight military merit, or merely by advancing in the official sequence.

sentences.zh: 實恐撫民無術，御吏無方，以此牧民，而民受其賜鮮矣。

translations.literal: I truly fear they have no method for comforting the people and no way to control officials; governing the people in this manner, the people receive little benefit.
translations.idiomatic: I truly fear they have no method for comforting the people and no way to control officials. Governing the people in this manner, the people receive little benefit.

sentences.zh: 望選能吏以蘇民瘼，用致升平。

translations.literal: I hope able administrators may be selected to relieve the people's distress and thereby bring about peace and order.
translations.idiomatic: I hope that able administrators may be selected to relieve the people's distress and thereby bring about peace and order.

sentences.zh: ”奏入，留中不出。

translations.literal: "The memorial was submitted and kept within the palace without response.
translations.idiomatic: "The memorial was submitted but kept within the palace without response.

sentences.zh: 俄為冊秦王李從嚴副使。

translations.literal: Soon after he served as deputy envoy in the investiture of Prince Qin Li Congyan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he served as deputy envoy in the investiture of Prince Qin Li Congyan.

sentences.zh: 張從恩以外戚為河南尹，奏授判官。

translations.literal: Zhang Cong'en, as a maternal relative of the emperor, served as Intendant of Henan and memorialized to appoint Guangfan as his adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cong'en, as a maternal relative of the emperor, served as Intendant of Henan and memorialized to appoint Guangfan as his adjutant.

sentences.zh: 遷秘書監兼御史中丞，入拜大理少卿。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director of the Secretariat and concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief, then entered court and was appointed Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Director of the Secretariat and concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief, then entered court and was appointed Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 漢初，改檢校刑部尚書、衛尉卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Han he was transferred to Supernumerary Minister of Punishments and Commandant of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Han dynasty he was transferred to Supernumerary Minister of Punishments and Commandant of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 上言：“伏見朝廷除刺史，不限年月，或未及期年，又聞除代。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial: "Your subject observes that when the court appoints prefectural governors, no term limit is set by years; sometimes before a full year has passed, word comes of replacement.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial saying, "Your subject observes that when the court appoints prefectural governors, no fixed term is set. Sometimes before a full year has passed, word comes of a replacement.

sentences.zh: 往來跋涉，豈暇撫懷。

translations.literal: Coming and going on long journeys, how can they find leisure to comfort and care?
translations.idiomatic: Traveling back and forth on long journeys, how can they find leisure to comfort and care for the people?

sentences.zh: 望慎選良牧，立定年限，以責輯綏之效。

translations.literal: I hope good governors may be carefully selected and fixed terms established, so that the effect of pacification and governance may be required of them.
translations.idiomatic: I hope that good governors may be carefully selected and fixed terms established, so that they may be held accountable for pacifying and governing their districts.

sentences.zh: ”疏入，不報。

translations.literal: "The memorial was submitted and received no response.
translations.idiomatic: "The memorial was submitted but received no response.

sentences.zh: 乾祐二年，連使宋州虞城、汝州襄城，按視民田之傷稼者。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianyou he was sent in succession to Yucheng in Song Prefecture and Xiangcheng in Ru Prefecture to inspect civilian fields where crops had been damaged.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qianyou he was sent in succession to Yucheng in Song Prefecture and Xiangcheng in Ru Prefecture to inspect civilian fields where crops had been damaged.

sentences.zh: 是冬，為吳越加恩使。

translations.literal: That winter he served as envoy to confer additional honors on Wuyue.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he served as envoy to confer additional honors on Wuyue.

sentences.zh: 周廣順初，出知陳州，遷秘書監，俄召拜御史中丞，賜襲衣、銀器、繒彩、鞍勒馬，復為禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun under Zhou he went out as prefect of Chen Prefecture, was promoted to Director of the Secretariat, and soon after was summoned and appointed Censor-in-Chief; he was granted ceremonial robes, silver vessels, silk brocade, and a saddled horse, and again served as Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Guangshun era under Zhou he went out as prefect of Chen Prefecture and was promoted to Director of the Secretariat. Soon after he was summoned and appointed Censor-in-Chief, granted ceremonial robes, silver vessels, silk brocade, and a saddled horse, and again served as Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 時禮部侍郎於貢部或掌或否，光範拜官，將及秋試，乃言於執政曰：“單門偶進，何言名第。

translations.literal: At the time the Vice Minister of Rites sometimes did or did not oversee the examination bureau; Guangfan received his appointment as the autumn examinations drew near, and he said to the chief ministers: "From a humble household I happened to advance—what claim have I to rank and degree?
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Vice Minister of Rites sometimes did and sometimes did not oversee the examination bureau. Guangfan received his appointment as the autumn examinations drew near and said to the chief ministers, "From a humble household I happened to advance—what claim have I to rank and degree?

sentences.zh: 若他曹公事，光範不敢辭；

translations.literal: If it is ordinary business of another office, Guangfan would not dare refuse;
translations.idiomatic: If it is ordinary business of another office, I would not dare refuse;

sentences.zh: 若處文衡，校閱名賢，品藻優劣，非下走所能。

translations.literal: but if I am to sit at the literary scales, examine and review eminent scholars, and judge excellence and inferiority, that is beyond what one of low station can do.
translations.idiomatic: but if I am to sit at the literary scales, examine eminent scholars, and judge their excellence and inferiority, that is beyond what one of my station can do.

sentences.zh: ”執政曰：“公晉末為翰林、樞密直學士，勿避事也。

translations.literal: "The chief ministers said: "Sir, at the end of Jin you were a Hanlin academician and direct academician of the Military Affairs Bureau—do not shirk duty.
translations.idiomatic: "The chief ministers said, "Sir, at the end of Jin you served as Hanlin academician and direct academician of the Military Affairs Bureau. Do not shirk your duty.

sentences.zh: ” 及期，光節辭疾不出，乃以翰林學士承旨徐台符掌之，時論多其自知。

translations.literal: "When the time came, Guangfan pleaded illness and did not appear; Hanlin Academician-in-Chief Xu Taifu was then put in charge, and contemporary opinion largely approved his self-knowledge.
translations.idiomatic: "When the time came, Guangfan pleaded illness and did not appear. Hanlin Academician-in-Chief Xu Taifu was then put in charge, and contemporary opinion largely approved Guangfan's self-knowledge.

sentences.zh: 宋初，征澤、潞，命光範為前軍轉運，計度鄭、洛、汝、孟、懷芻糧。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song, when Ze and Lu were being attacked, Guangfan was ordered to serve as transport commissioner for the vanguard army, calculating and provisioning fodder and grain for Zheng, Luo, Ru, Meng, and Huai.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Song dynasty, when Ze and Lu were being attacked, Guangfan was ordered to serve as transport commissioner for the vanguard army, calculating and provisioning fodder and grain for Zheng, Luo, Ru, Meng, and Huai.

sentences.zh: 秋，拜太常卿。

translations.literal: In autumn he was appointed Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn he was appointed Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 時張昭為吏部尚書，朝議以其耆老，令光範簽判選事。

translations.literal: At the time Zhang Zhao was Minister of Personnel; court deliberation, considering his advanced age, had Guangfan countersign and decide selection matters.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zhang Zhao was Minister of Personnel. Considering his advanced age, the court had Guangfan countersign and decide selection matters.

sentences.zh: 建隆四年，襄州節度慕容延釗征湖南，以光範權知州事，路當衝會，餉饋無闕。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianlong, when Military Commissioner Murong Yanzhao of Xiang Prefecture campaigned in Hunan, Guangfan was appointed acting prefect; the route lay at a strategic junction, and supplies were never lacking.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jianlong, when Military Commissioner Murong Yanzhao of Xiang Prefecture campaigned in Hunan, Guangfan was appointed acting prefect. The route lay at a strategic junction, and supplies were never lacking.

sentences.zh: 是冬郊祀，召還。

translations.literal: That winter, at the suburban sacrifice, he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, at the suburban sacrifice, he was recalled.

sentences.zh: 會延釗卒，復知襄州。

translations.literal: When Yanzhao died, he again served as prefect of Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanzhao died, he again served as prefect of Xiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 大軍數萬由陝路討蜀，出漢上，光範復當供億，人不知勞。

translations.literal: An army of tens of thousands marched by the Shaan route to attack Shu, emerging onto the Han River; Guangfan again took charge of provisioning, and the people felt no hardship.
translations.idiomatic: An army of tens of thousands marched by the Shaan route to attack Shu, emerging onto the Han River. Guangfan again took charge of provisioning, and the people felt no hardship.

sentences.zh: 嘗舉本鎮判官李楫為殿中侍御史，楫後坐事除籍，光範左遷太子賓客，仍知襄州。

translations.literal: He once recommended his circuit's adjutant Li Ji as Palace Censor; Ji later was implicated in an offense and struck from the rolls, and Guangfan was demoted to Household Companion of the Heir Apparent while still serving as prefect of Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He once recommended his circuit's adjutant Li Ji as Palace Censor. Ji was later implicated in an offense and struck from the rolls, and Guangfan was demoted to Household Companion of the Heir Apparent while still serving as prefect of Xiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 五年，兼橋道使，朝廷遣使督治道，常六七輩，一使所調發民皆數百人，吏緣為奸，多私取民課，所發不充數，而道益不修。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he concurrently served as Commissioner for Bridge Roads; the court sent envoys to supervise road repair, often six or seven at a time; each envoy's requisition mobilized several hundred civilians; officials used this as a pretext for corruption, often privately taking civilian labor dues; what was mobilized fell short of the quota, and the roads grew ever more unrepaired.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he concurrently served as Commissioner for Bridge Roads. The court sent envoys to supervise road repair, often six or seven at a time. Each envoy's requisition mobilized several hundred civilians. Officials used this as a pretext for corruption and often privately seized civilian labor dues. What was mobilized fell short of the quota, and the roads grew ever more unrepaired.

sentences.zh: 光範計其工，以州卒代民，官給器用，役不淹久，人以無擾。

translations.literal: Guangfan calculated the labor required, used prefectural soldiers in place of civilians, and had the government supply tools; the service did not drag on, and the people were undisturbed.
translations.idiomatic: Guangfan calculated the labor required, used prefectural soldiers in place of civilians, and had the government supply tools. The service did not drag on, and the people were undisturbed.

sentences.zh: 詔書褒美。

translations.literal: An edict praised him.
translations.idiomatic: An edict praised him.

sentences.zh: 開寶四年，復判吏部銓曹。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaibao he again served as acting chief of the Ministry of Personnel's selection bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Kaibao he again served as acting chief of the Ministry of Personnel's selection bureau.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞劉溫叟卒，以光範判御史臺事，數月，真拜中丞。

translations.literal: Vice Censor-in-Chief Liu Wensou died; Guangfan was appointed acting chief of the Censorate, and after several months was formally appointed Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Vice Censor-in-Chief Liu Wensou died, Guangfan was appointed acting chief of the Censorate. After several months he was formally appointed Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 六年，以疾解銓曹任。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, on grounds of illness he relinquished his post in the selection bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he relinquished his post in the selection bureau on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十三。

translations.literal: He died at age seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 光範性至孝，謙退和易，雅有吏幹。

translations.literal: Guangfan's nature was profoundly filial; he was modest, retiring, and easy in manner, and possessed refined administrative ability.
translations.idiomatic: Guangfan was profoundly filial by nature. He was modest, retiring, and easy in manner, and possessed refined administrative ability.

sentences.zh: 母病疽，光範嘗吮之。

translations.literal: When his mother suffered from a carbuncle, Guangfan once sucked the wound.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother suffered from a carbuncle, Guangfan once sucked the wound.

sentences.zh: 景德中，錄其孫易從同學究出身。

translations.literal: During Jingde his grandson Yicong was enrolled with the same xuejiu entry qualification.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingde era his grandson Yicong was granted entry through the same xuejiu qualification.

sentences.zh: 劉載，字德輿，涿州范陽人。

translations.literal: Liu Zai, style name Deyu, was a man of Fanyang in Zhuo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zai, whose style name was Deyu, came from Fanyang in Zhuo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 唐盧龍節度濟之六世孫。

translations.literal: He was the sixth-generation descendant of Ji, military commissioner of Lulong under Tang.
translations.idiomatic: He was the sixth-generation descendant of Ji, military commissioner of Lulong under Tang.

sentences.zh: 父昭，下蔡令。

translations.literal: His father Zhao was magistrate of Xia Cai.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhao served as magistrate of Xia Cai.

sentences.zh: 載，後唐清泰中舉進士。

translations.literal: Zai, during Qingtai under Later Tang, passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Zai passed the jinshi examination during the Qingtai era under Later Tang.

sentences.zh: 晉初，解褐校書郎，遷著作佐郎，賜緋，拜左拾遺、集賢殿直學士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jin he entered service as Collator, was promoted to Assistant Compiler, was granted crimson robes, and was appointed Left Remonstrance Censor and Direct Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jin dynasty he entered service as Collator, was promoted to Assistant Compiler, granted crimson robes, and appointed Left Remonstrance Censor and Direct Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 漢初，為殿中侍卿御史，丁內艱，服闋，復拜舊官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Han he served as Palace Attending Censor, entered mourning for his mother, and when mourning ended was again appointed to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Han dynasty he served as Palace Attending Censor. After entering mourning for his mother, when mourning ended he was again appointed to his former office.

sentences.zh: 判西京留臺，改倉部員外郎。

translations.literal: He served as administrative aide to the Western Capital's Retired Emperor's Pavilion and was transferred to Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: He served as administrative aide to the Western Capital's Retired Emperor's Pavilion and was transferred to Outer Gentleman of the Ministry of Granaries.

sentences.zh: 嘗著五論，曰《為君》、《為相》、《為將》、《去讒》、《納諫》，頗為文士所稱。

translations.literal: He once composed five treatises, titled "On Being a Ruler," "On Being a Chancellor," "On Being a General," "On Removing Slander," and "On Accepting Remonstrance," and they were much praised by literary men.
translations.idiomatic: He once composed five treatises titled "On Being a Ruler," "On Being a Chancellor," "On Being a General," "On Removing Slander," and "On Accepting Remonstrance," and they were much praised by literary men.

sentences.zh: 周世宗初，擢知制誥。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Shizong of Zhou he was promoted to Drafting Edicts.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Shizong's reign he was promoted to Drafting Edicts.

sentences.zh: 顯德三年，拜右諫議大夫，與右拾遺鄭起、尚書博士李寧同校道書。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xiande he was appointed Right Remonstrance Grand Master and, together with Right Remonstrance Censor Zheng Qi and Erudite of the Masters of Documents Li Ning, collated Daoist texts.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xiande he was appointed Right Remonstrance Grand Master and, together with Right Remonstrance Censor Zheng Qi and Erudite of the Masters of Documents Li Ning, collated Daoist texts.

sentences.zh: 遷給事中，使許州定田租。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Supervising Censor and sent to Xu Prefecture to fix land tax.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Supervising Censor and sent to Xu Prefecture to fix land tax assessments.

sentences.zh: 俄賜金紫，為魏王符彥卿加恩國信使。

translations.literal: Soon after he was granted gold and purple and served as credentialed envoy to confer additional honors on Prince Wei Fu Yanqing.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was granted gold and purple robes and served as credentialed envoy to confer additional honors on Prince Wei Fu Yanqing.

sentences.zh: 宋初，浚五丈河，自陳橋達曹州之西境，命護其役。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song the Wuzhang River was dredged from Chenqiao to the western border of Cao Prefecture, and he was ordered to oversee the work.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Song dynasty the Wuzhang River was dredged from Chenqiao to the western border of Cao Prefecture, and he was ordered to oversee the work.

sentences.zh: 建隆四年，貝州節度使張光翰來朝，遣載權知州事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianlong, Military Commissioner Zhang Guanghan of Bei Prefecture came to court; Zai was dispatched to serve as acting prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jianlong, Military Commissioner Zhang Guanghan of Bei Prefecture came to court, and Zai was dispatched to serve as acting prefect.

sentences.zh: 光翰歸鎮，載還，知貢舉。

translations.literal: Guanghan returned to his command; Zai came back and supervised the civil service examinations.
translations.idiomatic: When Guanghan returned to his command, Zai came back and supervised the civil service examinations.

sentences.zh: 乾德初，掌建安榷貨務。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qiande he managed the Jian'an Commodity Monopoly Office.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Qiande era he managed the Jian'an Commodity Monopoly Office.

sentences.zh: 六年，就為江南國主生辰使，召還，令知鎮州。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he served as birthday envoy to the lord of Jiangnan, was recalled, and was ordered to serve as prefect of Zhen Prefecture.
