translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he served as birthday envoy to the lord of Jiangnan, was recalled, and was ordered to serve as prefect of Zhen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 開寶四年，坐與何繼筠不協，改山南東道行軍司馬。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaibao, for being at odds with He Jiyun, he was transferred to Military Administrator of the Shannan East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Kaibao, for being at odds with He Jiyun, he was transferred to Military Administrator of the Shannan East Circuit.

sentences.zh: 十年不召，嘗受詔權點檢州事。

translations.literal: For ten years he was not summoned; he once received an edict to act as inspector of prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: For ten years he was not summoned to court. He once received an edict to act as inspector of prefectural affairs.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，復入為給事中。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo he again entered court as Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Taiping Xingguo era he again entered court as Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 三年，出知襄州，六年，代還。

translations.literal: In the third year he went out as prefect of Xiang Prefecture; in the sixth year he was replaced and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he went out as prefect of Xiang Prefecture. In the sixth year he was replaced and returned.

sentences.zh: 告老，改工部侍郎致仕，乃賜一子出身。

translations.literal: He requested retirement on grounds of age, was transferred to Vice Minister of Works with retirement honors, and one son was granted entry qualification.
translations.idiomatic: He requested retirement on grounds of age, was transferred to Vice Minister of Works with retirement honors, and one son was granted entry qualification.

sentences.zh: 八年，卒，年七十一。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he died at age seventy-one.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he died at the age of seventy-one.

sentences.zh: 載尤好學，博通史傳，善屬文。

translations.literal: Zai was especially fond of learning, thoroughly versed in historical records and biographies, and skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Zai was especially fond of learning, thoroughly versed in historical records and biographies, and skilled at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 嘗受詔撰明憲皇后諡冊文，又作《吊戰國賦》萬餘言行於世。

translations.literal: He once received an edict to compose the posthumous-title document for Empress Mingxian, and also wrote "Lament for the Warring States," more than ten thousand characters in length, which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He once received an edict to compose the posthumous-title document for Empress Mingxian, and also wrote "Lament for the Warring States," more than ten thousand characters in length, which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 雅信釋典，敦尚名節。

translations.literal: He deeply believed in Buddhist scriptures and earnestly upheld reputation and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He deeply believed in Buddhist scriptures and earnestly upheld reputation and integrity.

sentences.zh: 子宗言，至比部郎中。

translations.literal: His son Zongyan reached Court Gentleman of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zongyan rose to Court Gentleman of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 宗望，景德二年進士及第。

translations.literal: Zongwang passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Jingde.
translations.idiomatic: Zongwang passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Jingde.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符四年，其孫介以載文集來獻，以為試將作主簿。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Dazhong Xiangfu his grandson Jie presented Zai's collected writings; he was made Trial Assistant Magistrate of the General's Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Dazhong Xiangfu his grandson Jie presented Zai's collected writings and was made Trial Assistant Magistrate of the General's Office.

sentences.zh: 程羽，字冲遠，深州陸澤人。

translations.literal: Cheng Yu, style name Chongyuan, was a man of Luze in Shen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yu, whose style name was Chongyuan, came from Luze in Shen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少好學，能屬文。

translations.literal: From youth he loved learning and could compose literary works.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved learning and could compose literary works.

sentences.zh: 晉天福中，擢進士第，授陽穀主簿。

translations.literal: During Tian Fu under Jin he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed chief clerk of Yanggu.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tian Fu era under Jin he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed chief clerk of Yanggu.

sentences.zh: 歷虞鄉、醴泉、新都令，皆有政績。

translations.literal: He served successively as magistrate of Yuxiang, Liquan, and Xindu, and in each post had administrative achievements.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as magistrate of Yuxiang, Liquan, and Xindu, and achieved notable results in each post.

sentences.zh: 開寶中，選為兩使判官，入對，太祖詢以時事，敷奏稱旨，擢著作郎，出知興州。

translations.literal: During Kaibao he was selected as adjutant to a diplomatic envoy; entering audience, Emperor Taizu questioned him on current affairs, and his full presentation accorded with the emperor's intent; he was promoted to Compiler and went out as prefect of Xing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaibao era he was selected as adjutant to a diplomatic envoy. At audience Emperor Taizu questioned him on current affairs, and his full presentation accorded with the emperor's intent. He was promoted to Compiler and sent out as prefect of Xing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 逾年，改知興元府。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was transferred to administer Xingyuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was made administrator of Xingyuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 八年，詔歸闕，以本官領開封府判官。

translations.literal: In the eighth year an edict recalled him to court; with his original office he headed the judicial staff of Kaifeng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year an edict recalled him to court, and he served as chief judicial officer of Kaifeng Prefecture while retaining his original rank.

sentences.zh: 羽性淳厚，蒞事恪謹。

translations.literal: Yu was sincere and generous by nature and conducted affairs with scrupulous care.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was sincere and generous by nature and handled affairs with scrupulous care.

sentences.zh: 時太宗尹京，頗以長者待之。

translations.literal: At that time Taizong governed the capital and treated him rather as an elder.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the future Taizong governed the capital and treated him with the respect due an elder.

sentences.zh: 及即位，拜給事中，知開封府。

translations.literal: When he took the throne, Yu was appointed Supervising Censor and made administrator of Kaifeng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When he took the throne, Yu was appointed Supervising Censor and put in charge of Kaifeng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 未幾，出知成都府，為政寬簡，蜀人便之。

translations.literal: Before long he went out as administrator of Chengdu Prefecture; his government was lenient and simple, and the people of Shu found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was sent out as administrator of Chengdu Prefecture. His government was lenient and simple, and the people of Shu found it agreeable.

sentences.zh: 入朝，拜禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He entered court and was appointed Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court and was appointed Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 上欲優以清職。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to honor him with a pure, exalted office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to honor him with a prestigious, purely advisory post.

sentences.zh: 故事，端明殿設學士二員，居翰林學士上，專備顧問，馮道、趙鳳始居是職，累朝因之。

translations.literal: By precedent the Hall of Illuminated Clarity had two academicians, ranking above Hanlin academicians and reserved for consultation; Feng Dao and Zhao Feng first held these posts, and successive dynasties followed the practice.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent the Hall of Illuminated Clarity had two academicians who ranked above Hanlin academicians and served solely as imperial advisers. Feng Dao and Zhao Feng were the first to hold these posts, and successive dynasties followed the practice.

sentences.zh: 及是，即殿名以羽為文明殿學士，位在樞密副使下，且即泰寧坊營第以賜之。

translations.literal: On this occasion, taking the hall's name, Yu was made Academician of the Hall of Civilization, ranking below the vice commissioner of Military Affairs, and a residence was built for him in Taining Ward and bestowed on him.
translations.idiomatic: On this occasion, taking the hall's name, Yu was made Academician of the Hall of Civilization, ranking below the vice commissioner of Military Affairs, and a residence was built for him in Taining Ward and granted to him.

sentences.zh: 太平興國五年，典試貢士，御試得人居多。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taiping Xingguo he presided over the examination of presented scholars, and many of those chosen in the imperial examination were his selections.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Taiping Xingguo he presided over the civil service examinations, and many of those chosen in the imperial examination were men he had recommended.

sentences.zh: 六年，以老疾求解職，拜兵部侍郎，未幾致仕，仍給全奉。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, on grounds of old age and illness he requested release from office, was appointed Vice Minister of War, and before long retired, while still receiving his full salary.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, citing old age and illness, he asked to leave office, was appointed Vice Minister of War, and soon retired while continuing to receive his full salary.

sentences.zh: 雍熙元年，卒，年七十二。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongxi he died, aged seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongxi he died at the age of seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He was posthumously appointed Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 子希振，以蔭至尚書虞部員外郎。

translations.literal: His son Xizhen, by hereditary privilege, reached Vice Director in the Ministry of Works' Parks Office.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xizhen, through hereditary privilege, rose to Vice Director in the Ministry of Works' Parks Office.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符元年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu.

sentences.zh: 其子適，賜同學究出身。

translations.literal: His son Shi was granted the qualification of a fellow licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shi was granted the qualification of a fellow licentiate.

sentences.zh: 從孫琳，別傳。

translations.literal: His collateral descendant Lin has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: His collateral descendant Lin is treated in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 論曰：五季為國，不四、三傳輒易姓，其臣子視事君猶傭者焉，主易則他役，習以為常。

translations.literal: The commentary says: In the Five Dynasties as states, within three or four generations the surname would change; their ministers regarded serving a ruler as hired labor—when the master changed they took another commission, and this became habitual.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: During the Five Dynasties, within three or four generations a ruling house would change surname. Ministers treated service to a ruler like hired labor: when the master changed they took another post, and this became habitual.

sentences.zh: 故唐方滅即北面於晉，漢甫稱禪已相率下拜於周矣。

translations.literal: Thus when Tang had just perished they at once faced north to Jin; when Han had barely claimed the abdication they already bowed in succession to Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Thus when Tang had just fallen they at once submitted to Jin, and when Han had barely claimed the throne they were already bowing in succession to Zhou.

sentences.zh: 君子傷之，此《雜臣傳》所繇立也。

translations.literal: Men of principle grieved at this; hence the establishment of the "Biographies of Miscellaneous Ministers."
translations.idiomatic: Men of principle grieved at this, which is why the "Biographies of Miscellaneous Ministers" was established.

sentences.zh: 李穀、邊歸讜、竇貞固、李濤輩，或在廟堂，或侍帷幄，世主之所寵任，社稷之所倚賴，而更事異姓，不能以名節生死，倫義廢矣。

translations.literal: Li Gu, Bian Guidang, Dou Zhengu, Li Tao, and their like—some in the ancestral temple hall, some attending within the curtain—were favorites of their age's rulers and pillars on whom the altars of state relied, yet they served houses of different surnames and could not live or die for reputation and integrity; human duty was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gu, Bian Guidang, Dou Zhengu, Li Tao, and men like them—some in the halls of government, some attending within the imperial curtain—were favorites of their rulers and pillars on whom the state relied. Yet they served houses of different surnames and could not live or die for reputation and integrity; moral duty was cast aside.

sentences.zh: 且穀以籌策自名，乃不能料藝祖有容人之量，及受李筠饋遺，懼其見殺，遂以憂死，又何繆耶？

translations.literal: Moreover Gu made his name by strategy, yet could not foresee that Taizu had the magnanimity to tolerate men; when he accepted Li Yun's gifts and feared execution, he died of grief—how perverse was that?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Gu had made his name by strategy, yet failed to foresee that Taizu had the magnanimity to tolerate others. When he accepted Li Yun's gifts and feared execution, he died of grief—how mistaken was that?

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，魏范粲、齊顏見遠，宜見褒於前史也。

translations.literal: Alas, Fan Can of Wei and Yan Jianyuan of Qi ought to have been praised in the earlier histories.
translations.idiomatic: Alas, Fan Can of Wei and Yan Jianyuan of Qi deserved praise in the earlier histories.
